Rhizobia are symbiotic bacteria of leguminous plants, and the symbiotic structure of nodules has a naturally microaerobic environment, while DHA and EPA are high-value and microaerobic substances. We deleted specific enzyme genes to increase precursor substances and added regulatory sequences and synthetic gene clusters to enable them to produce DHA and EPA under low-oxygen, high-nitrogen conditions in nodules. Proper inoculation and nitrogen fertilization ensure the efficiency of Nodule Factory, providing impoverished regions with high-added-value legumes for income and nutrition. In the future, we aim to transfer these nutrients to soybeans to further empower the soybeans. Our modular Nodule Factory will pioneer sustainable and microaerobic production, significantly contributing to global sustainability.

title: NanoDisguiser: Redefining Broad-Spectrum Antiviral Therapy with Nanodisc Technology Platform
text: NanoDisguiser: Redefining Broad-Spectrum Antiviral Therapy with Nanodisc Technology Platform. Nanodiscs are tiny, disk-shaped structures engineered as drugs, antibodies, or in vitro biological components. Our project introduces a groundbreaking nanodisc-based antiviral therapy, NanoDisguiser, designed to tackle the limitations of traditional methods, such as viral drug resistance.  By using broad-spectrum nanodiscs therapy with virus-specific receptors, these nanodiscs act as decoys, luring and disrupting viruses before they can infect cells. This cutting-edge approach provides a powerful and versatile defense against a wide range of viruses, including new and mutant strains. We're also working to validate and commercialize this technology as an injectable antiviral solution, aiming to redefine antiviral therapy in a post-pandemic world.

title: VEBATIN-Engineering bacteria to inhibit solid tumor proliferation by competing VEGF
text: VEBATIN-Engineering bacteria to inhibit solid tumor proliferation by competing VEGF. One of the major challenges in the treatment of solid tumors arises from the immunosuppressive nature of the surrounding tumor microenvironment（TME）, which weakens the immune system's cytotoxic ability. Currently, therapeutic strategies targeting the solid tumor microenvironment have gained extensive attention, while most existing treatments still confront with challenges such as off-target risks. Our team has noticed that harmless Escherichia coli Nissle 1917(EcN) can automatically colonize the tumor microenvironment, demonstrating excellent targeting potential. Therefore, we plan to utilize the angiogenesis mechanism driven by vascular endothelial growth factorin （VEGF）in the human body. We plan to genetically modified EcN to express VEGF competitive binding receptors under ideal conditions of TME and conduct a surface display in ECN. By integrating and consuming VEGF in the tumor microenvironment, we plan to reduce its concentration in the TME, thereby effectively inhibiting angiogenesis in tumor areas and ultimately suppress tumor proliferation.

title: BioALA+: Advanced 5-ALA Synthesis for Sustainable Agriculture
text: BioALA+: Advanced 5-ALA Synthesis for Sustainable Agriculture. The supply of grain is the foundation of people's livelihood. However, with many agricultural fields in various regions suffering from drought, diseases, pests, and other attacks, many people still live in hunger. Using biopesticide to enhance crops' resistance to abiotic and biotic stresses, while promoting crop yield is an available solution. 5-aminolevulinic acid (5-ALA) is a sophisticated and sustainable biopesticide, especially when compared to the various highly toxic and non-degradable chemical pesticides currently in use. The exploration of the biological manufacturing of 5-ALA in recent years has driven our research. However, issues such as the stability of ALAS gene expression, the obsolescence of targets, and the low efficiency of screening for target strains still persist. This project addresses these three issues by utilizing CRISPR-associated transposon system, enzyme-constrained model, and droplet microfluidic high-throughput screening technologies to explore solutions.

title: BIOTARGET: Bacterial Iterative Optimized Therapy and Assisted Resistance Guard Enhancement Technology
text: BIOTARGET: Bacterial Iterative Optimized Therapy and Assisted Resistance Guard Enhancement Technology. JLU-NBBMS 2024 has developed the BIOTARGET, an advanced biological system iteratively engineered using bacteria. This system integrates modular design concepts from synthetic biology, RNAi technology, attenuated Salmonella, and nanotechnology to precisely target and treat chemotherapy-resistant cancer cells. It enhances tumor recognition with a targeting module, suppresses chemoresistance gene expression with a gene regulation module, ensures Salmonella's controllable behavior within the body through a safety module, and facilitates precise drug delivery via a nanoparticle-mediated module. We have further validated the metabolism, dynamics, and efficacy of the BIOTARGET using mathematical models and cell experiments to ensure its safety and efficacy, aiming to provide personalized treatment options for patients and enhance the effectiveness of chemotherapy drugs.

title: Mo-Base: Multi-Omics Bioformatics Analysis SynthEsis Platform
text: Mo-Base: Multi-Omics Bioformatics Analysis SynthEsis Platform. We are attempting to build a highly interactive and comprehensive bioinformatics service platform. The platform includes a fully optimized single-cell analysis pipeline that can be applied to synthetic biology research requiring transcriptomics analysis. In addition, we have explored the current applications of deep learning models, and have also integrated a community within the platform to allow users to communicate and discuss with each other at any time.

title: Natronaut: Harnessing Nitrate Assimilation for Single Cell Protein (SCP) Production and Coastal Eutrophication Bioremediation
text: Natronaut: Harnessing Nitrate Assimilation for Single Cell Protein (SCP) Production and Coastal Eutrophication Bioremediation. MSP-Maastricht is addressing coastal eutrophication, a local and global issue. Excessive fertiliser run-off from agriculture, a key economic sector of the Netherlands’ economy, has polluted waterways, spreading into marine ecosystems. This leads to ocean acidification, anoxia, and harmful algal blooms, which intensify climate change and disrupt biodiversity. Natronaut focuses on engineering the marine bacterium Vibrio natriegens to mitigate nitrate pollution in coastal waters. By harnessing its rapid growth and metabolic capacity, we aim to assimilate excess nitrates and convert them into single-cell proteins (SCPs), which can serve as sustainable livestock feed. This innovation reduces the need for conventional feed crops and fertilisers, promoting resource efficiency and circularity. Our project addresses the environmental challenge of eutrophication by not only reducing eutrophication but also working to prevent its recurrence. Ultimately, we aim to convert agricultural waste into valuable biomass, turning the tide on nitrate pollution.

title: Manipulate Astrobiology for Revolutionary Synthetic-survival （MARSs)
text: Manipulate Astrobiology for Revolutionary Synthetic-survival （MARSs). Mars is a potential destination for human migration. However, future explorers will face significant challenges, including the lack of natural food resources and oxygen, toxic and poor soil for crop production, and limited synbio toolkit. We proposed solutions across four key areas inspired by a series of human practices. First, to provide sustainable nutrition, we aim to co-culture engineered yeast and cyanobacteria to produce essential compounds such as lycopene, nerol, and limonene. Second, to convert Martian soil into arable land, we isolated nitrogen-fixing bacteria and used directed evolution to enhance bacteria’s resistance to Martian toxins.  Third, we introduced updates to our TTTT system, released in 2023, which now reduces plant transformation time by up to 50%, encouraging more iGEM participants to engage in plant synthetic biology. Finally, as a creative endeavor, we applied DNA data storage to archive significant records of Earth's biodiversity and culture for future generations

title: NeuroMuSceteer: "all for one" against Multiple Sclerosis
text: NeuroMuSceteer: "all for one" against Multiple Sclerosis. Multiple Sclerosis is an increasingly prominent, multifactorial disease that affects almost 3 million people worldwide,with that number being expected to increase exponentially. Its treatment is currently centered around symptom management and decelerating its progression, as there is no available cure. Recognising this major gap in modern therapeutics, we developed NeuroMuSceteer; a modular, precision medicine, holistic therapy. It involves T- cells that are engineered to selectively target specific disease antibodies and act as immune regulators (Tregs),boosting the immune system and the CNS. Furthermore, we included two molecular structures, one that detects and one that releases microRNA agents in target cells, repairing nerve damage. The design was made in collaboration with various stakeholders in both research and healthcare, with the purpose of tackling all aspects of Multiple Sclerosis with accuracy and safety. Its modularity also allows it to be adapted for various autoimmune disorders, making it a useful tool for future researchers.

title: SkinBAIT: Innovative Approach for Targeting Skin Parasites and Infestations Using Engineered Skin Microbiota
text: SkinBAIT: Innovative Approach for Targeting Skin Parasites and Infestations Using Engineered Skin Microbiota. The SkinBait project aims to develop an innovative approach to treat skin diseases caused by external organisms, with a current focus on scabies, a condition caused by the mite Sarcoptes scabiei. It involves engineering the skin bacterium Cutibacterium acnes to produce toxins that are lethal to scabies but harmless to humans. Our project had two main parts: the expression of Cry proteins and the expression of endolysin regulated by an RNA thermometer. We optimized gene circuits for Cry toxin production using C. acnes and E. coli, developed safety mechanisms using RNA thermometers and the endolysin, and designed experiments to evaluate Cry toxin efficacy and biocontainment strategies. Several mathematical models were included that simulate what effect our approach would have. Through this design, we aim to create a safe, effective, and biologically contained treatment for skin parasites, setting the foundation for broader applications in skin disease treatment.

title: The Pentacone; Coastal Defense, Engineered by Nature.
text: The Pentacone; Coastal Defense, Engineered by Nature.. Coastal erosion and plastic pollution are growing threats to coastlines worldwide, and Ghana is no exception. These environmental challenges have severely impacted communities near the coast, destroying homes and infrastructure, displacing families, and burdening the economy heavily. Despite efforts to address these issues, current solutions have proven ineffective in providing lasting relief.  The Sea Titans aim to deliver a groundbreaking and sustainable solution to combat plastic pollution and coastal erosion. Our innovative approach involves the Pentacone, a structure equipped with advanced biotechnology designed to decompose PET plastic in the sea and reduce coastal erosion. This Pentapod is designed to self-regenerate when damaged, ensuring longevity. This circular approach not only cleans our seas but also strengthens coastal defenses.  As Sea Titans, we want to create a future where our oceans and coastlines are cleaner, more resilient, safer for coastal communities and contribute to the global fight against pollution and environmental degradation.

title: Caffeine Cycle
text: Caffeine Cycle. This project focuses on the reutilization of food waste by employing directed evolution of key enzymes to improve the production of 7-methylxanthine (7-MX), a high-value compound, with caffeine from coffee grounds as the substrate. This research not only provides an innovative and sustainable solution for the reutilization of coffee grounds, thus promoting the sustainable development of the circular economy, but also opens up new possibilities in the biosynthesis of methylxanthine compounds.

title: BEST-ABfree: Efficient synthesis of β-glucan to reduce antibiotic utilization
text: BEST-ABfree: Efficient synthesis of β-glucan to reduce antibiotic utilization. Livestock farming has long been essential for providing high-quality protein and other animal by-products. Antibiotics are extensively used in this industry to ensure stable production. However, misuse of antibiotics leads to environmental residues and the emergence of antibiotic-resistant superbugs, posing significant human health risks. β-glucans, naturally occurring β-D-glucose polysaccharides found in grains, bacteria, and fungi, offer a potential alternative to antibiotics due to their immunomodulatory and anti-inflammatory. β-glucans, particularly from Aureobasidium melanogenum BZ-11, can be efficiently produced via fermentation. This fungus isolated from mangroves secretes extracellular polysaccharides, including β-glucans, but also melanin and pullulan, which complicate the purification process. Using synthetic biology techniques, we employed Cre-loxP to block the secretion of melanin and pullulan, enhancing the purity of β-glucans. Additionally, introducing an oxygen uptake system improved yield. Our optimized fermentation process allows for the efficient production of β-glucans, presenting a viable antibiotic alternative for livestock feed, potentially mitigating antibiotic misuse.

title: The Revolutionary Tea -VitaliNK; Using Traditional Japanese Food "Natto" to Prevent Thrombosis
text: The Revolutionary Tea -VitaliNK; Using Traditional Japanese Food "Natto" to Prevent Thrombosis. Thrombosis accounts for one in four deaths worldwide. "Thrombosis" is a general term for diseases caused by blood clots obstructing blood vessels, including myocardial infarction, stroke, pulmonary embolism, and cardioembolic stroke. This is a significant issue in Japan, which is experiencing an aging society. Among the G7 countries, Japan has the highest percentage of elderly people within its total population. However, current treatments for Thrombosis consist of side effects that heavily affect the body. which is why we decided to use nattokinase, which is found in the Japanese traditional food, “Natto”. Nattokinase demonstrates strong thrombolytic activity by enhancing the effects of the fibrinolytic enzyme plasmin present in the body, therefore easy to consume the body, less resistant from consumers, and is a new preventative solution for Thrombosis. Our product form of tea is easily consumed daily and without health issues as barriers.

title: Reneurish: A novel cell therapy to restore neural tissue damage post-stroke
text: Reneurish: A novel cell therapy to restore neural tissue damage post-stroke. Reneurish aims to genetically modify neural progenitor cells (NPC) to overexpress BDNF –a potent neurotrophic factor- to tackle the challenges attributed to neural transplants; low neuronal integration and cell survival.   This overexpression is achieved through the infection of NPCs with an AAV vector. Donor’s NPCs are kept in a reservoir and infected after stroke takes place, then transplanted into the patient’s damaged brain region to enhance regeneration, improving integration, synapsis and minimizing tissue death.  During our investigation, the need for precise monitoring led to the development of a customizable reporter transfection cassette, which can be easily removed during the humanization of the vector.  This study concluded that BDNF can be overexpressed in human NPCs for over 50 days. We observed that an increase in BDNF levels correlates with a higher neural activity, better axon connectivity and higher cell count, without generating aberrant networks.

title: Hydro Guardian: A Biosensor for Detecting β-Lactam Antibiotic and Heavy Metal Residues
text: Hydro Guardian: A Biosensor for Detecting β-Lactam Antibiotic and Heavy Metal Residues. We developed a cellular sensor using genetically modified HEK cells to detect both heavy metals and antibiotic residues. The Hydro Guardian integrates the eukaryotic metal-binding transcription factor 1 (MTF1) pathway for heavy metals and the PASTA domain from prokaryotes, which is sensitive to beta-lactam antibiotics. The sensor was optimized through a sophisticated spectroscopic analysis pipeline and refined using a detailed differential equation-based model, enabling the determination of minimal residue detection limits. Throughout the design process, we collaborated with stakeholders from various fields and contributed over 20 new parts to the iGEM Registry. To validate the sensor concept, we successfully demonstrated the expression of distinct fluorophores, activated by specific promoter-regulator pathways for the MTF1 and PASTA domains, confirming the functionality of the system in detecting target contaminants.

title: Neovio Dye——A new type of dyeing implemented by light induction system
text: Neovio Dye——A new type of dyeing implemented by light induction system. ZJU-China has designed a new and interesting microbial staining method. On the basis of synthesizing Violacein's highly efficient metabolic modification and addressable RNA scaffold, it uses light-induced DNA recombinase and light-sensitive transcription factors to realize memory pattern drawing, hoping to bring the color of synthetic biology to the fashion industry. Please join us to find fashion!

title: General disease detection with Protease and Aptamer (GPA)
text: General disease detection with Protease and Aptamer (GPA). Aimed at creating a new methodology for disease diagnosis, GPA combines AI with protease-based circuits to accomplish modularization, the core value of synthetic biology, which is embodied in the design of our system－the variable biomarker recognition part and the constant signal amplification and output part. For the first part, featuring on flexible structures, aptamers (i.e., single stranded nucleotides) recognize variable biomarkers. Additionally, an AI tool－MAGA, has laid foundations for applying aptamers to biomarker binding. With MAGA, given a biomarker of a specific disease, we can obtain different aptamers recognizing it with high affinities. For the second part comes the protease-based circuits to transform and amplify signals. For the third part, a special designed gold colloidal test serves as the output. With GPA, we envision a future where the primary disease diagnosis takes fewer time, costs lower, prioritizes user-friendliness and ensures everyone a healthier life.

title: "Gut Guardian" - A Probiotic Escherichia coli Nissle 1917 That Can Sense and Treat IBD
text: "Gut Guardian" - A Probiotic Escherichia coli Nissle 1917 That Can Sense and Treat IBD. Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is a chronic intestinal inflammation of unknown etiology and incurable nature. This project utilizes  Escherichia coli Nissle 1917 as the chassis cell, employing six functional modules to address IBD. The sensing module, regulated by the SoxR/SoxS promoter, detects excessive NO, ensuring that the gene circuit is activated only in the IBD environment, thereby enhancing safety and specificity. The therapeutic modules include the immune module (PD-L1), adhesion module (Mfp), and antioxidant module (SOD), which are designed to suppress immune responses, repair damaged intestinal tissues, and eliminate reactive oxygen species, respectively. The lysis module automatically lyses probiotic cells upon their accumulation at the inflammation site, releasing therapeutic proteins. The safety module activates the expression of the MazF toxin via a blue light-responsive promoter, ensuring the engineered bacteria die upon excretion, thus mitigating potential risks.

title: Genetically engineering Acidithiobacillus ferrooxidans for effective biomining
text: Genetically engineering Acidithiobacillus ferrooxidans for effective biomining. Given the global increasing demand for mineral resources and the ore grades decline, there is an increasing utilization of microorganisms in biomining to extract valuable metals from low-grade ores and electronic waste. Biomining offers a sustainable and environmentally friendly alternative to conventional mineral processing technologies. However, it faces challenges like long leaching cycles, low extraction efficiency, and unspecific bioleaching. The genetic engineering of microorganisms can enhance their capabilities for improved biomining performance promisingly. Acidithiobacillus, a genus of extremophilic acidophiles commonly inhabiting mining process waters and acid mine drainage, is a promising chassis for metal recovery and bioremediation of metal-contaminated sites. In 2024, CUG-China aims to enhance biomining efficiency for nonferrous metals by genetically engineering Acidithiobacillus ferrooxidans. This engineered strain incorporates a cyclic di-GMP synthesis module for the enhancement of bacteria-ore interactions, a gold-specific detection module for targeted recovery, and an electron transfer module for further improving biomining processes.

title: Engineering E. coli to Secrete Protease Inhibitors to Mitigate Pseudogymnoascus destructans in Bat Populations
text: Engineering E. coli to Secrete Protease Inhibitors to Mitigate Pseudogymnoascus destructans in Bat Populations. White-Nose Syndrome affects five of the nine bat species located in Michigan: the Little Brown bat, the Big Brown Bat, the Tricolored bat, the Indiana bat, and the Northern Long-Eared bat. The disease is caused by the fungus Pseudogymnoascus destructans, which infects bats during their hibernation period, causing the collagen in their noses to slowly degrade due to proteolytic enzymes produced by the fungus. This causes the bats to become active from hibernation prematurely, which results in lethargy due to the limited resources. Without the necessary means to sustain life available in the winter season, death is often a result. There is currently no widespread treatment to prevent P. destructans infections in bats. We aim to engineer E. coli that secrete a serine protease inhibitor(s) to prevent collagen degradation.

title: Engineering Shewanella oneidensis MR-1 for Polylactic Acid Degradation to Generate Electrical Energy
text: Engineering Shewanella oneidensis MR-1 for Polylactic Acid Degradation to Generate Electrical Energy. Many researchers have challenged the degradability of the biopolymer Polylactic Acid (PLA), hugely popular in 3D printing. To address PLA's environmental persistence, we are working to engineer the bacterium Shewanella oneidensis MR-1 to degrade PLA and generate power from its breakdown. S. oneidensis is a gram-negative, facultative anaerobe capable of extracellular electron transfer, and can break down organic material and generate electricity in microbial fuel cells. It utilizes lactic acid as its carbon source to produce electricity. Therefore, we engineered S. oneidensis with genes encoding for PLA depolymerases from 4 bacterial strains. When expressing these genes, we expect that S. oneidensis will be capable of depolymerizing PLA to lactic acid, then using the lactic acid as a substrate for electricity production. The S. oneidensis strains that were successful in degrading PLA will be used in a microbial fuel cell for electricity production with PLA as the carbon source.

title: Broccoli Master :Sustainable de novo synthesis of sulforaphane in Saccharomyces cerevisiae
text: Broccoli Master :Sustainable de novo synthesis of sulforaphane in Saccharomyces cerevisiae. Cancer is a major health issue, and chemotherapy, while a primary treatment, often has severe side effects and limited effectiveness. Sulforaphane, an isothiocyanate found in cruciferous vegetables like broccoli seeds, has strong anti-cancer properties with minimal side effects. However, its production from plants leads to land waste, high costs, and unsustainable practices. We aim to synthesize sulforaphane de novo in Saccharomyces cerevisiae and use computational and synthetic biology to enhance its yield. This approach will reduce costs, land waste, and deforestation, offering a sustainable alternative that supports global climate change efforts and improves human health.

title: Aflatoxin B1 Real-time Crasher
text: Aflatoxin B1 Real-time Crasher. Aflatoxin B1 (AFB1) is a highly toxic and carcinogenic foodborne pollutant, which seriously threatens food safety and public health. In order to degrade AFB1 that may be generated during the transportation, storage and processing of food, feed and so on in real time, we take Lactobacillus rhamnosus as the chassis, and let the nano-fluorescence system that can specifically bind to AFB1 and the light-induced VVD photosensitive system work together to activate the expression of laccase (CodAGold) that degrades AFB1, so as to achieve real-time degradation of AFB1. In addition, MazF is under the control of a glucose sensitive promoter, to prevent the escape of engineered bacteria and ensure biosafety. This method is expected to provide a valuable strategy for agriculture, animal husbandry and food safety to realize real-time harmless treatment of AFB1.

title: BYEbuprofen - for cleaner water
text: BYEbuprofen - for cleaner water. Pharmaceutical pollutants, particularly nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) like ibuprofen, and diclofenac, and hormones such as estrogen, have been increasingly detected in aquatic ecosystems, where they threaten wildlife and disrupt ecological balance. Current wastewater treatment processes are often insufficient for removing these contaminants, leading to their accumulation in water bodies. The objective of this project is to develop an innovative solution using immobilized laccase, to degrade pharmaceutical pollutants in wastewater. Additionally, this project aims to lay the groundwork for the development of a biosensor to detect and monitor ibuprofen and diclofenac, providing a novel method for assessing water contaminations. The use of enzymatic degradation and improved pollutant detection represents a sustainable and cost-effective approach for the enhancement of wastewater treatment processes, thereby reducing the environmental impact of pharmaceutical contamination.  This project supports the broader goal of enhancing water quality worldwide and preserving aquatic ecosystems.

title: Bright Ideas Come in Nanocompartments: Detecting Johne's disease with Split-luciferase Fused Encapsulins
text: Bright Ideas Come in Nanocompartments: Detecting Johne's disease with Split-luciferase Fused Encapsulins. Johne’s disease is caused by Mycobacterium avium subspecies paratuberculosis (MAP) and causes Crohn’s disease-like symptoms in ruminants. MAP2121c is a novel Type 2A Encapsulin that readily forms multimeric cages to protect a cysteine desulfurase from environmental oxidative stress. Exploiting this cage formation, we fused encapsulin monomers to two parts of a split-luciferase to develop our bioluminescent test. Cage formation between the two luciferase-linked encapsulins allows the luciferase to form and upon the addition of the substrate, a bioluminescent signal would be observed, indicating a negative result for Johne's disease. The introduction of wild-type encapsulin from an infected bovine blood sample would disrupt split-luciferase binding and reduce the bioluminescence, yielding a positive test result for Johne's disease. Our light detection kit is intended to be used to detect the bioluminescence on-site, with potential for farmers to use in the future.

title: iEraser—Erase the Pain of Inflammatory Bowel Disease (IBD)
text: iEraser—Erase the Pain of Inflammatory Bowel Disease (IBD). Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is a chronic intestinal disease, known for its complex pathogenesis. Currently, it remains incurable and has a high prevalence worldwide, affecting an estimated 8 million individuals.We are an iGEM team from China, and we are committed to synthesizing E. coli with gene expression vectors, recombinant with selected inflammatory priming factors, adhesion factors, and anti-inflammatory factors for the treatment of IBD. Hope we can use the knowledge of synthetic biology to find a way out for IBD patients.

title: DetectiMOL - a Continuous Cortisol Monitoring Patch
text: DetectiMOL - a Continuous Cortisol Monitoring Patch. Cortisol is a hormone involved in immune response, regulating the body, and stress response. Continuous cortisol measurements can give important insights to imbalances in this hormone signalling, for example in Addison’s disease or stress. While many approaches are being investigated, no final continuous wearable cortisol measuring device is publicly available yet. In this project a molecular mechanism around the use of the glucocorticoid receptor that binds cortisol specifically is being developed. In the future the basic molecular mechanism for cortisol ligand binding measurements could be done by electrochemical impedance spectroscopy. Here the receptor is attached to a gold electrode and changes conformation upon ligand binding, which changes the resistivity of the electrode and therefore electric signal. This concept is then implemented into a small wearable device that resembles a glucose monitoring device worn by diabetes patients to go with a publicly already established design.

title: Bevatech: Rapid Anti-Counterfeiting Aptamer-based Lateral Flow Device for Detecting Bevacizumab
text: Bevatech: Rapid Anti-Counterfeiting Aptamer-based Lateral Flow Device for Detecting Bevacizumab. Drug counterfeiting has been a significant global threat in recent decades, accounting for over 6000 counterfeit cases in 2021. This issue poses a critical threat to cancer patients in vulnerable regions, including war regions and developing countries that do not have sufficient facilities for testing. In previous years, The U.S. The Food and Drug Administration identified more than 19 medical facilities distributing Bevacizumab, a vital cancer drug that explicitly targets Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor (VEGF). To tackle this problem, our team designed an aptamer-based lateral flow test strip that provides a rapid, affordable, and sensitive point-of-care device that can be distributed globally and operated without specialized expertise. We optimized a DNA aptamer sensor that sensitively binds to Bevacizumab active ingredients and immobilized it onto the LFA membrane. Through this innovation, potential improvement in patient treatment quality assurance can be achieved, ensuring access to genuine cancer treatment for all.

title: Bacillus Gemini: Plant Guard and Nematode Buster
text: Bacillus Gemini: Plant Guard and Nematode Buster. Nematode infestations are among the most destructive pathogens in agriculture. According to estimates by FAO of the United Nations, global losses in food and fiber crops due to nematode damage amount to approximately 12.3% annually. We have engineered Bacillus velezensis and Bacillus subtilis as chassis organisms based on their own characteristics. These bacteria work in concert to enhance plant immunity and exert nematocidal effects. Using Bacillus subtilis, we employ virus-like particles conjugated with immune-activating proteins through spontaneous covalent coupling. They can widely distribute from the plant's roots to the phyllosphere, serving to activate the plant's own immune response induction. Bacillus velezensis can detect changes in the level of phytohormones (salicylic acid) produced by plants in response to nematode damage. Upon sensing the signaling stimulation, the engineered bacteria are capable of producing antinematodal proteins, trans-aconitic acid, and antisense RNAs targeting important genes in nematode's life cycle, attacking nematodes from multiple aspects.

title: Surface Display of Tumor Targeting Proteins on Engineered Bacteria for Fighting Triple Negative Breast Cancer
text: Surface Display of Tumor Targeting Proteins on Engineered Bacteria for Fighting Triple Negative Breast Cancer. This project is aimed to display tumor-targeting SIRPα on surfaces of E coli that has an inner membrane and an outer membrane separated by the periplasm.  The transport unit of an outer membrane autotransporter called adhesin involved in diffuse adherence-I (AIDA-I) is chosen as the carrier for SIRPα, which facilitates the export across the cell envelope and anchor onto the bacterial cell surface with proper surface exposure.  A short peptide GGGGS is designed as a flexible linker between gene-encoding sequences, including the signal peptide of cholera toxin B subunit that has high binding affinity with raft-associated ganglioside as well as a His tag for the verification of protein expression with immunofluorescence.  A mathematic model has been developed for the elucidation of dynamic proteomic changes.  Integrated human practice has been conducted.  A wearable thermal ablation and portable diagnostic device has been established for early treatment and diagnosis.

title: Using thermostable and active Fast PETase enzyme to degrade PET plastics in simulated marine environment
text: Using thermostable and active Fast PETase enzyme to degrade PET plastics in simulated marine environment. Due to the influx of microplastic pollution in water systems, the abundance of polyethylene terephthalate (PET) plastics in the oceans causes issues for both marine and terrestrial life. The enzymes, PETase and MHETase, found in the bacterium Ideonella sakaiensis, have shown degradation of PET plastics. However, because I. sakaiensis is found mainly in soil, it is not an ideal host when attempting to degrade PET plastics in the ocean. By introducing Fast PETase (a more thermostable and active form of PETase) and MHETase into Alteromonas macleodii, a marine bacterium, there is the possibility of degradation of PET in saltwater conditions. Using the Loop Assembly method, plasmids were constructed with FastPETase and MHETase into E. coli, and conjugated into A. macleodii. Ongoing experiments comparing Fast PETase and PETase will demonstrate the possibility for a more efficient plastic degradation reaction, with degradation measured through concentration of hydroxyl groups in FTIR Analysis.

title: A Gene Editing Therapy of Hepatitis B Based on High-precision CRISPR Nuclease
text: A Gene Editing Therapy of Hepatitis B Based on High-precision CRISPR Nuclease. Viral hepatitis B is a common infectious disease affecting the world, the cause of which is hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection and induced autoimmune reaction. HBV cannot be eradicated with traditional chemical treatments, but it is possible with the safety-enhancing CRISPR-Cas gene editing tool. Aiming at curing hepatitis B with CRISPR-Cas gene editing technology, our project mainly carried out the following work: (1) On-target, off-target and gRNA were designed according to HBsAg gene. A high-throughput screening system consisting of three plasmids was constructed by optimized sacB and other screening genes. (2) A library of MAD7 mutants was constructed by zero-shot mutational effect prediction and error-prone PCR. A high-precision and high-activity MAD7 nuclease mutant (HF-MAD7) was screened out by high-throughput screening. Compared to MAD7(WT), the off-target rate is reduced by 96.80% and the editing activity is 59.51%. The project provides a reliable gene editing therapy for viral hepatitis B.

title: InfinityF∞ - an intranasal mRNA delivery system for Factor VIII using ionizable lipid nanoparticles
text: InfinityF∞ - an intranasal mRNA delivery system for Factor VIII using ionizable lipid nanoparticles. InfinityF∞ delivers the mRNA sequence for factor VIII encapsulated by a lipid nanoparticle that serves as a carrier for the medicine. When the nanoparticle reaches its target in the body, the cells will take it up into an endosome and break the LNP preserving the genetic sequence inside. After that, the cell produces the protein factor VIII from the mRNA and releases it into the blood. The factor VIII mRNA is produced with in vitro transcription using factor VIII pcDNA as a template. Our ionizable lipid nanoparticles contain synthetic lipids as well as an ionizable lipid, which is essential for the release of the mRNA in the cells.

title: Mechanism of creation and application of prokaryotic polyploid minimal chassis cells
text: Mechanism of creation and application of prokaryotic polyploid minimal chassis cells. In this study, we designed a novel prokaryotic polyploid minimal chassis system capable of stably maintaining both engineered and wild-type chromosomes. Morphological analysis revealed increased length, volume, and surface area in polyploid E. coli, with intracellular enrichment of metabolites like phenylalanine. This system showed enhanced stress resilience under high temperatures and varying pH levels, suggesting potential for evolutionary adaptation. Additionally, the chassis demonstrated improved carbon and protein metabolism, enhancing production of heterologous proteins such as GFP and poly-β-hydroxybutyrate PHB, with output exceeding that of streamlined and wild-type strains. We also developed a genome-scale metabolic network model for DGF-298 and its polyploid counterpart, integrating transcriptomic data to refine growth rates and biomass yield. Multi-objective optimizations within the metabolic model, combined with a deep learning-aided environmental model, enabled real-time PHB production predictions in fermenters via multi-sensor arrays.

title: Platelet-based Therapeutic to Recognize and Degrade Circulating Tumor Cell (CTC) Clusters
text: Platelet-based Therapeutic to Recognize and Degrade Circulating Tumor Cell (CTC) Clusters. The 2024 MIT iGEM team focused on developing a therapeutic to target and degrade CTC clusters to reduce metastatic potential in cancer patients. The team's innovative solution involves engineering platelets to recognize and bind to both CTCs and neutrophils. Once both binding events occur, the engineered platelets release cytotoxic signals to degrade the CTC clusters, thereby aiming to reduce metastasis. We conducted multiple proof-of-concept experiments testing the Syn-Notch and CC-GEMS systems using HEK293 cells as a model and documented our parts collection of robustly tested Syn-Notch systems in the iGEM Registry. In addition, our team established frameworks for both diffusion gradient modeling and background architecture for computational fluid modeling. As part of our human practice, we compiled a Genomic Privacy Handbook and collaborated with physicians and medical researchers to offer scientific and bioethical frameworks for both present and future iGEM teams.

title: IMPROViSeD : Integrated Modelling of Protein Complexes Via Single-shot registration using DREAM
text: IMPROViSeD : Integrated Modelling of Protein Complexes Via Single-shot registration using DREAM. The exploration of protein-protein interactions and their implications in cellular functions is pivotal for the development of effective therapeutic strategies. This project introduces IMPROVISeD, an advanced platform designed for the modeling of protein complexes. We create models in one shot by directly incorporating geometric constraints from extracted experimental data to orientate the structure of the subunits (proteins) forming the complex. The approach uses significantly less time compared to contemporary algorithms that employ sampling-based approaches. The approach was tested for both synthetically – and experimentally-derived constraint data. The method is permissive to missing and ambiguous constraint data. The underlying nonlinear optimization formulations, including one-shot registration, make IMPROViSeD's approach computationally efficient, robust, and scalable. The availability of modelled complexes provides key insights into the structure, function, and interactions of subunits and establishes a solid framework for designing targeted therapies. The tool can also be leveraged for modelling heterogeneous macromolecular complexes.

title: P-CASE
text: P-CASE. P-CASE is an innovative multiplex biosensor designed for the detection of pancreatic cancer using Surface Plasmon Resonance (SPR) technology. It integrates three detection chambers, each targeting a specific biomarker: CA19-9, Glypican-1 (GPC1) mRNA, and miR-206. The first chamber utilizes a DNA aptamer to bind CA19-9, the second employs a CRISPR-dCas13a system for GPC1 mRNA, and the third features a complementary ssDNA probe for miR-206 with a poly-A tail for enhanced sensor surface stability. This configuration enables simultaneous, real-time monitoring of these biomarkers, improving sensitivity and specificity for accurate diagnosis. P-CASE offers a novel approach for early pancreatic cancer detection and monitoring through a combination of synthetic biology and advanced diagnostic technologies.

title: Smart Algicidal Bacteria to Control Water Blooms
text: Smart Algicidal Bacteria to Control Water Blooms. Eutrophication of water bodies can lead to cyanobacterial blooms, which cause serious harm to water ecosystems and the safety of drinking water.    Algicidal bacteria (e.g., Bacillus subtilis) is a kind of bacteria that can directly or indirectly kill algal cells or inhibit their growth.    Although algicidal bacteria can inhibit the growth of cyanobacteria and solve the problem of water blooms, the overgrowth and proliferation of any kind of microorganisms may hurt the natural environment.    This project aims to develop and design a controllable ‘smart algicide bacteria’ that can inhibit the spread of bloom and also regulate the growth of algicide bacteria to prevent secondary pollution to the environment.    We hope to provide an efficient and safe solution to the cyanobacterial problem and demonstrate the potential of synthetic biology applications in environmental governance, opening up new possibilities for future ecological protection and resource management.

title: Gassle
text: Gassle. We have devised Gassle, an E. coli that detects nitric oxide (NO), which is produced in large quantities during inflammation. This research explores the possibility of diagnosing Inflammatory Bowel Disease (IBD) through characteristic fart odors. Early immunosuppressive therapy has been shown to improve response to treatment and reduce adverse outcomes. This is because it leads to mucosal healing, reduced hospitalizations and surgeries, and improved quality of life. Our Project has three main components. First, development of E. coli that detects elevated nitric oxide concentrations during inflammation and produces propionic acid. Second, control of E. coli proliferation using Herpes Simplex Virus Thymidine Kinase/Ganciclovir system(HSV-TK/GCV) system. Third, development of a capsule to deliver E. coli to the colon.

title: Rational Construction of Saccharomyces Cerevisiae Strain for Utilization of Xylose
text: Rational Construction of Saccharomyces Cerevisiae Strain for Utilization of Xylose. Fuel ethanol, with its high octane number and clean combustion, is a promising biofuel alternative to petrochemical energy. A sustainable approach involves cellulosic ethanol production from lignocellulosic biomass, known for its tough texture and complex structure. After pretreatment, it releases both glucose and xylose, but wild-type Saccharomyces cerevisiae, a key strain for ethanol production, cannot naturally utilize xylose. Enhancing its ability to metabolize xylose requires introducing metabolic pathways for xylose isomerization, often achieved through laboratory adaptive evolution, which can be time-consuming and may lead to unstable strain phenotypes. This study aimed to overcome these limitations by reconstructing the xylose utilization pathway in S. cerevisiae. We identified the NFS1I492N gene mutation and integrated the multi-copy xylA gene, which encodes xylose isomerase, to enable efficient xylose metabolism. This approach seeks to develop more robust S. cerevisiae strains capable of efficiently converting xylose into ethanol, contributing to more sustainable biofuel production.

title: CarvengerX：Novel exosomal tumor therapy using bidirectional calcium overload platform built with synthetic biology
text: CarvengerX：Novel exosomal tumor therapy using bidirectional calcium overload platform built with synthetic biology. UM_Macau utilized synthetic biology to construct a controlled calcium overload system for killing cancer cells. We selected the MscS and hTPRC1 ion channels, which are sensitive to ultrasound, as the target proteins and introduced their gene sequences into different plasmids to express these ion channel proteins on the chassis cell HEK293. After successfully expressing the channel proteins, we used the lamp2b protein to package the them, also synthesized using synthetic biology, into vesicles (EVs) using exocytosis. We then allowed the vesicles to fuse with the target cell. Finally, we induced the calcium ion channels on the cancer cell membrane and the endoplasmic reticulum calcium release channel (RyR) in the cancer cells to open under the combined action of ultrasound and hNOS2, significantly increasing the intracellular calcium influx and releasing the calcium the endoplasmic reticulum. This triggered calcium overload in cancer cells, leading to cell death and achieving an anti-cancer effect.

title: PalettEmo
text: PalettEmo. PalettEmo is composed of "Palette" and "Emotion", aiming to combine AI emotion weighting algorithm and synthetic biology art. We innovatively constructed Quorum sensing with Fluorescence Resonance Energy Transfer (FRET), which can achieve quantitative control to produce mixed fragrance automatically. As for model, we not only successfully constructed a Facial Expression Recognition model with an accuracy rate of up to 92%, achieving new state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance and surpassing the previous best models, but also integrated model and Wet Lab closely to assist in selecting FRET linkers. Starting from the mechanisms of FRET and visual perception, we created a theoretical attraction method for scent molecules and emotion, and explored the biological processes behind color recognition and emotional changes. We delve into society to receive feedback and spread education to the world, building PalettEmo influence and promoting global welfare.

title: Metabolic engineering and synthetic biology ​approaches for L-DOPA ​production in Nicotiana benthamiana​ using BaMV-based vector
text: Metabolic engineering and synthetic biology ​approaches for L-DOPA ​production in Nicotiana benthamiana​ using BaMV-based vector. Our project explores innovative approaches to produce and test L-DOPA, a critical drug for Parkinson's disease treatment, using plant-based methods. In the first experiment, total RNA was extracted from beet. Then the BvAD6 and BvADH genes were cloned into plasmid vectors, and introduced into Agrobacterium tumefaciens. These transformed bacteria were then used to infiltrate Nicotiana benthamiana. The infiltrated leaves were analyzed to assess L-DOPA content using HPLC. Building on this, the second experiment tested the efficacy of the L-DOPA in treating Parkinson-like symptoms in zebrafish embryos. L-DOPA was obtained from tobacco overexpressing L-DOPA, as well as from industrial synthesis. The study aimed to validate the potential of transgenic plants to produce sufficient quantities of L-DOPA and to assess and to evaluate whether plant-derived neurodegenerative drugs are more effective than industrially synthesized drugs in alleviating symptoms of related diseases.

title: ReguROS
text: ReguROS. Our project focuses on developing a versatile platform for early detection and treatment of diseases by targeting reactive oxygen species (ROS). Elevated ROS levels are a common indicator in both plant and human diseases. The platform aims to engineer probiotic E. coli Nissle 1917 and the yeast S. cerevisiae to detect high ROS levels and produce therapeutic agents or visible signals. by implementing high-pass filter behavior in promoters bound by the transcription factors OxyR, Yap1 and TGA2. This innovation seeks to improve disease management and outcomes in agriculture and medicine, addressing case study problems of fireblight in plants and chronic inflammation in humans.

title: SepScan: a rapid, quantitative, point-of-care-test for Sepsis and acute kidney injury
text: SepScan: a rapid, quantitative, point-of-care-test for Sepsis and acute kidney injury. Sepsis contributes up to 11 million preventable deaths annually. The burden of disease is particularly concentrated in India, where advances in rapid-diagnostics is a neglected path to improving health outcomes. Recognising this, the UCL iGEM team developed asepsis scanning tool (SepScan). SepScan is a point-of care-test (POCT) to provide a quantitative read out of biomarker concentration for distribution in low and middle income countries. By using nanobody-nanoluciferase fusion proteins, we offer a new modality for lateral flow that can be adapted to suit other biomarkers, with further potential applications in pandemic preparedness. With a particular emphasis on sepsis and acute kidney injury in India, SepScan aims to provide a rapid readout of urinary cystatin c. By aiming to increase the information capital of clinicians in resource constrained environments, this can be used to aid healthcare or community workers with triaging, managing risk, and ultimately saving preventable deaths in underserved communities.

title: Logical Gate-Based Synergistic Toxicity Detection System
text: Logical Gate-Based Synergistic Toxicity Detection System. Environmental endocrine disruptors (EDCs) are chemicals that can mimic or interfere with natural hormones, primarily affecting organisms through endocrine disruption by interacting with hormone receptors. However, studies suggest they may also induce oxidative stress and other effects, causing more profound impacts. Traditional detection only monitors single endocrine disruption effects, neglecting the combined toxicological effects within organisms. We aim to assess these complex effects using a microbial sensor based on multiple logic gates. We've developed a hormone-sensitive intein to detect endocrine disruption and used the recA element from the SOS response to identify oxidative damage. An AND gate detection circuit with HRP regulation network enables the simultaneous detection of both effects. Additionally, we've designed a high-throughput, automated, portable fluorescence detection platform for our biosensor. Our project helps identify EDCs and monitor their oxidative damage effects, which is crucial for a comprehensive assessment of their potential impacts on organisms.

title: NOVA by Agrinova: Microbial SOILutions for Precision Agriculture
text: NOVA by Agrinova: Microbial SOILutions for Precision Agriculture. NOVA is an innovative device that combines hardware and synthetic biology to enable real-time detection of heavy metal contamination, specifically cadmium and manganese, in agricultural settings. Engineered E. coli plasmids with metal-sensitive promoters trigger the expression of fluorescent reporter genes upon detecting these metals. This fluorescence allows NOVA to generate measurable signals corresponding to the concentrations of cadmium and manganese. Designed as a versatile, cost-effective fluorometer, NOVA is accessible to a wide range of users, including student researchers and small-scale farmers. By integrating microfluidics and sensitive optical sensors, the device offers an efficient, user-friendly way to detect fluorescence. Its stepper motor enables multiple parallel tests, improving efficiency while maintaining accuracy. NOVA's affordability and scalability make it a valuable tool for real-time heavy metal detection and broader environmental monitoring, offering a practical, low-cost solution for research and educational purposes.

title: Pandage - An intelligent approach to infection disease control on skin wound healing with probiotics
text: Pandage - An intelligent approach to infection disease control on skin wound healing with probiotics. Bacterial skin wound infections are a global health issue, in addition to the overuse of antibiotics has led to antimicrobial resistance (AMR), causing significant global mortality, with infections in hospitals and military settings being particularly severe. Traditional wound management has been a “reactive” process, and often results in slower recovery or even serious medical complications. Here, we have developed Pandage, designed for individualized wound infection control and healing. Pandage integrates monitoring, automatic drug delivery, and wound healing promotion. We used engineered probiotics (Lactococcus lactis) to secrete growth factors (GM-CSF) to promote wound healing.To assess wound condition, we utilize anti-LPS aptamer biosensors to detect harmful bacteria, releasing antimicrobial peptide (AMP) after the Pandage Intelligent Treatment Modeling. In addition, Pandage is also equipped with Bluetooth module to enable mobile health (mHealth) operation. We hope Pandage can tailor treatment to each patient's specific wound condition for optimizing wound care managemen

title: Tumor-Targeting Salmonella-Mediated Apoptosis Therapy (T-SAT)
text: Tumor-Targeting Salmonella-Mediated Apoptosis Therapy (T-SAT). Westlake team has developed a novel cancer therapy, Tumor-Targeting Salmonella-Mediated Apoptosis Therapy, utilizing an attenuated strain of Salmonella (VNP20009) to deliver a targeted therapeutic system. This strain is engineered with a surface-displayed single-chain variable fragment (scFv) to recognize cancer-specific antigens, enhancing its invasion efficacy. Upon internalization, a bacterial auto-lysis circuit is activated, releasing plasmids that form a cancer-specific killing system. This system includes an effector gene for inducing apoptosis and a bio-switch to regulate effector gene expression based on intracellular signals. To optimize the therapy, a mathematical model was developed to simulate the diffusion, growth, and bactericidal effects of the engineered Salmonella within the tumor microenvironment. The model provides insights into optimal dosing and timing, aiming to maximize therapeutic efficacy. This approach holds promise for treating cancers with limited treatment options, such as liver and metastatic breast cancer.

title: CalciCapture
text: CalciCapture. Developing synthetic biology based carbon capture solutions using marine coccolithophore Emiliania Huxleyi. Our project aims to enhance the process of calcification in E. huxleyi to increase its carbon capture capacity. Through computational modelling, we have identified key cellular and environmental factors that promote calcification.

title: New Tagatose-4-epimerase with high conversion rate through gene mining and protein engineering
text: New Tagatose-4-epimerase with high conversion rate through gene mining and protein engineering. D-Tagatose, a functional sugar, holds promise as a therapeutic agent for type II diabetes. However, the current fructose-catalyzed production of tagatose faces challenges, including limited enzyme sources and low conversion rates. In this project, gene mining was utilized to identify sequences with potential tagatose-4-epimerase activity, resulting in an increased tagatose yield of 24 g/(L·h) and a conversion rate of 37% through iterative mutation. The enzymatic properties of the most effective mutants were subsequently analyzed. Additionally, this project tackled the issue of inclusion bodies arising from the expression of the new enzyme by employing molecular chaperones, pro-fusion labeling, and fermentation optimization. The new enzyme and the best mutant components developed in this project can be utilized by future iGEM teams.

title: Prometheus: Large Language Model for Synthetic Biology
text: Prometheus: Large Language Model for Synthetic Biology. Over the past fifty years, synthetic biology has achieved significant advancements, with last year marking the 20th anniversary of iGEM. Despite these accomplishments, the complexity of components and disorganized knowledge structures have hindered its full potential. As we enter iGEM’s new decade, NJU-China's 2024 goal is to unlock synthetic biology’s potential using new tools. We utilized a knowledge graph as the foundational database architecture and leveraged a large language model to facilitate processes such as raw data cleaning, database retrieval, and natural language dialogue with users. We developed Prometheus, a professional-grade, novice-friendly synthetic biology language model. Prometheus helps users retrieve components, construct plasmids, and guide experimental design, thus promoting synthetic biology. After completing the development of Prometheus, we successfully promoted the model among a wide audience through extensive Human Practice activities, unleashing the fire of synthetic biology.

title: Tumor-Specific Gene Nanoparticles
text: Tumor-Specific Gene Nanoparticles. Two signals are required to induce T cell activation and proliferation: binding of CD3 to the TCR to form the TCR-CD3 complex to deliver the first activation signal and the second signal generated by synergistic co-stimulatory molecules, mainly CD86. We designed a tumor-specific gene nanomedicine such that it expresses only anti-CD3 scFv (αCD3, CD3 activator) and anti-CD86 scfv (αCD86, CD86 activator) on the surface of tumor cells while mobilizing the tumor cells to secrete IL-2, a cytokine for T-cell proliferation and survival, in order to activate the T-cells and to enhance the immunotherapy effect. This study provides a strategy to maximize immunotherapy efficacy independent of tumor heterogeneity.

title: Addressing Cutibacterium acnes acne by genetically altering E. coli to secrete PFK1 acting on biofilm
text: Addressing Cutibacterium acnes acne by genetically altering E. coli to secrete PFK1 acting on biofilm. Acne is the most common skin condition in the US. Recent research provides significant insight into the mechanisms Cutibacterium acnes to developing acne, including the ability of C. acnes to form a biofilm. The biofilm matrix of C. Acnes is composed of 62.6% polysaccharides, 9.6% proteins, 4.0% DNA, and 23.8% other compounds. By manipulating the innate carbohydrate degradation of C. acnes, the degradation of the extracellular matrix can hypothetically be promoted.  This study evaluated modified E. coli strain .By using a plasmid which will be engineered to synthesize and secrete PFK1 (catalyst of glycolysis) that can degrade polysaccharide found in C acne. Since the biofilm is rich in carbohydrates, increasing the glycolytic activity of E. coli by inserting a catalyst will allow for degradation of the biofilm. In the future, we aim to utilize a hydrogel or enzymatic transporter to administer this catalyst to C. acnes.

title: Toward the COSMIC Dream: Space ‘Tai Chi’
text: Toward the COSMIC Dream: Space ‘Tai Chi’. Humans have a growing desire for space exploration. For astronauts, there are still some tricky problems, such as circadian rhythm disorder and circulatory disorder. iGEM Tianjin 2024 created ‘Space Tai Chi’，which was inspired by Chinese traditional culture. We constructed two plasmids and transformed them into one yeast, aiming at providing melatonin and crocetin for astronauts. We designed a blue light-galactose dual-factor orthogonal system to regulate the synthesis process. On the one hand, melatonin synthesis is controlled by optogenetics. Utilize blue light to induce photosensitive protein to activate the enhancer, thereby promoting the expression of melatonin synthesis gene. On the other hand, when exogenous galactose is added，it will induce the expression of crocetin synthsis gene. We also constructed fusion proteins through EBD to reduce leakage in the system. In the future, life support system based on synbiomanufacturing will escort human exploration of the cosmic world！

title: Yeastea - An oscillatory yeast-derived skincare solution for enhanced skin barrier repair
text: Yeastea - An oscillatory yeast-derived skincare solution for enhanced skin barrier repair. Sensitive skin affects approximately 60% of the global population, leading to an increasing demand for safe and effective skincare solutions. However, natural ingredients like (–)-α-bisabolol, known for the anti-inflammatory properties, are costly when combined with yeast extracts. To address this, we designed "Yeastea", a novel 2+1 yeast-fermented skincare product combining (–)-α-bisabolol, ceramides, and yeast extract for enhanced skin barrier repair. We engineered Saccharomyces cerevisiae to produce the key ingredients via the genetic oscillator that reduces cytotoxicity and enhances the yeast lifespan. We increased ceramide production by 37%. This innovative yeast-fermented skincare product offers an affordable, sustainable solution for sensitive skin, with a broader future in the skincare and cosmetic industry.

title: Enhancing Bone Repair: Solving the Burst Release Problem in Regenerative Materials with Fusion-Expressed Cell Factors
text: Enhancing Bone Repair: Solving the Burst Release Problem in Regenerative Materials with Fusion-Expressed Cell Factors. Bone injuries, scoliosis, and bone defects are major health issues in China, caused by trauma, infections, tumors, or congenital diseases, causing functional impairment and pain. Current treatments like autografts, allografts, and artificial bone materials have limitations. Autografts are limited by donor availability and need extra surgery. Allografts risk rejection and infection. Artificial bone materials lack biocompatibility and bioactive components. Our study aims to develop a dual-cell factor(VEGF&BMP-4) release system with collagen-binding properties, addressing the limitations of artificial bone materials, to ensure safe and rapid bone formation, reducing risks of oncogenesis and ectopic ossification. The innovative dual-cell factor release design allows for the enhancement of repair efficacy while reducing the side effects associated with non-sequential release, to offer a far more efficient and safer bone repair solution. The proposed system illustrates significant potential for broad clinical applications, by elevating and refining the treatment of bone defects and associated conditions.

title: Application and development of nanomedical drugs based on RNA interference technology in inhibiting pan allergens
text: Application and development of nanomedical drugs based on RNA interference technology in inhibiting pan allergens. Populus tomentosa allergy, common in Beijing and northeastern China during spring and fall, often leads to allergic rhinitis and asthma (Liu et al., 2010). Our product utilizes RNA interference (RNAi) technology to suppress two key pan-allergenic proteins: Heat Shock Protein 70 (HSP 70) and Profilin 3 (PFN 3), effectively reducing allergic reactions. The siRNA vector is delivered via polyethyleneimine-modified carbon quantum dots (PEI-CDs), a nanoparticle system that facilitates siRNA delivery into plant cells. We are exploring leaf and trunk injection methods for real-life applications, with potential for a spray method in the future to target a wider range of plant species. The targeting of HSP 70 and PFN 3 provides a generalized application for trees with these allergenic proteins.

title: Spidey Microbe: Adhesion and interaction Network drug-delivery platform for Parkinson's Disease treatment
text: Spidey Microbe: Adhesion and interaction Network drug-delivery platform for Parkinson's Disease treatment. We have engineered a superhero—Spidey Microbe. We have analyzed probiotics by constructing databases and software packages, and screened for Escherichia coli Nissle1917, Lactococcus lactis F44, and Lactobacillus plantarum ATCC 8014.This includes a biotin-affinity based gut adhesion system and a quorum sensing-based interaction system, allowing the probiotics to "weave webs" and adhere the gut as well as Spider-man. We aim to design genetic circuits to control the expression of mucin binding protein in EcN and facilitate inter-probiotic adhesion to control Spidey Microbe's "spider silk" in the gut. Additionally, we plan to endow Spidey Microbe with enhanced superpowers, so we are developing cell factories in Lactococcus lactis F44 to express various therapeutic agents. Spidey Microbe will challenge the disease “monsters”—Parkinson's Disease.

title: Opening the Door to Self-Induced Chemical Synthesis with Riboswitches
text: Opening the Door to Self-Induced Chemical Synthesis with Riboswitches. Our project addresses critical challenges in the biomanufacturing industry, where dependence on costly exogenous inducers limits production efficiency. We have developed a self-induced production system that utilizes riboswitches and the LacI repressor (New Composite Parts), incorporating two distinct lysis mechanisms (New Improved Parts). By employing these innovative riboswitch systems, we improved the expression of biosynthesis gene clusters in response to their products, leading to a significant increase in product titers: riboflavin production reached 414.31 mg/L (versus 66.16 mg/L in the control), while TPP production reached 364.59 mg/L (versus 65.14 mg/L). Additionally, our improved thermally inducible lysis system achieved a lysis rate that was 30.45% higher than that of the previously constructed arabinose-induced system. We also optimized a quorum-sensing (QS) lysis system, which outperformed the earlier light-sensing system in both lysis efficiency and operational effectiveness. These innovations provide novel solutions for enhancing efficiency in biomanufacturing, reducing costs, and streamlining operational workflows.

title: Liver-Brain Guardian: Engineering Bacteria to prevent Hepatic encephalopathy
text: Liver-Brain Guardian: Engineering Bacteria to prevent Hepatic encephalopathy. Hepatic encephalopathy (HE) , which develops from liver cirhosis, causes increasing mortality worldwide and places huge burden on patients and the society. However, preventing HE has been challenging, with medication mainly focus on alleviating syptoms after developing HE and have long-term side effects. Here, we demonstrate a synthetic biology-inspired probiotic therapeutic, Liver-Brain Guardian, to automatically respond to the level of HE biomarker and initiate the degradation of HE pathogenic factor, and could improve intestinal barrier function and epithelial recovery. Our results showed that the engineered bacteira(EcN) can successfully sense the rising level of PEA, a reliable risk factor in HE patients , and activate the FeaR-TynA inducible promoter system to initiate the downstream metabolic module to degrade ammonia. Our approach offers an exciting and promising way to help cirrhosis patients with high risk of developing HE from progressing and start in-time treatment.

title: Soil-IQ: An In-plant Soil Nitrate Indicator for Producers in the Developing World
text: Soil-IQ: An In-plant Soil Nitrate Indicator for Producers in the Developing World. Farmers in the developing world currently lack affordable, intuitive systems for optimizing fertilizer use. As a result, many under or overfertilize, harming their yields, and damaging the environment. Many sustainable development practices make farmers feel like they have to choose between their livelihoods and the environment, leading to decreased results of efforts to alleviate poverty or to protect the environment. Soil-IQ utilizes a novel nitrate detecting promoter and an intuitive colorimetric reporter to help farmers know when they have fertilized enough to maximize their yields without harming the environment. Designed for farmers and by farmers, Soil-IQ removes the guesswork in fertilizer optimization and helps farmers be both sustainable and more productive. As a result, Soil-IQ helps protect those at most risk from climate change and environmental degradation while simultaneously enabling them to create more resilient and efficient farms, making sustainable development a win-win for both farmers and other stakeholders.

title: Engineering Fate for Myogenic Lineages
text: Engineering Fate for Myogenic Lineages. Here we show a synthetic biology system for the engineering of the fate of myogenic lineages from normal fibroblasts. The ultimate goal would be the creation of a synthetic driver-detector system that could be deployed in induced pluripotent stem cells to drive to muscle formation for therapeutic applications. We have used Normal Human Dermal Fibroblasts (NHDF) cells as the starter cell line on which we construct our system for overexpression of MYOD-1 induced by doxycycline. Initial results obtained suggest that these lineages can be engineered efficiently and future work will couple secreted luciferase reporters for efficient and high-throughput detection of lineage commitment.

title: Engineering probiotic OMVs with encapsulated CRISPR/Cas9 ribonucleoproteins for targeted gene editing
text: Engineering probiotic OMVs with encapsulated CRISPR/Cas9 ribonucleoproteins for targeted gene editing. Gram-negative bacteria naturally produce spherical nanovesicles known as outer membrane vesicles (OMVs) during their growth. These OMVs, due to their nanoscale size, efficient cellular uptake, and ability to protect biomolecules, are ideal for drug delivery. In this project, we aim to genetically modify E. coli Nissle 1917 (ECN) to produce OMVs with surface-displayed targeting elements and encapsulated Cas9 RNPs. By filtering through molecular sieves, we obtain OMVs capable of targeted gene-editing complex delivery, potentially revolutionizing precision medicine.

title: GHK: HEP(Hair Expecto Patronum)
text: GHK: HEP(Hair Expecto Patronum). At present, the problem of hair loss is becoming more and more serious, and the trend of younger age is serious, which seriously affects the physical and mental health of patients.    Copper peptide (GHK-Cu) is a tripeptide ultra-short peptide, which has significant effects on hair follicle repair and hair loss treatment with less side effects, and is widely used in the beauty industry, and.is a current research hotspot. This year, our team adopted series expression to efficiently express copper peptides in engineered bacteria, and adopted quorum sensing technology to build a controlled bacterial ecosystem, trying to improve its production efficiency. In addition, we use microemulsions coated with copper peptides to present the product. The application of this series of innovative technologies aims to effectively solve the problem of hair loss with minimal side effects and help people get rid of hair loss.

title: HBUT-Wuhan:  Manufacturing a hypoglycemic peptide Vglycin for diabetic patients
text: HBUT-Wuhan:  Manufacturing a hypoglycemic peptide Vglycin for diabetic patients. There are over 540 million people suffering from diabetes mellitus globally. Although numerous medications have been approved to control blood glucose levels, the side effects present huge challenges for their application. P37, a novel oral hypoglycemic peptide group derived from soybeans, has been shown to improve blood glucose in mice and in clinic. However, direct extraction from soybeans is problematic due to low yields, complex processes and high cost. HBUT-Wuhan plans to use synthetic biology to produce Vglycin (Vg), a member of P37 family that have huge potential to be innovative medicine. Finally, we successfully constructed the GS115 expression system of Vglycin, and optimize the parts in the construct to improve its yield. Our findings also indicated that the mutation at position 28 to Ala has stronger affinity with the receptor. In the future we would like to further study the expression of mutational Vg in Pichia pastoris.

title: From Longan to Astaxanthin—— A Curious Fusion of Science and Nature
text: From Longan to Astaxanthin—— A Curious Fusion of Science and Nature. With the attention to health, astaxanthin has entered our field of vision. It is a keto carotenoid, known as the "king of antioxidants." However, at present, in addition to the high content of astaxanthin extracted from Rhodium pluvium algae, the content of astaxanthin extracted from other sources is relatively low. Therefore, our team proposed a scheme to extract astaxanthin from longan leaves. We introduced the target genes from Chlamydomonas rheinensis and Rhodococcus pluvialis into longan leaves for expression to improve astaxanthin extraction. We will apply the exploration of this proposition to the beauty industry. At the same time, we conducted a series of publicity activities and the production of popular science videos to pass this exploration to more groups and let more people know about this research and development results.

title: Intereting pathway to chenolic compounds degradation
text: Intereting pathway to chenolic compounds degradation. Inshore pollution concerns scientists and governments. The inshore ecosystem is vital but suffers more pollution. Public awareness of marine protection is growing, yet phenolic compounds are overlooked pollutants. Phenols can damage organisms and are hard to degrade. In this year, QS-FMI aims to solve phenols pollution by designing a synthetic biological pathway.

title: IchthyoCare - Providing a Substitution Therapy for the Skin Disease Ichthyosis
text: IchthyoCare - Providing a Substitution Therapy for the Skin Disease Ichthyosis. Ichthyosis is a group of rare, genetically inherited skin disorders characterised by severe dryness, scaling, and disrupted skin barriers due to malfunctioning enzymes. Current treatments are limited and time-consuming, often requiring individuals to spend hours each day managing their skin. Our project, IchthyoCare, aimed to tackle the underlying cause of ichthyosis by developing an enzyme replacement therapy utilising liposomal drug delivery technology. Our evidence suggests that we have encapsulated purified 12R-LOX, expressed in an E. coli system, within large unilamellar vesicles. This would hopefully improve the skin, and moving forward the idea is that the encapsulated enzymes would be applied topically, with liposomes facilitating fusion with skin cells to deliver the therapeutic enzymes directly. This strategy will hopefully lessen the symptoms and decrease the time affected individuals need to spend taking care of their skin.

title: Entero Guard, a probiotic system for safe and efficient detection and treatment of IBD
text: Entero Guard, a probiotic system for safe and efficient detection and treatment of IBD. To address the shortcomings in current treatments for IBD, we presented Entero Guard, an automatic engineered probiotic system that can diagnose and treat IBD efficiently and safely.  We first designed a biodiagnosis strain that contains ThsS and ThsR to form a signaling network after detecting sulfide to detect inflammation. We then added a CRISPR based editor system to amplify the signal reaction by controlling our drug--AvCystatin's expression, which plays a crucial role in regulating macrophage immune responses, activating cellular MAP kinase and inducing the expression of IL-10 and IL-12/23, thereby effectively alleviating gut inflammation. To control drug expression, we designed a suicide switch with PnorV, a key biobrick that can detect the level of nitric oxide in gut and eventually activate a toxic protein, MazF, which leads to cell apoptosis. we wish this idea can bring new possibility for IBD treatment and help IBD patients return to a normal life.

title: Enzymatic DNA
text: Enzymatic DNA. This project aims to advance DNA synthesis technology by developing a novel enzymatic approach utilizing Terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase (TdT). Despite TdT's potential for template-free DNA synthesis, its random nucleotide addition limits its practical application. We will harness directed evolution to enhance the catalytic activity and capacity of the wild-type TdT from Zonotrichia albicollis (ZaTdT). Additionally, we will design and synthesize deoxynucleotide substrates with reversibly protected 3' termini, allowing for controlled nucleotide incorporation. This combination aims to achieve precise and orderly enzymatic DNA synthesis, addressing the efficiency and purity challenges associated with traditional chemical methods. By integrating these innovations, our project seeks to establish a greener, more efficient DNA synthesis platform, paving the way for advancements in genomics, synthetic biology, and data storage technologies.

title: HERMES - An Improved Bacterial Delivery System for Targeting Solid Tumours
text: HERMES - An Improved Bacterial Delivery System for Targeting Solid Tumours. Cancer remains the second leading cause of death worldwide. Chemotherapy, radiotherapy, and surgery remain front line treatments however, their systemic toxicity remains a notable concern as over 65% of patients suffer from severe adverse side effects. McMaster_Canada aims to utilize the oncogenic nature of bacteria to develop Hermes, a platform technology that localizes and regulates therapeutic delivery at the tumour site.  Our team designed a synthetic protien inspired by FAP2 on Fusobacterium nucleatum (F. nucleatum/Fn), that allows the our chassis, E. coli Nissle 1917, to colonize and co-exist in the tumour by binding to the overexpressed sugars - Gal-GalnAC. Once colonized, Hermes is equipped with a tumour microenvironment sensor that selectively triggers the production of a therapeutic agent at the site of the tumour. Using Hermes, we aim to improve clinical application of in-sera bacterial delivery system by reducing the dosage while maintain specificity for tumour colonization.

title: Detection of Fusarium oxysporum f.sp. cubense through an Optimized Lux and Hardware System
text: Detection of Fusarium oxysporum f.sp. cubense through an Optimized Lux and Hardware System. Our project addresses the issue of the Panama wilt disease caused by Fusarium oxysporum f.sp  cubense (Foc).  This disease clogs the plant's xylem vessels; leading to water and nutrient deprivation, defoliation, and plant death. Panama is a significant banana producer in Latin America, yielding approximately 2.5 million tons annually, contributing about $200 million to Panama's economy. Foc TR4 has rendered Cavendish susceptible to Fusarium Wilt and little can be done through isolation due to it being largely asymptomatic. Our solution involves engineering bacteria for early detection of Foc through signal detection, amplification, and propagation.  A genetic circuit is activated by fusaric acid produced by the fungus through an inducible promoter. Upon detection, the signal is amplified by a positive feedback loop of AHL through Lux quorum sensing.  Signal Propagation is achieved through an optimized BRET reporter protein triggered by the AHL-LuxR activator and its compatibility with the hardware.

title: B.A.R.B.I.E. Bioengineered Aquatic pollutants Removal and Bio-sensing through Integrated Eco-filter
text: B.A.R.B.I.E. Bioengineered Aquatic pollutants Removal and Bio-sensing through Integrated Eco-filter.
