This system provides a robust foundation for the efficient biosynthesis of isoorientin and supports its potential large-scale production as a natural therapeutic for diabetes.

title: Inexpensive EGFR Mutation Detection Kit for Early Diagnosis of Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer
text: Inexpensive EGFR Mutation Detection Kit for Early Diagnosis of Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer. Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer-related deaths, with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) accounting for 85% of cases. Current detection methods are either invasive or costly, limiting accessibility. Our project aims to develop an affordable, non-invasive diagnostic kit for early detection of NSCLC by targeting EGFR mutations, a key biomarker. Using padlock probes and rolling circle amplification (RCA) coupled with a split lettuce probe detection mechanism, the kit amplifies and identifies the mutated sequence in cell-free DNA from patient blood samples. This process eliminates the need for expensive PCR equipment, making the test accessible in low-resource settings. The fluorescent signal generated by the lettuce probe binding to the amplified product indicates the presence of the mutation. By providing a preliminary diagnosis, this kit can help identify high-risk individuals earlier, increasing the chances of timely treatment before the cancer advances to critical stages.

title: ATLAS.Y:Advanved Targeting Localization Assistance System for Yeast
text: ATLAS.Y:Advanved Targeting Localization Assistance System for Yeast. ATLAS.Y is a specialized tool designed to optimize protein subcellular localization within yeast. It uses signal peptide and linker databases to engineer fusion proteins with precise localization signals. The software employs the ESM-fold model for fast 3D structure prediction, the Rosetta model to assess protein stability, and the CAD-score to ensure functional consistency. DeepLoc 2.0 assists in verifying localization accuracy. Additionally, ATLAS.Y uses a graph-based deep learning algorithm for directed evolution, allowing proteins to adapt to specific microenvironments. For applications requiring precise control, the system offers a dynamic version integrating optogenetics for spatiotemporal regulation of protein localization.

title: CelluGuard: Desert Tree Survival Enhancer
text: CelluGuard: Desert Tree Survival Enhancer. The area of global desertification is expanding at a rate of 23 football fields per minute, posing a significant threat to the availability of land. Over the years, China has actively fulfilled its commitments under the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification and has made notable progress. However, the global rate of desertification remains alarming, severely threatening ecological security and sustainable development. As a group of high school students committed to a responsible future, we have engineered Komagataeibacter xylinus to produce bacterial cellulose (BC) more efficiently. BC possesses exceptional water-retention properties, is environmentally friendly, and does not hinder the growth and development of tree roots, making it an ideal candidate as a water-retaining matrix material for afforestation in deserts. By enriching BC around the roots of tree, we aim to enhance the drought tolerance and survival rate of newly transplanted trees, thereby contributing to the mitigation of land desertification.

title: LA&N: Yeast-Derived Human Lactoferrin and N-Acetylneuraminic Acid as Supplements for Infants
text: LA&N: Yeast-Derived Human Lactoferrin and N-Acetylneuraminic Acid as Supplements for Infants. In the face of economic pressures and epidemic challenges, China's breastfeeding rate is a concern. The high cost and limited nutritional value of formula milk have placed a financial burden on many families. This project aims to use Saccharomyces cerevisiae for the low-cost production of two important nutrients in the growth of infants and young children: lactoferrin and N-acetylneuraminic acid. We introduced the human lactoferrin synthesis gene and the high-yield Neu5Ac synthesis gene into Saccharomyces cerevisiae cells using the pESC-URA plasmid vector, respectively. Subsequently, the functions of the engineered cells were verified using a variety of methods, including kits and SDS-PAGE, and the production of the target product was finally confirmed. Our goal is to provide economical nutritional supplements that promote the health and well-being of infants and relieve the psychological stress of mothers who are unable to breastfeed themselves.

title: SynBio missile : barrier clearance and immune enhancement strategy targeting OSCC tumor microenvironment
text: SynBio missile : barrier clearance and immune enhancement strategy targeting OSCC tumor microenvironment. Regarding cancer solutions, remodeling the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME) and enhancing the activation of immune-infiltrating cells through multifaceted strategies is considered one of the most promising avenues to overcome these challenges. Currently, a series of immune checkpoint inhibitors have gained clinical acceptance to improve the immunosuppressive environment within the tumor and enhance the anti-tumor effects of CD8+ T lymphocytes. And synthetic biology serves as a possible approach to enable the coordinated release of defective cytokines in the tumor microenvironment (TME) to be able to produce similar immunomodulatory effects. Targeting the OSCC tumor microenvironment to achieve barrier clearance and immune enhancement through specific components or structures in the TME that induce tumor immunosuppression has aroused our interest. Through studying the literature and communicating with expert predecessors, we focused on choosing the bacterial-encoded hyaluronidase Hy and flagellin FlaB as our key research molecules.

title: ChloroNova: Proposing Algal Chloroplast as the New Status Quo for Biopharmaceutical Peptide Production
text: ChloroNova: Proposing Algal Chloroplast as the New Status Quo for Biopharmaceutical Peptide Production. As the climate crisis intensifies and the cost of living rises, the demand for a circular economy has never been greater. Project Chloronova leverages microalgae as a scalable carbon-sequestering organism by partnering with major industrial polluters in our hometown of Hamilton, Ontario to reduce carbon dioxide emissions while producing high-value biomolecules. Unlike bacteria, microalgae offer the unique ability to perform post-translational modifications, make multiple heterologous proteins and withstand antimicrobial mechanisms. Inspired by our human practices research, Chloronova engineers microalgae to produce antimicrobial peptides (AMPs), thus addressing the alarming rise of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) and the urgent need for sustainable bioproduction. Using PEG-mediated transformation in a cell-wall deficient strain of Chlamydomonas reinhardtii (cw15+), we are able to introduce our plasmid into the chloroplast DNA of the microalgae. By optimizing AMP production within C. reinhardtii, we are creating a scalable, modular biofactory. It’s a new day, and algae is here to stay.

title: Thermoguard: A Novel Treatment for Skin and Soft Tissue Infections(SSTIs)
text: Thermoguard: A Novel Treatment for Skin and Soft Tissue Infections(SSTIs). Skin and Soft Tissue Infections (SSTIs) encompass a broad spectrum of infectious conditions that affect the skin and underlying soft tissues. Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) accounts for over 50% of SSTI cases. In the United States, SSTIs affect more than 14 million outpatients annually, with 900,000 requiring hospitalizations. The rise of antimicrobial resistance threatens the efficacy of antibiotics used to treat SSTIs, prompting the search for alternatives. Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs), especially those produced by thermophilic bacteria, have gained attention as potential solutions. In our project, we utilized bioinformatics tools to identify novel AMP genes in the genome of the thermophilic bacteria Brevibacillus borstelensis AK1, a thermophilic bacteria isolated from a hot spring in Saudi Arabia. We then designed a plasmid to contain these AMP genes and cloned them into Escherichia coli for heterologous expression, aiming to develop a novel AMP-based treatment for SSTIs in the face of rising antibiotic resistance.

title: CaraCOS: To produce versatile COS from waste carapace with the application of dual-enzyme synergistic catalysis
text: CaraCOS: To produce versatile COS from waste carapace with the application of dual-enzyme synergistic catalysis. The accumulation of shrimp and crab carapaces waste poses serious environmental hazards. Despite the potential to convert these chitin-rich materials into high-value chitooligosaccharides (COS), the scarcity and high cost of recycling technologies mean that these carapaces are often overlooked. By selecting from Bacillus species and site-directed mutating, we will obtain high-activity chitin deacetylases (CDA) and chitosanases (CsnB) and improve the enzymatic method to produce COS from chitin, thereby enhancing the recycling and utilization of waste carapaces.

title: Biosynthesis of Interleukin-18-Binding-Protein for the Treatment of Inflammatory Bowel Disease
text: Biosynthesis of Interleukin-18-Binding-Protein for the Treatment of Inflammatory Bowel Disease. Inflammatory Bowel Disease (IBD) is a group of autoimmune diseases that involves the inflammation of the digestive tract. It is currently becoming much more prevalent in Asia due to rapid urbanization and the adoption of Western dietary habits. IBD has a lower onset age than most other chronic diseases. However, there is no effective treatment for IBD. In this context, we utilized genetic engineering techniques to produce a macromolecular drug, Interleukin-18-binding-protein (IL-18BP) to treat IBD. In our project, human IL-18BPa and IL-18BPc genes were modified with SUMO to improve the protein stability, Fc to achieve potential targeted drug delivery, and His tag for purification. Our research results revealed the protein's ability to successfully lower IFN-gamma levels (a sign of inflammation), demonstrating its anti-inflammatory effect and potential application in IBD treatment.

title: Engineered Probiotic for Targeted Tumor Therapy
text: Engineered Probiotic for Targeted Tumor Therapy. Tumors pose multifaceted harm, including life-threatening risks, organ damage, complications, psychological impact, and reduced quality of life. Genetically engineered bacteria have emerged as a promising strategy for disease diagnosis and treatment. These engineered bacteria have been used to monitor cancer liver metastases, liver dysfunction, and various gastrointestinal disorders, such as inflammation and infection. Certain bacteria, like Salmonella and Escherichia coli Nissle (EcN), can selectively colonize tumors due to their ability to infiltrate the hypoxic cores of immune-deficient tumors. In this study, we utilized a lactic acid-responsive promoter to control the expression of anti-PD-L1 antibody or azurin killer protein. EcN was engineered as a tumor-specific drug delivery system to target tumors and locally release drugs, thereby inhibiting tumor growth and reducing both drug dosage and cost. This approach could provide new insights and strategies for cancer treatment.

title: Colorfold
text: Colorfold. Our project addresses environmental and health concerns associated with synthetic dyes by exploring biological alternatives. We aim to reduce the toxic chemicals used in dye production by focusing on two objectives: the discovery of new biological pigments from environmental microorganisms, and the mutation of new colours in existing chromoproteins for large-scale production. Specifically, we are targeting AmilCP to make new colours more suitable for industrial use. Using size exclusion chromatography, SDS-PAGE semi-native analysis and bioinformatics, we aim to identify novel chromoproteins using AI tools for protein engineering. Synthetic dyes, widely used in textiles and other industries, are major pollutants, especially in water systems. Biological pigments offer a sustainable alternative. Inspired by previous research into microbial pigments, our project aims to contribute to a greener future by providing scalable and environmentally friendly solutions to current dyeing practices.

title: Pichia Pastoris Production Plant for Healthy Sugar SubstituteD-Psicose
text: Pichia Pastoris Production Plant for Healthy Sugar SubstituteD-Psicose. Traditional sweeteners have become a research focus due to issues such as high calorie content and high blood sugar levels .D-Psicose,as an emerging low calorie sweetener, combines good sweetness with health benefits such as reducing fat and lowering blood sugar. Due to its scarcity in nature, there are two synthetic methods: chemical synthesis, which pollutes the environment, and biological synthesis, which is highly favored for its environmental friendliness and efficiency. However, the existing enzyme species of the key enzyme in the biosynthesis of D-Psicose, 3-isomerase, have poor thermal stability and low expression.In this study, we selected the coding genes of D-psicose 3-epimerase from different sources, induced the expression and purification of the target protein in Pichia pastoris, and detected its enzymatic properties to screen D-psicose 3-epimerase with good thermal stability.

title: A New Fungal Probe: Innovation of a rapid eco-friendly, and visually fungal-detecting approach
text: A New Fungal Probe: Innovation of a rapid eco-friendly, and visually fungal-detecting approach. As a widely distributed eukaryotic microorganism found in nature, some fungi have posed significant threats to food safety and human health through infections. Current fungal detection methods, like DNA isolation and gram staining microscopy, require specialized equipment, experimental conditions, and high costs. Lacking direct visualization capabilities also limits their broad use in food safety inspection and clinical diagnosis. Moreover, the accuracy of microscopy can be affected by difficulties in differentiating various fungi from background noise. To address these issues, we designed a fungi-detecting probe utilizing carbohydrate-binding modules (CBMs) for their special affinity to fungal cell wall polysaccharides and chitin. By combining CBMs with fluorescent proteins, this probe enables rapid, eco-friendly, and visual in situ detection of fungal contamination in samples from different scenarios.

title: Engineering and Development of Collagen-based Rotavirus Subunit Vaccines
text: Engineering and Development of Collagen-based Rotavirus Subunit Vaccines. Rotaviruses are the most common causative agents of severe gastroenteritis in children under five years of age. Vaccination is the most effective measure to prevent Rotavirus infection. It was previously shown that the outer capsid viral protein (VP4) is an essential target for developing a recombinant rotavirus vaccine as it mediates the attachment and penetration of rotavirus. However, the current live rotavirus vaccines show reduced effectiveness. Here, we focus on crafting a recombinant rotavirus vaccine with improved efficacy and safety. The coexpression of a human collagen type Ⅲ with VP4 in Escherichia coli was employed to generate oligomerization of recombinant rotavirus vaccines. Further, a stable hydroxyproline-free ABC heterotrimeric collagen mimetic system was used to produce a polyvalent rotavirus vaccine. Importantly, these newly designed vaccines utilize non-infectious virus-like particles with enhanced immunogenicity and protection, which could be considered viable candidates for further development to become a parenterally administered rotavirus vaccine.

title: Golden solutions: the power of AuNPs@PBP in the detection & sterilization of foodborne bacteria
text: Golden solutions: the power of AuNPs@PBP in the detection & sterilization of foodborne bacteria. Nowadays, food safety has not been comprehensively guaranteed mainly due to the severe health risks foodborne bacteria bring. However, current bacterial detection methods are time-consuming and less accessible. Our team believes that these limitations can be improved by developing a more efficient and effective product by coupling gold nanoparticles that have useful physical properties, with Phage-derived bacterial-binding protein (PBP). This biosensor rapidly binds to three specific bacteria (Escherichia coli, Salmonella, Staphylococcus aureus) within thirty minutes, analyzes their concentrations via RGB values on a smartphone app, and sterilizes bacteria using near-infrared (NIR). Additionally, it achieves efficient antibacterial effects under 808 nm light irradiation for 10 minutes. This study is significant for the detection and elimination of foodborne pathogens for both synthetic biology development and practical influences in the food industry. Furthermore, we will investigate the target market to ensure a pragmatic and applicable product is available to our potential consumers.

title: Early screening products for Parkinson’s disease
text: Early screening products for Parkinson’s disease. Parkinson’s disease (PD) is one of the most common neurodegenerative diseases. Early screening of the disease is a key measure to prevent the occurrence and development of the disease. NF-L is a universal marker of nerve damage and is elevated in a variety of neurodegenerative diseases, including PD. In the early stages of PD, elevated NF-L levels can be detected. Using α-synuclein, Aβ42, and NF-L as biomarkers simultaneously can improve the sensitivity and specificity of PD diagnosis. Each marker provides a different pathological perspective, making the comprehensive analysis more comprehensive. This study intends to obtain PD-specific markers α-syn, Aβ42, and NF-L through genetic engineering, and use ELISA to verify the accuracy of the obtained proteins, which can lay a good foundation for the acquisition of specific antibodies and the construction of early screening kits in the future.

title: CALIMOD - GIX
text: CALIMOD - GIX. Drug addiction is a chronic condition characterized by compulsive drug seeking and use despite negative consequences. Extensive research shows that surges of dopamine during pleasurable activities affect the brain's reward circuits. G9a, an under-researched gene, regulates dopamine production and release, influencing how the brain responds to addictive substances. Elevated levels of EHMT2 (the coding gene for G9a) are observed in addiction, and our research aims to reduce these levels using RNAi technology, specifically small-interfering RNA. Through a three-component system involving the construction of plasmids altered for overproduction of our gene to be expanded in further research on addiction, siRNA technology tests for optimal concentration and conditions, and a concept model of lipid-nanoparticles as a delivery method, we hope to contribute to the possibility of creating an accessible therapeutic to solve this problem.

title: Targeted intracellular delivery of LshCas13a using  bacterial DTA toxin-based platforms into targeted non-synthetic HIV-1 strains
text: Targeted intracellular delivery of LshCas13a using  bacterial DTA toxin-based platforms into targeted non-synthetic HIV-1 strains. Targeted delivery of therapeutic proteins toward latent HIV-infected cells remains a major challenge in eradicating HIV. Leading therapies block entry via envelope proteins or coreceptors, as well as reverse transcription. We developed a protein-based delivery system using a detoxified single-chain diphtheria toxin (DTA) as a translocation carrier across the cell membrane. This system delivers large protein cargoes, such as Cas13a, into cells in a receptor-dependent manner. A GP120 gene fragment was added to the fusion protein to act as the ligand for CD4+ T-helper cell receptors. These systems remain under development and low expression of Cas13a-DTA in E. coli (10-beta, Rosetta, and W3110 strains) poses challenges in extraction. Our research complements gene editing and external protein therapies to evaluate HIV cleavage in mimic CD4 receptor cells (HEK293). Quantifications of ssRNA cleavage via RT-qPCR will be presented, suggesting how effectively this treatment could extend to pharmaceutical applications.

title: Yeast Medics：Hydrogel Wound Dressing Infused with Engineered Yeast's Healing Arsenal for Diabetic Wound Regeneration
text: Yeast Medics：Hydrogel Wound Dressing Infused with Engineered Yeast's Healing Arsenal for Diabetic Wound Regeneration. Globally, nearly 588 million people live with diabetes, and up to 25% of them suffer from chronic, non-healing wounds, facing risks of infection, gangrene, and even amputation. Current conventional therapies are ineffective and cumbersome, exacerbating patient suffering, while advanced treatments remain inaccessible due to high costs, limited functionality, or lack of dynamic regulation. To address this, we introduce “Yeast Medics”—an innovative injectable dressing based on engineered Yarrowia lipolytica and L-DOPA-modified thermosensitive chitosan. This system dynamically senses wound status, displays antimicrobial peptides (Pexiganan) on the yeast surface, and programmatically releases both anti-inflammatory (IL-4) and pro-angiogenic (VEGF) factors. It synergistically addresses the three major challenges of infection, inflammation, and regeneration on a single platform, providing diabetic patients with an integrated, self-driven, low-burden healing solution.

title: Adipocyte for Breast Cancer Surveillance(ABCS)
text: Adipocyte for Breast Cancer Surveillance(ABCS). Adipocytes can be transformed into cancer-associated adipocytes (CAAs) by cytokines from cancer cells. As CAAs demonstrate distinct gene expression pattern, we aimed to engineer adipocytes that could report such pattern. Systematic analysis revealed that the optimal combination to identify CAAs is PLOD2 and LIF, which could be induced by PAI-1 and CXCL8 respectively. We designed a RADAR sensor that targets the transcripts of PLOD2 and LIF simultaneously and delivered this sensor into differentiated adipocytes. These engineered adipocytes responded to the combined stimulation of PAI-1 and CXCL8 only. Most importantly, these engineered adipocytes responded to the treatment of the conditioned medium from breast cancer cells, revealing the potential of these adipocytes to respond to actual cancer microenvironment. We chose Gaussia luciferase (Gluc), an enzyme to generate luminescence, as output reporter. As Gluc could be secreted into urine, it offers a convenient way to report the results of in vivo cancer monitoring.

title: SILK:Stability-Integrated Industrialization Leveraging Key plasmids
text: SILK:Stability-Integrated Industrialization Leveraging Key plasmids. The SILK project (Stability-Integrated Industrialization Leveraging Key plasmids) addresses the critical challenge of environmental sensitivity in industrial fermentation by harnessing Xinjiang’s extremophilic microbial resources. Xinjiang's diverse environment has fostered highly tolerant bacterial communities, whose natural plasmids encode evolutionarily shaped stress-resistance mechanisms. By isolating and sequencing these plasmids, our team identifies functional gene elements—such as tolerance to extreme pH levels—to construct standardized expression modules for industrial strains. Integrating nature's evolutionary solutions into bioreactor frameworks, the SILK project aims to enhance fermentation stability, reduce energy consumption for environmental control, and expand the synthetic biology toolkit for extreme environments—transforming Xinjiang's “microbial silk” into industrial resilience.

title: InkSight
text: InkSight. Tattoos have long served as markers of identity and belonging. InkSight repurposes this historical medium for modern medicine as a platform comprising engineered mammalian cells encapsulated in a hydrogel matrix for intradermal delivery as a tattoo. This system enables the real-time, equipment-free detection of circulating biomarkers through direct interrogation of the interstitial fluid. The engineered cells express a Modular Extracellular Sensor Architecture (MESA) for target recognition, which triggers one of three engineered contrast-change mechanisms: expression, assembly, or agglomeration. This response is driven by synthetic melanin-producing compartments, specifically encapsulin nanocages that house tyrosinase to enable localized and safe melanin production, resulting in a visible shift in tattoo contrast. InkSight constitutes, to our knowledge, the first paradigm for a continuous, cell-based tattoo biosensor with a visible output, establishing a foundational platform for decentralized diagnostics and personalized medicine.

title: An Inhalable Probiotic Platform for RNA-Mediated Silencing for Asthma Management
text: An Inhalable Probiotic Platform for RNA-Mediated Silencing for Asthma Management. Asthma is a very common respiratory disease, its severe form is often characterized by uncontrolled or corticosteroid-resistant inflammation. To overcome this, we developed PRESS, a modular therapeutic platform combining a probiotic delivery system (Lactobacillus plantarum) with an siRNA-based silencing tool (CO-BERA) targeting the inflammatory alarmin TSLP mRNA. Our engineered L. plantarum senses airway inflammation through dual inputs (Hydrogen peroxide and acidic pH) and, upon activation, synthesizes CO-BERA to silence TSLP and suppress downstream inflammatory pathways. For efficient administration, we designed a dry-powder inhalation system, optimized by computational fluid dynamics and validated for aerosol behavior and bacterial viability. PRESS adapted multi-layered biosafety measures, including a toxin–antitoxin kill switch to ensure containment. Reinforced by modeling-guided design and educational outreach with achieving eight UN SDGs. PRESS showcasing how engineered probiotics can function as living inhalable therapeutics, providing a safe, sustainable, and targeted solution for asthma and other inflammatory lung diseases.

title: Slupeer: Removal of Cadmium From Sludge
text: Slupeer: Removal of Cadmium From Sludge. Cadmium is a severe heavy metal pollutant in several regions. Its effect as a pollutant threatens food safety, notably causing 14-17% of global cropland to be affected. Among sources of cadmium pollution, sludge is particularly detrimental with exacerbated consequences from downstream damage to human health and ecosystems. Within the sludge, there only exists trace yet still harmful concentrations of sludge, causing general heavy metal remediation methods to be ineffective against it. Simultaneously, it is the most significant ecological risk amongst heavy metals. Our team targets sludge and removes the pollutant cadmium by engineering Pseudomonas putida to express metallothioneins on its surface. Our team has introduced this metallothionein to the iGEM Registry and characterized it through Wet Lab Data and Dry Lab modeling. Supported by extensive Human Practices work, our team hopes to demonstrate the potential of our work and it as a promising and sustainable heavy metal bioremediation method.

title: Treating End-Stage Liver Disease via Synergistic Co-delivery of miRNA-Engineered Exosomes
text: Treating End-Stage Liver Disease via Synergistic Co-delivery of miRNA-Engineered Exosomes. Human umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cell (hUC-MSC)-derived exosomes can ameliorate liver disease via their diverse effector cargo. While individual miRNAs like miR-455-3p and miR-148a-5p are known anti-fibrotic agents, their therapeutic synergy is uninvestigated. This study co-delivers two distinct exosome populations, each artificially supplemented with one of these miRNAs, to assess their combined efficacy.

title: Glycosy-N-ation: Developement of microbial plataforms for the production of recombinant glycoproteins
text: Glycosy-N-ation: Developement of microbial plataforms for the production of recombinant glycoproteins. N-glycosylation, the attachment of glycans to asparagine residues, is a critical post-translational modification that influences protein folding, stability, signaling, and activity. Over half of human proteins are glycosylated, yet current therapeutic glycoprotein production depends on eukaryotic hosts, as common models such as Saccharomyces cerevisiae and Escherichia coli are unsuitable. E. coli lacks an N-glycosylation pathway, leading to insoluble proteins, while S. cerevisiae produces hypermannose glycans that are immunogenic in humans. To overcome these limitations, we are engineering optimized microbial platforms for glycoprotein synthesis. In yeast, glycan chain extension is disrupted to generate simpler structures, and in E. coli, a de novo glycosylation system is reconstructed using modular Golden Gate-compatible parts. Both systems aim to produce the universal precursor Man₃GlcNAc₂. We developed 24 yeast mutants to evaluate growth, fitness, morphology, protein production, and glycan transfer, and incorporated archaeal oligosaccharyltransferases into E.coli to explore their ability to transfer glycans to human-like sequons.

title: CRUSTA: Circular Reutilization of Untappable Seafood-shell: Transfomation into Antimicrobial-preservatives
text: CRUSTA: Circular Reutilization of Untappable Seafood-shell: Transfomation into Antimicrobial-preservatives. In our CRUSTA project, we designed and developed an innovative COS-based bio-preservation technology using principles of synthetic biology. This technology provides a green and efficient alternative to traditional chemical preservatives in the food industry. In our project, we achieved chitosan degradation via a secretion system, enhancing the antibacterial performance of the degradation products by 7.96-fold compared to the wild-type. This project not only has the potential to propel technological innovation and catalyze industrial advancement in food preservation but also aims to introduce advanced concepts of synthetic biology and eco-friendly preservation. These initiatives are expected to improve preservation efficiency, elevate food safety standards, and enhance environmental sustainability, thus bolstering market competitiveness and fostering the sustainable growth of the green food industry and the circular economy.

title: Synbio-MuralShield——Using synthetic biology to restore microbial damage to murals
text: Synbio-MuralShield——Using synthetic biology to restore microbial damage to murals. As an ancient art form, murals possess significant historical and artistic value. However, factors such as climate change and human activities frequently lead to microbial outbreaks on mural surfaces, resulting in issues such as discoloration of mineral pigments, powdering and flaking of painted layers, and organic staining, which severely threaten their preservation. We have developed a microbial platform capable of producing antimicrobial peptides to inhibit the growth of fungi and bacteria, as well as generating enzymes to degrade organic pigments including melanin and carotenoids. This platform utilizes a pH-inducible switch to transcribe different products under varying pH conditions and incorporates a toggle-switch-based containment mechanism to ensure that our engineered bacteria survive only under specific conditions, thereby preventing environmental release.

title: Engineered bacteria for PFAS degradation and dectection
text: Engineered bacteria for PFAS degradation and dectection. Forever chemicals, or PFAS, are synthetic compounds composed of carbon–fluorine bonds that are nearly impossible to break down. First produced in the 1940s for their exceptional stability and resistance, they are now ubiquitous—in cookware, textiles, and firefighting foams—leading to their accumulation in the environment and human bodies. Long-term exposure has been linked to cancer, hormonal disruption, and immune dysfunction. Yet, no scalable, low-energy solutions currently exist for PFAS degradation. FluoroBreaker aims to address this challenge through two complementary strategies targeting PFOA and TFA. First, we used an AI-assisted bioinformatics docking approach to identify key mutations in a dehalogenase enzyme to enhance TFA degradation. Second, we engineered reporter bacteria carrying a promoter responsive to PFOA, enabling fast, user-friendly detection of PFAS in water. Together, these innovations pave the way for a sustainable, biotechnology-driven response to the PFAS pollution crisis.

title: DOCTOR：Diagnostic Optimization & Chemical Treatment Of Rhinosinusitis
text: DOCTOR：Diagnostic Optimization & Chemical Treatment Of Rhinosinusitis. Chronic rhinosinusitis (CRS) is a widespread yet underestimated disease that causes severe discomfort and lacks effective clinical solutions. To address challenges in early diagnosis and precise treatment, we focused on Granzyme K (GZMK), a key enzyme driving CRS progression. Centered on this target, we established an integrated diagnostic–therapeutic framework. A colloidal-gold rapid test strip enables early and accessible detection, while small-molecule inhibitors achieve precise enzymatic inhibition and inflammation control. In parallel, we developed two supporting technology platforms: Prometheus, for de novo protein design, and Nexus, for high-throughput affinity measurement. They enable efficient design and validation of high-affinity protein binders, contributing more powerful research tools to the field of synthetic biology.

title: CASPER — A Synthetic Platform to Combat Antimicrobial Resistance
text: CASPER — A Synthetic Platform to Combat Antimicrobial Resistance. Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a silent pandemic claiming millions of lives each year as more pathogens evade existing treatments. CASPER (cell-based antimicrobial screening and programmable elimination response) offers an integrated platform that unites diagnostics and therapeutics into a single, accessible system. The diagnostic module overcomes limitations of PCR and lateral flow assays by using a two-step reaction that screens for bacterial presence and produces a clear color change as a visible output. This enables rapid, broad-range, and equipment-free detection suitable for low-resource settings. The therapeutic module introduces programmable mini cells and extracellular vesicles as DNA delivery shuttles capable of selectively recognizing bacterial targets and triggering cell death from within. By combining detection and response, CASPER provides a scalable and affordable solution to antimicrobial resistance with the potential to transform infection control and save millions of lives worldwide.

title: Cohera: A New Foundation For Engineered Multicellularity
text: Cohera: A New Foundation For Engineered Multicellularity. One of nature’s greatest feats is multicellularity—joining together single cells into a whole that is greater than the sum of its parts. Cohera is a complete toolkit for multicellular engineering, allowing synthetic biologists to access the full potential of cell-cell adhesion. Our system enables the creation of microbial networks that can be formed and dissolved on command using a collection of membrane-displayed proteins. Our Model, CoheraTune, expands the range of environments in which our tool operates by strengthening the core of our project at the molecular level. At the macroscopic level, bioengineers can leverage Cohera to solve problems in diverse fields. To facilitate the use of our system as a foundational tool, we developed human-centred roadmaps for applications spanning all iGEM plazas. Cohera streamlines the process of engineering cell-cell adhesion, unlocking endless possibilities.

title: Pepcitrus: Peptides in defense of Citrus
text: Pepcitrus: Peptides in defense of Citrus. Orange production faces severe losses caused by Greening, Green Mold and Sour Rot, threatening food security and vitamin C availability. Especially in Brazil, leader of orange juice and fruit production, this directly affects livelihoods. To tackle this challenge, we focused on CTX, an antimicrobial peptide from Brazilian Cerrado biodiversity, and engineered three different hosts: E. coli, S. cerevisiae, and A. oryzae to optimize its production through coupling-strategies. To guide CTX application, we developed a mathematical model simulating Greening progression in the phloem and designed Sniffer, a hardware device combining an electronic nose and machine learning for rapid field diagnosis. Performing economic analysis to assess industrial scalability of approaches we demonstrated cost-effectiveness through solid-state fermentation using orange peels residues. Thus, Pepcitrus bridges laboratory innovation and real-world application, incorporating different perspectives from farmers, industry, and society to save oranges.

title: DeathCapTrap: a modular nanobody-based antidote against α-amanitin
text: DeathCapTrap: a modular nanobody-based antidote against α-amanitin. 90% of mushroom poisonings are caused by α-amanitin, one of the deadliest mushroom toxins which can be found in the death cap mushroom. Just half a mushroom can be fatal, as the toxin inhibits RNA Polymerase II, blocking protein production and causing severe organ damage, especially to the liver and kidneys. Although treatments exist, there is no specific antidote yet. Our iGEM project, DeathCapTrap, aims to develop a modular nanobody-based antidote to neutralize α-amanitin in the bloodstream and protect liver cells. In the WetLab, we established a pipeline to produce a nuclear-targeted nanobody in E. coli. We also explored lipid nanoparticles for delivery and designed a testing protocol with liver cell models. In the DryLab, AI tools helped us design toxin-binding proteins. Our goal is to create a life-saving therapy and a versatile platform to fight intracellular toxins, while raising awareness of the dangers of mushroom poisoning.

title: Gut Health Guardian: Engineered Probiotics for the Treatment of Perioperative Intestinal Microecological Dysbiosis
text: Gut Health Guardian: Engineered Probiotics for the Treatment of Perioperative Intestinal Microecological Dysbiosis. This project aims to develop an intelligent engineered bacterium for the precise treatment of perioperative gut microbiota dysbiosis. Using the safe Lactobacillus casei as the chassis, we have integrated a multifunctional genetic circuit. First, by introducing the accA and OLE1 genes, the engineered bacterium can synthesize and release oleic acid—beneficial for gut barrier repair—under the specific regulation of the bile salt-responsive promoter P16090. Simultaneously, the bacterium expresses the antimicrobial peptide defensin DEFB4A to precisely suppress opportunistic pathogens. To ensure biosafety, we designed a bile salt-responsive Hok/Sok toxin-antitoxin "kill switch" system, controlled by the same P16090 promoter. This mechanism ensures that the engineered bacterium only colonizes the gut; any leakage into the external environment triggers its automatic clearance. Together, this living therapeutic platform is equipped with functions for barrier repair, pathogen suppression, and self-regulation, setting a new standard for targeted, safe, and intelligent interventions.

title: Hyaluronext
text: Hyaluronext. Hyaluronic acid (HA) is a biomolecule widely utilized in healthcare and cosmetic applications. Traditionally, HA is extracted from animal or bacterial sources. Research has examined the potential of microbial production using non-pathogenic bacteria. These methods could be a promising ethical and scalable alternative. Given current demand, HA yields remain insufficient.  We aim to maximize production efficiency through Multiplex Automated Genome Engineering (MAGE) and specialized E. coli. MAGE enables rapid, high-throughput modification of multiple genomic sites simultaneously, facilitating metabolic pathway optimization and synthetic biology applications. However, MAGE is hindered by high cost, complexity, and limited versatility of existing hardware. Our group is developing the Open-Source Automated Genome Engineering (O-SAGE) platform, leveraging affordable, commercially available components and open-source parts. The goal is to engineer E. coli capable of efficient HA production using O-SAGE, providing a safe, ethical, and scalable source of HA while also democratizing access to advanced genome engineering technologies.

title: BiOilRo: Sustainable Biosynthesis of Ginsenoside Ro for Valorization of Low-Value Carbon Sources in Waste Oil
text: BiOilRo: Sustainable Biosynthesis of Ginsenoside Ro for Valorization of Low-Value Carbon Sources in Waste Oil. Ginsenoside Ro is one of the rarest and most valuable bioactive compounds in ginseng, celebrated for its potent antioxidant properties and multi-target therapeutic potential. However, its natural abundance is extremely low, and traditional extraction methods are both costly and environmentally unsustainable. To address this challenge, we engineered a recombinant Saccharomyces cerevisiae system capable of converting waste oil–derived carbon sources, such as glycerol and fatty acids, into Ro through an optimized three-step biosynthetic pathway. By integrating metabolic engineering, enzyme evolution, and modeling-guided optimization, we achieved a substantial enhancement in Ro yield while reducing resource consumption and environmental footprint. This platform exemplifies the principles of a circular bioeconomy, transforming industrial waste into high-value pharmaceuticals. Combining strong environmental benefits with significant economic potential, our work establishes a scalable, sustainable model for advancing green manufacturing and the future of synthetic biology–based healthcare.

title: POLYGONE: Development of marine high-efficiency polyester-degrading enzyme
text: POLYGONE: Development of marine high-efficiency polyester-degrading enzyme. Polyester plastics (PET/PBAT/PLA) persist in marine environments and form harmful microplastics. To tackle source-level persistence and end-of-pipe remediation we combined marine-enzyme discovery, computational protein redesign and AI-driven mutation design, inorganic CaCO₃–SiO₂ immobilization compatible with melt processing, and an E. coli dual-anchor surface-display (adhesion + SpyTag/SpyCatcher-tethered hydrolase). A marine hydrolase (“2013”) was mined, characterized and redesigned to a soluble active variant (SEQ4); immobilization conferred thermal robustness with ≈40% activity retained after brief high-temperature treatment, supporting processing compatibility. Enzyme-containing films exhibited accelerated surface erosion in 28-day real-seawater assays; the dual-anchor strain enhanced local TPA release versus controls; and a rapid hydroxylation–Fenton fluorescence assay enabled sensitive TPA quantification. Future work will optimize kinetics for high-crystallinity PET, scale immobilization/compounding to pilot, integrate a genetically encoded TPA biosensor, and assess environmental fate, safety and regulatory pathways.

title: Tuneable Dream Drive
text: Tuneable Dream Drive. Tuneable Dream Drive: To address sleep disorders caused by circadian rhythm disruption during space missions, the JLU-CP team engineered a multi-layer regulatory melatonin synthesis system using Escherichia coli Nissle 1917 (EcN) as a chassis. This system integrates a red-light-controlled genetic circuit with the serine recombinase Bxb1, enabling reversible promoter inversion to switch between serotonin production and melatonin biosynthesis. A pharmacokinetic (PK) model optimized dosage under simulated microgravity, while deep-learning-driven enzyme engineering enhanced HsAANAT catalytic efficiency. We then built an expression model to predict melatonin yield under light conditions for controllable production. For biosafety, the design includes a hypoxia-activated toxin–antitoxin module and tryptophan-auxotrophic safeguard. Additionally, we developed iTutor, the most inclusive-iGEM LLM trained on iGEM Wiki, PubMed, and arXiv data, provides real-time computational and experimental guidance. This engineered probiotic functions as a gut-colonizing “biological clock calibrator,” enabling precise, red-light-induced melatonin release to support astronauts’ circadian health during spaceflight.

title: NomNomNylon: towards a sustainable future for nylon waste
text: NomNomNylon: towards a sustainable future for nylon waste. Fast fashion has accelerated the accumulation of synthetic textile waste, with nylon being among the least recycled fractions. Landfilling and incineration are the current disposal methods, producing microplastics and emitting greenhouse gases. NomNomNylon proposes a bio-upcycling strategy that couples enzymatic pretreatment with microbial valorisation. To enhance depolymerization, we developed a protein engineering pipeline to increase thermostability and activity while exploring nature’s enzymatic diversity through sequence mining. These variants and homologues were tested in vitro using a cell-free assay on raw nylon. We employed a bioengineered Pseudomonas putida strain to metabolise nylon-derived oligomers and channel carbon flux toward indigoidine, a sustainable alternative to petrochemical indigo. Beyond lab work, we integrated feedback from experts, policymakers, and NGOs, and raised awareness among the public and youth through educational initiatives. We have shown that nylon waste can serve as a valuable feedstock for high-value products, contributing to a greener textile future.

title: Squoilene
text: Squoilene. Squoilene tackles waste oil (WO) pollution and the high cost of squalene production by integrating experimental work, model and hardware into a cohesive synthetic biology project, engineering Yarrowia lipolytica into an efficient cellular refinery.Through human practice and interdisciplinary communication, we refined design and promoted implementation. We established TriScale, a hierarchical in silico pipeline integrating signal peptide–linker–based peroxisomal targeting design, rational tHMGR enzyme engineering, and system-level growth modeling for predictive and knowledge-guided prototyping. Building on this framework, we developed a compartmentalized metabolism strategy, relocating the entire MVA pathway into peroxisomes to enhance flux and isolate toxic intermediates. To bridge lab design with application, we created the low-cost, automated Integrated Fermentation & Processing System (iFPS), streamlining production from inoculation to crude lysate collection. Our integrated approach demonstrates a sustainable, economically viable route to convert pollutants into valuable cosmetic ingredients，while contributing innovations in culture analysis and fermentation processing.

title: "AMIGO": CRISPR-Cas9-Mediated Metabolic Engineering of Aureobasidium melanogenum for Glucose Synthesis from Methanol
text: "AMIGO": CRISPR-Cas9-Mediated Metabolic Engineering of Aureobasidium melanogenum for Glucose Synthesis from Methanol. In response to growing climate concerns, biological CO2 capture and utilization technologies have attracted significant attention. Beyond direct CO2 fixation, the biological assimilation of the liquid one-carbon compounds, such as methanol, offers a promising alternative route for converting CO2 into value-added products. Aureobasidium melanogenum, a kind of poly-extremotolerant yeast-like fungus, exhibits remarkable potential for producing diverse bioproducts. Here, we established a CRISPR‑Cas9 gene‑editing system for A. melanogenum and elucidated the mechanisms underlying its methanol metabolism. By reprogramming key metabolic pathways, we constructed an engineered strain capable of synthesizing glucose from methanol. Furthermore, to optimize the cultivation of A. melanogenum, we developed a real-time methanol monitoring and automatic feeding device based on a gas-liquid exchange model, enabling convenient and accurate methanol concentration measurement. This study provides a foundational framework for leveraging A. melanogenumin the bioconversion of C1 compounds toward chemical production, highlighting its potential for sustainable carbon utilization.

title: PHAntom: PHA Novel Tools for Off-world Manufacturing
text: PHAntom: PHA Novel Tools for Off-world Manufacturing. Since the Mariner 4 flyby, Mars has inspired interplanetary exploration, but high payload costs limit human settlement. Our team proposes PHAntom, a synthetic biology system using engineered E. coli to convert Martian CO₂ into bioplastics and metabolites. Our two-strain E. coli system converts CO₂ into PHBV via an acetate intermediate. Strain 1 autotrophically fixes CO₂ and secretes acetate using the pta–ackA pathway. Strain 2, aided by tdcB/tdcE for propionyl-CoA supply and tesB/yciA to balance 3HB/3HV monomers, converts acetate into PHBV. A bicarbonate-responsive cAMP–CRP mechanism enhances transcription under high HCO₃⁻, while CRISPRi knockdown of gltA diverts acetyl-CoA from the TCA cycle, optimizing acetate production and PHBV yield. Team PHAntom has built a clinostat to simulate non-Earth gravity conditions and an extrusion system to convert PHBV granules into printable filaments. PHAntom enables sustainable off-world biomaterial production through integrated carbon capture, adaptive metabolism, and on-site manufacturing

title: HydroGuard
text: HydroGuard. Catheter associated urinary tract infections (CAUTIs) are the most common hospital infection, disproportionately affecting vulnerable populations such as those in long-term care homes or the critically ill. While the standard treatments for these infections rely primarily on antibiotics, the increasing prevalence of antimicrobial resistant infections demands for an alternative solution. To combat this issue, we have developed HydroGuard, a biocompatible, infection-responsive hydrogel with controlled phage release. Our hydrogel, made up of gelatin methacryloyl, degrades in the presence of gelatinase (gelE), a protein naturally produced by E.faecalis during infection. The degradation of gelatin in the hydrogel releases the embedded phage cocktail, which targets and eradicates the biofilm. Using a combined wet-lab and computational approach, our work demonstrates the viability of this solution by incorporating the gelE gene into E.coli for lab-safe proof of concept solution.

title: Integrative Melatonin and Bioengineered Wax-Coating System for Lychee Preservation
text: Integrative Melatonin and Bioengineered Wax-Coating System for Lychee Preservation. Lychee deteriorates rapidly after harvest due to high respiration, browning, and fungal decay. Current preservation methods rely on costly cold chains and chemical additives. Our project proposes a sustainable synthetic biology solution integrating melatonin biosynthesis and bioengineered wax coating. Engineered Bacillus subtilis produces melatonin to reduce respiration, delay browning, and enhance lychee immunity. Meanwhile, a LacI–lactose regulatory system promotes fatty acid accumulation, enabling the formation of a protective wax layer that retains moisture and prevents microbial invasion. Complemented by AI-assisted dry-lab tools—BactaGenome for bacterial genome analysis, SynbioMCP for intuitive biological design, and a drone-based spraying system for large-scale application—our approach provides an eco-friendly and intelligent lychee preservation platform that extends shelf life and reduces postharvest waste.

title: SurFactory: A Sustainable Pulmonary Surfactant Innovation
text: SurFactory: A Sustainable Pulmonary Surfactant Innovation. Premature newborns often face respiratory distress due to underdeveloped lungs, requiring pulmonary surfactant for survival. Current treatments are costly, rely on animal-derived sources, and remain inaccesible to many healthcare systems wolrdwide. Our project uses synthetic biology and biomanufacturing to create an alternative surfactant that is animal-free, affordable, and scalable. By engineering microorganisms to produce key surfactant proteins, we aim to deliver a sustainable solution that bridges health inequities and reduces dependence on traditional animal-derived products. This approach not only addresses a pressing medical challenge but also introduces an ethical and environmentally responsible production pipeline. Through our work, we envision a future where every premature infant, regardless of geography or economic status, can access life-saving pulmonary surfactant demonstrating how synthetic biology can transform global health challenges into opportunities for innovation, sustainability, and equity.

title: Optogenetic Activation System for Intelligent Surfactin expression（OASIS）
text: Optogenetic Activation System for Intelligent Surfactin expression（OASIS）. Harmful algal blooms (HABs) pose severe threats to marine ecosystems, aquaculture, and human health. Traditional control methods are often inefficient, environmentally risky, and prone to secondary pollution. To address these challenges, the SUSTechOCEAN team developed an intelligent and controllable HAB mitigation system that integrates artificial intelligence prediction with synthetic biology intervention. Using a deep learning–based OI-SwinUnet model, we predict the risk of HAB occurrence from environmental parameters such as nutrient concentrations, temperature, and dissolved oxygen. When the predicted risk exceeds a defined threshold, engineered Bacillus subtilis expresses Surfactin C14—a biodegradable, low-toxicity biosurfactant with strong algicidal activity—under blue-light induction. Meanwhile, red light activates the expression of the phage-derived YonE protein, which depletes intracellular NAD⁺ and triggers cell death, ensuring biosafety. This system achieves intelligent linkage between “prediction” and “intervention,” providing a sustainable, eco-friendly, and safe synthetic biology solution for marine ecosystem protection.

title: Rational Engineering of Novel Ultra-Efficient Amidohydrolases for Ochratoxin A Degradation
text: Rational Engineering of Novel Ultra-Efficient Amidohydrolases for Ochratoxin A Degradation. By integrating enzyme engineering with synthetic biology, we have developed a highly efficient and specific biodegradation platform with exceptional potential. Starting from ADH3—the most active OTA hydrolase reported to date—we rationally designed the S88E mutant, whose additional hydrogen-bond network increases catalytic efficiency (kcat/KM) by 3.7-fold. To surmount the remaining catalytic bottleneck, we mined the sequence space of ADH3 and identified the homologous enzyme LIADH (73 % identity) that possesses twice the native activity of ADH3. Structure-guided redesign of LIADH yielded the I326A variant; removal of the γ-branched side chain relieves steric congestion at the acyl-enzyme intermediate, affording a further 75 % improvement in activity. Collectively, we obtained two high-performance biocatalysts—ADH3-S88E and LIADH-I326A—and accomplished the first comprehensive structural, kinetic, and mechanistic characterization of any OTA hydrolase.

title: O! Super Carpet
text: O! Super Carpet. Green tides caused by Ulva prolifera have become a seasonal ecological disaster in Qingdao. The traditional physical salvage methods are time-consuming and laborious. So our team’s project uses a synthetic biology solution to address green tides at the source—spores, a key driver of bloom recurrence.​ Since the core of our project is "capture spore", we rearranged letters and named our project “O! Super Carpet”. It is composed of three main modules. We would like to name them after spells from Harry Potter. First, the 'Ennervate' survival spell ensures that our engineered bacteria can survive in high-salinity seawater. Second, the 'Permanent Sticking' functional spell is responsible for efficiently capturing Ulva spores with specificity. Finally, the 'Avada Kedavra' biosafety spell guarantees safety of the project in open environments.  By combining synthetic biology with ecological insight, our project aims to demonstrate how engineered microbes can offer sustainable solutions to marine environmental crises.

title: Pure Era - XJTLU-Software 2025
text: Pure Era - XJTLU-Software 2025. Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) are essential natural molecules with broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity. To accelerate AMP discovery, we developed SPADE, a Systematic Platform for Antimicrobial peptide Database with Evaluation, integrating and standardizing data from four major AMP repositories (APD3, DRAMP, DBAASP, and LAMP), resulting in over 39,000 curated peptides. After rigorous cleaning and unification of experimental conditions, we established the AMP-Oriented Six tasks (AMPOS) dataset and the AMP-Oriented Multi-Property Prediction Task (AMPPT), covering classification and regression subtasks including MIC, half-life, and hemolytic activity. We further designed the AMP-Oriented Multi-task Model (AOMM), achieving state-of-the-art performance across all AMPPT subtasks. Additionally, a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) system was implemented to enhance intelligent AMP searching. Overall, SPADE provides an integrated, reproducible, and extensible foundation for AMP data analysis, model benchmarking, and AI-assisted peptide design in modern bioinformatics.

title: Plaszyme: AI-Powered Discovery of Plastic-Degrading Enzymes
text: Plaszyme: AI-Powered Discovery of Plastic-Degrading Enzymes. Plastic pollution represents a growing global crisis, while biodegrading enzymes provide a sustainable route to plastic recycling. To accelerate enzyme identification, Plaszyme integrates AI-based models that learn from both biological and chemical representations to predict enzyme–polymer interactions with interpretability and precision. Our framework combines machine learning classifiers and structure-aware dual-tower neural networks, enabling multi-level prediction from amino acid sequences to 3D enzyme–polymer compatibility. A lightweight Web App offers browser-based batch prediction, visualization, and interpretability without local setup. In parallel, we curated and released PlaszymeDB, an open-access database compiling verified enzyme–plastic pairs, sequences, structures, and physicochemical descriptors under FAIR principles. Through continued development and open dissemination via iGEM and the Web App, Plaszyme establishes a unified resource for data-driven exploration of plastic biodegradation and sustainable material recycling.

title: Lacbutler
text: Lacbutler. Lactose intolerance, a prevalent global condition, causes symptoms like diarrhea and abdominal pain due to lactase deficiency in the gut. Current dietary management lacks long-term efficacy and impacts life quality. We propose a sustainable synthetic biology-based therapy using engineered Bifidobacterium. This strain is modified with a optimized bgaB lactase and LacY lactose transporter for efficient lactose metabolism. It also incorporates a genetic circuit with a deoxycholic acid-inducible MucBP adhesion protein and an AI-2/CcdB-mediated population control system. This design enables stable colonization at an appropriate density, ensuring continuous lactose breakdown for long-term management of lactose intolerance.

title: Glow to Grow
text: Glow to Grow. Desferrioxamine is the most economically important siderophore, used in life-saving chelation therapy for thalassemia patients and iron overload disorders, plus industrial applications like gallium recovery from wastewater. However, high production costs limit its accessibility. Current production relies on Streptomyces pilosus, which suffers from slow growth, low yields, and complex lifecycles that complicate industrial-scale fermentation, making it unsuitable as a production platform. Our team is transferring the desferrioxamine biosynthetic gene cluster to Rhodococcus, which doesn't naturally produce desferrioxamine but is well-established in industry for producing complex secondary metabolites. Rhodococcus offers fast growth, high scalability, and excellent fermentation characteristics. Both species belong to Actinobacteria, sharing similar genetic architecture, codon usage, and metabolic frameworks necessary for expressing the desferrioxamine pathway. To confirm successful pathway integration and transcriptional activity during transfer, we designed a split-GFP monitoring system. We aim to reduce desferrioxamine production costs and increase its accessibility for medical and industrial applications.

title: CyanoSense: Microcystin Detection and Degradation with Acinetobacter baylyi ADP1
text: CyanoSense: Microcystin Detection and Degradation with Acinetobacter baylyi ADP1. Rapid growth of algae in response to environmental pressures, such as climate change, has increased cyanotoxin prevalence in freshwater ecosystems, exceeding safety standards. The most prevalent cyanotoxins produced are microcystins, known to cause harm to humans and animals upon ingestion. Current methods of identifying microcystins involve complex and expensive quantitative assays, which are impractical for field deployment. Our team explored a method to safely detect and degrade these toxins by engineering Acinetobacter baylyi (ADP1) to perform as a biosensor and biodegrader. The system detects environmental DNA (eDNA) released by microcystin-producing cyanobacteria. Upon detection of a target region of DNA within the microcystin gene pathway, the biosensor will activate genes responsible for enzymatic microcystin degradation, providing a potential strategy for eliminating microcystins.

title: RGBio: Trichromatic Optogenetic Regulation of Gene Expression in E. coli
text: RGBio: Trichromatic Optogenetic Regulation of Gene Expression in E. coli. RGBio focused on creating an “optogenetic toolkit” allowing regulation of three genes or regulons using red, green, and blue light. This toolkit uses three optogenetic switches to orthogonally regulate gene expression in response to each type of light stimulus. Our team applied this toolkit to bioplastic synthesis and modulation of polymer properties. Bioplastics can be made from standard carbon sources or from waste carbon, making the system robust and allowing for remediation of molecules like waste acetate that are produced in large amounts yearly. Other teams and researchers can use our optogenetic toolkit to regulate their genes of interest without the need for induction molecules, and can easily remove or replace components of our optogenetic switches through a simple restriction digest and Gibson Assembly-compatible insert.

title: NCLOSE
text: NCLOSE. With our project NCLOSE, we are tackling the growing global challenge of nitrate pollution. Agriculture is one of the main drivers: synthetic fertilizers and animal manure release large amounts of ammonium, which soil microbes convert to nitrate. NCLOSE aims to counteract this by producing γ-polyglutamic acid (PGA), a natural polymer capable of reversibly binding ammonium, directly in manure. This reduces nitrate leaching while providing crops with a slow-release nutrient source.  We introduced three genes encoding PGA synthetase into Clostridium cellulovorans, an anaerobic, cellulolytic bacterium, well-equipped for growth in manure. Additionally, we created resources to make this chassis more accessible for future teams, including adapted workflows, a genome-scale model and a taxonomic analysis. The development of a solid biosafety concept was also a central aspect. Through integrated human practices, we ensured NCLOSE remains safe, sustainable and socially responsible, turning manure from part of the problem into part of the solution.

title: APHiGO-A Next-Generation RNA Pesticide Platform for Citrus Aphid Control
text: APHiGO-A Next-Generation RNA Pesticide Platform for Citrus Aphid Control. As the world's largest citrus producer, China contributes one-quarter of global citrus output, yet faces severe threats from the concealed brown citrus aphid. To address this, we present APHiGO—an RNAi-based platform for sustainable aphid control, integrating smart monitoring with precise molecular intervention. APHiGO’s early-warning module uses engineered Bacillus subtilis to detect honeydew and emit volatile signals, monitored via IoT sensors. Upon detection, RNAi molecules targeting vital aphid genes are delivered via trunk injection. Packaged in engineered virus-like particles, these molecules are efficiently ingested, silencing key genes and impeding development. For localized outbreaks, modified Metarhizium fungi deliver dsRNA externally and internally, enhancing lethality and delaying resistance. By combining biosensing, RNAi targeting, and biocontrol, APHiGO transitions pest management from chemical reliance to intelligent, sustainable precision agriculture.

title: Pause-aware Codon Design Assistant
text: Pause-aware Codon Design Assistant. Protein translation proceeds discontinuously, with ribosomes pausing to enable co-translational folding of nascent chains. Although ribosome profiling (Ribo-seq) has revealed widespread translational pauses, existing mRNA design frameworks largely ignore these kinetic features. Here, we identify conserved pausing sites across multiple human cell lines using EIF-based Ribo-seq and propose that such pauses facilitate proper protein folding. We developed PACD (Pause-Aware Codon Design), a computational framework that incorporates ribosome pausing information into mRNA optimization. A neural model trained on pausing sequences enables predictive integration with LinearDesign to preserve beneficial pauses during codon optimization. While pause-constrained designs slightly reduce mRNA stability and CAI, they are expected to enhance folding efficiency. This study represents the first systematic attempt to link translational pausing with codon design, providing a foundation for engineering “pause-aware” synthetic genes with improved structural fidelity.

title: Pyronix - The Next Generation of Firefighting
text: Pyronix - The Next Generation of Firefighting. Wildfires present major global challenges, from CO2 emissions and ecosystem destruction to severe public health impacts. Current firefighting methods also carry significant drawbacks. Pyronix offers a new approach, harnessing synthetic biology to create a more sustainable solution. We engineered a hydrogel-based fire retardant assembled from components produced by microorganisms. The gel structure is composed of cellulose and chitosan. Silica nanoparticles and a fire-retardant protein are embedded in the gel to improve its fire resistance. To deploy the hydrogel, we developed an artificial intelligence equipped drone for safe and automated firefighting, supporting life-saving decisions made by the operators.  We engineered yeast strains for enhanced chitosan production, bacterial cells building up silica nanoparticles, and expression systems to produce fire retardant proteins. We assembled the components into a gel-like structure to study its fire-retardant properties. Pyronix provides a solid foundation for developing sustainable firefighting methods from production to deployment.

title: Splintein
text: Splintein. The lack of precise control over post-translational modifications in synthetic protein production is a significant obstacle in research and biomanufacturing, especially in the development of biopharmaceuticals. To overcome this we developed Self Integrating Scaffolds (SIS), protein fragments flanked by split inteins. This project aims to insert a glycosylated SIS in Immunoglobuline G. To optimise our SIS, it’s necessary to test how efficient two pairs of inteins can be used together. Because of that, we have designed a FRET assay, which enables us to test split intein pairs in high-throughput for their quantitative kinetic compatibility in real-time using only a plate reader. In addition, we applied dynamical modelling, docking simulations, structural comparisons, mathematical modelling and programming in R-studio to provide a more in-depth understanding of all these aspects regarding our SIS and FRET assay. Together, our results lay the foundation of using split inteins to change the world of protein engineering.

title: Unravelling PET at the Seams
text: Unravelling PET at the Seams. To alleviate the problem of plastic pollution and mitigate the serious impacts made by plastic on our environment, our team worked on multiple DNA combinations to break down PET. Our solution is HotPETase, an enzyme that can degrade PET plastics readily at high temperatures. We have paired it up with the genes BaCBM2 and CsgA respectively, then combined all three genes together to form our final gene combination. Out of all gene constructs, HotPETase-BaCBM2 showed the best performance, having the greatest increase in absorbance and the largest decrease in mass of the PET fragment at 70°C. Our main target gene combination, CsgA-HotPETase-BaCBM2 showed promising results during the absorbance test, having the second highest increase in absorbance at 60°C. SEM imaging was conducted on the PET samples, with irregular cracks being observed on the PET surface, in contrast to the smooth surface of the control.

title: PURPLE - Plastic Upcycling to Reduce Pollution and Loop the Economy
text: PURPLE - Plastic Upcycling to Reduce Pollution and Loop the Economy. In response to the global challenge of plastic waste, our iGEM project aims to develop innovative biological pathways for the upcycling of polyethylene terephthalate (PET) plastic into high-value products, such as BHB (Beta Hydroxybutyrate).  Our approach designs synthetic pathways in E. coli and P. putida, enabling them to convert PET waste into Polyhydroxybutyrate (PHB) and later BHB. Utilizing computational tools and Flux Balance Analysis (FBA), we will optimize the engineered pathways to enhance the flux towards PHB production. This will include the use of kinetic models to predict and refine enzyme activity based on varying substrate concentrations. By designing and constructing novel biological parts, we aim to establish an innovative production pathway that aligns with circular economy principles. This will not only facilitate the conversion of PET plastic waste into valuable products but also provide a sustainable solution to a pressing environmental issue.

title: GumEraser+：Combat Peach Gummosis Initiative
text: GumEraser+：Combat Peach Gummosis Initiative. Peach gummosis seriously harms peach tree health, mainly triggered by fungal infections and environmental stress. It causes bark cracking and gummy exudation, weakening trees severely or even killing them. Current controls depend on chemicals and agricultural management, but problems like drug resistance and pollution remain, leaving a gap for efficient, eco-friendly solutions.  ‘GumEraser+’ proposes to manipulate three key factors required for disease occurrence:  1) Apply specific RNA-based biopesticides to inhibit the activity of pathogens;  2) Promote the cultivation of disease-resistant host varieties;  3) Promote pruning of peach trees to improve orchard air circulation.  The ‘+’ symbol here stands for three aspirations in addressing it: 1) Boost farmers’ income; 2) Enhance personal growth; 3) Promote knowledge transfer.

title: DNA-Based Biosensors for Cardiovascular miRNA Detection with Machine Learning–Integrated Design Tool
text: DNA-Based Biosensors for Cardiovascular miRNA Detection with Machine Learning–Integrated Design Tool. Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) remain the leading cause of global mortality, highlighting the need for rapid and sensitive diagnostic technologies. We developed an integrated nucleic acid–based biosensing platform that detects CVD-related microRNAs (miRNAs) with high specificity. The biosensor combines three-way junction (3WJ) probe recognition and a split G-quadruplex (G4) DNAzyme switch, where target-induced linker release reconstitutes the G4 structure. The G4/hemin complex catalyzes the oxidation of TMB, producing measurable electrochemical signals on a portable reader. The system achieved a limit of detection of 480 pM, demonstrating strong sensitivity and specificity. To accelerate probe optimization, machine learning (ML) models trained on experimental datasets (2500 miRNA-specific 3WJ probes and 728 split G4 probes) reached 83% accuracy for the 3WJ model and 80% for the split G4 model. This data-driven biosensor framework bridges biosensing probe design and ML prediction, enabling rapid, customizable, and cost-effective miRNA diagnostics for cardiovascular and other diseases.

title: ColoTrace
text: ColoTrace. Significance Colorectal cancer (CRC) is one of the most ubiquitous types of cancer in Hong Kong, with approximately 10,000 new cases diagnosed annually. Early detection can significantly improve prognosis, with successful treatment rates exceeding 90%. However, the current mainstream screening methods, such as colonoscopy, FOBT, and FIT, have their limitations of being invasive and inconvenient. Project Mechanics Our project aims to create a tool that detects CRC in its early stages. Our ColoTrace kit detects overexpressed microRNAs (miR) of CRC in the faecal samples, and create coloured proteins that indicate a positive detection. Engineering and Results Six toehold switches that detect miR-92a-3p and miR-135b-5p are designed, and one of the ligated toehold-plasmids was successfully cloned in E. coli, and two of the toehold-plasmids showed strong expression when triggered by the target microRNA.

title: Aptagenix: One-Pot Isothermal Assay for EGFR Mutation Screening in Lung Cancer
text: Aptagenix: One-Pot Isothermal Assay for EGFR Mutation Screening in Lung Cancer. The project aims to develop a low-cost, rapid, and user-friendly diagnostic kit for detecting EGFR mutations in circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA), which are associated with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). The system integrates Recombinase Polymerase Amplification (RPA) with CRISPR-Cas9 amplicon cleavage and a Lateral Flow Assay (LFA) readout, enabling a one-pot, isothermal assay that delivers a visual result without specialized equipment. This approach aims to make early molecular screening for NSCLC accessible, especially in resource-limited regions.

title: Crypto-Knight: A Novel Point Of Care Colourimetric Diagnostic Test For Cryptosporidiosis Based On LAMP
text: Crypto-Knight: A Novel Point Of Care Colourimetric Diagnostic Test For Cryptosporidiosis Based On LAMP. One of the most neglected tropical diseases, Cryptosporidiosis kills an estimated 200,000 children every year and 10 million disability adjusted life years lost annually. It is caused by a parasite, and spreads through infected water samples globally. Current methods, such as qPCR, are expensive, unreliable and affected by inhibitors in faecal samples, with the most common methods having a sensitivity of around 40-60%.    Using Loop Mediated Isothermal Amplification, we designed a novel point of care diagnostic for the 18s rRNA of Cryptosporidium, designing an efficient primer set, and four new fusion Bst polymerases, with subdomains designed to increase reverse transcriptase activity, thermostability and inhibitor tolerance. Targeting 18s rRNA allows the test to detect 1 oocyst/gram of faecal sample (compared to qPCR’s 300/gram). Results are shown colourimetrically for easy use. With our model and education work, we made the test even more accessible.    It's time to shine a LAMP On Cryptosporidiosis!

title: REEvolutionaTe
text: REEvolutionaTe. Rare earth elements (REEs) and tellurium are essential for high-tech and renewable technologies, yet less than 1% are currently recycled. To address this, we developed a sustainable, bio-based strategy to recover these elements from e-waste streams. We engineered a modular system using amyloid protein fibers displaying REE-binding proteins, achieving high-affinity capture of REE ions and creating a powerful part collection. Mathematical modeling and molecular dynamics simulations guided design optimization, while a business plan and market analysis evaluated commercial viability. For tellurium recovery, we harnessed the Ter operon to efficiently reduce toxic tellurite into elemental tellurium. To promote our project and raise awareness of synthetic biology, we conducted extensive outreach through exhibitions, workshops, educational activities, blogs, podcasts, and interactive games across hospitals, museums, and schools. Thus, our project demonstrates an integrated synthetic biology platform for the biological recovery of REEs and tellurium from electronic waste.

title: RePLAce with PLAstic: Enabling On-Site PLA Degradation
text: RePLAce with PLAstic: Enabling On-Site PLA Degradation. Through IHP, we identified two key challenges from stakeholders’ perspectives: insufficient efficiency of PLA-degrading enzymes and unclear recycling classification. To address the first issue, we engineered recombinant enzymes (AC, CA, DP, PK) and developed an auto-induction measurement system for high-throughput screening, with PK variants showing the most promising activity. For the second issue, we aligned with the SDGs by organizing a target field to test PLA usage in isolation and submitting a citizen proposal to advocate for clearer waste management policies and the establishment of industrial composting facilities in Taiwan, providing a practical solution to misclassification. Our project demonstrates the integration of enzyme engineering with community engagement to advance PLA degradation and sustainable waste management.

title: MeowTrack: A Probiotic Platform for Feline Gut Health
text: MeowTrack: A Probiotic Platform for Feline Gut Health. Cats are among the most popular companion animals worldwide, yet many of their health issues remain undiagnosed due to subtle symptoms and limited diagnostic tools. Inflammatory Bowel Disease (IBD), often aggravated by hairball accumulation, is a prevalent chronic condition that compromises digestive health. To address this, we developed MeowTrack, a programmable therapeutic probiotic platform that detects, treats, and records feline gut health. The system senses taurocholic acid (food intake) and calprotectin (IBD biomarker) and integrates these inputs through an AND logic gate, ensuring responses occur only under disease conditions with food available. Upon activation, MeowTrack expresses keratin-degrading enzymes to remove hairballs, butyrate-producing enzymes to restore gut balance, and chromoproteins or fluorescent proteins to visualize disease states in feces. Additionally, a Retro-Cascorder module records transcriptional events linked to inflammation, while a smart litter box equipped with fluorescence detection enables seamless, at-home monitoring of feline gut health.

title: antiBACjacket
text: antiBACjacket. Plastic cling films are widely used in food preservation but pose long-term environmental risks due to poor degradability, while microbial spoilage continues to cause significant food waste. To address these challenges, SMS-Shenzhen is designing a biodegradable and antimicrobial cling film using synthetic biology. We introduced the pls gene from Streptomyces albulus into Bacillus subtilis to enable ε-polylysine (PLL) production and introduced PPK2 and lysC311 to enhance the productivity. A kill switch is constructed by knocking out the alrA gene, rendering the strain auxotrophic and limiting its survival to controlled conditions.
