Protein quantification indicated increased secretion in engineered strains (0.10 vs 0.04 µg/µL controls). Functional assays validated pgxC activity: engineered L. reuteri released significantly greater amounts of D-galacturonic acid from pectin, with degradation efficiencies varying across fruit sources (pear and tomato > kiwi > banana > watermelon). This work demonstrates probiotic-mediated fruit peel valorization and highlights applications in biofuels, feed, and prebiotic production through a sustainable waste-to-resource platform.

title: Stress Protection of mRNA with Tardigrade IDPs for Vaccine Stability Applications
text: Stress Protection of mRNA with Tardigrade IDPs for Vaccine Stability Applications. Tardigrades are extremophiles capable of surviving desiccation, freezing, and irradiation, owing to unique intrinsically disordered proteins (IDPs) that protect cells and biomolecules under stress. As mRNA vaccines become increasingly important, protecting these fragile molecules from degradation is crucial, particularly given the expense and inequity associated with cold chain storage systems. To harness tardigrade resilience, we synthetically engineered ten IDP genes from Ramazzottius varieornatus and Hypsibius exemplaris and expressed them in Chinese hamster ovary (CHO) cells and Human Embryonic Kidney (HEK) cells. As a proof of concept, these proteins will be combined with mRNA encoding green fluorescent protein (GFP) and subjected to variations in temperature and heating. GFP mRNA integrity and translational capacity will be assessed in using gel electrophoresis. Demonstrating mRNA protection could enable tardigrade IDP-based stabilization of vaccines, reducing cold chain dependence and improving global vaccine accessibility.

title: PHOENICS: Smart Synthetic Immune Cells for Precision Oncology
text: PHOENICS: Smart Synthetic Immune Cells for Precision Oncology. We present PHOENICS, a modular signaling platform that uses phosphorylation logic to enable programmable, ligand-specific cancer therapies. Combining synthetic GPCR and MESA receptors with kinase/phosphatase computation and tunable expression or secretion outputs, PHOENICS provides rapid, reversible, and retargetable control of therapeutic activity. Supported by the in silico optimization platform SPARC, it offers flexible adaptation to distinct tumor microenvironments and therapeutic effectors. Beyond the bench, we built an educational innovation ecosystem that equips future pioneers with the network and knowledge to navigate the challenges of translational research. Uniting innovation and education, PHOENICS drives modular precision oncology and empowers future translational innovators.

title: PHAntom Thalassic :  From Salty-Water Strains to Ocean-Safe Plastics
text: PHAntom Thalassic :  From Salty-Water Strains to Ocean-Safe Plastics. Plastic pollution is a global crisis demanding sustainable alternatives. Our project, PHAntom Thalassic, develops a cost-effective method to produce biodegradable polyhydroxyalkanoates (PHA) using deep-sea halophilic bacteria. Focusing on Halomonas strains LA4 and LA5, which thrive in high-salt, alkaline environments, we enable open, contamination-resistant fermentation and wastewater recycling. The phaCAB operon from Ralstonia eutropha (Cupriavidus necator) was introduced into Halomonas via E. coli S17-1λ conjugation, and PHA yield was assessed by Nile Red staining and GC-MS. Using CRISPR/Cas9, we integrated PHA genes into the Halomonas genome. Through extensive Human Practices, we engaged professors, fishermen, policymakers, and industry experts to align our work with real-world needs. Our PHA plastics are designed to degrade safely in marine environments, providing a sustainable solution to reduce ocean pollution and protect coral reefs and mangroves.

title: Vesper: Engineering a Bioluminescent and Aromatic Yeast for Sleep and Mood Regulation
text: Vesper: Engineering a Bioluminescent and Aromatic Yeast for Sleep and Mood Regulation. Modern society faces a pervasive sleep and mental health crisis, with conventional solutions often being inadequate or accompanied by side effects. Our project, Vesper, harnesses the power of synthetic biology to create a natural, non-habit-forming alternative. We engineered two distinct Saccharomyces cerevisiae strains: one capable of autonomous, gentle bioluminescence through an optimized fungal caffeic acid pathway, and another producing a spectrum of therapeutic terpenoid aromas like linalool and citronellol. These strains are designed to work in synergy within a personal sleep device, the Bio-Pod, delivering multi-sensory therapy. Our human-centered design, informed by extensive human practices, is complemented by a built-in dual-layer suicide switch for robust biocontainment. Vesper offers a holistic approach to wellness, reconnecting users with the restorative power of nature through engineered biology.

title: Development of a Biosensor for Arsenic Contamination in Rice Using RNA Aptamer Technology
text: Development of a Biosensor for Arsenic Contamination in Rice Using RNA Aptamer Technology. This project develops a cost-effective biosensor for detecting arsenic in rice using Broccoli RNA aptamer technology, addressing food safety concerns per the Healthy Babies Bright Futures report (May 2025). The WIST team designed an ArsR-regulated system where the Broccoli aptamer activates fluorescence with DFHBI-1T upon arsenic binding. Through Design-Build-Test-Learn iterations, two plasmids were optimized: WIST_SENSE_MedArsR_StrArsC_001_A, producing ArsR and ArsC under a constitutive promoter for detection, and WIST_REPORT_002_B, generating the F-30 Broccoli aptamer for fluorescence. Mathematical modeling with a 4-parameter logistic model established a Limit of Detection below the FDA’s 100 ppb threshold, a 5–100 ppb dynamic range, and a 20–30 minute optimal window, validated by testing against interferents (Pb²⁺, Cu²⁺, Fe³⁺) and rice extracts from the HBBF report. Cell-free systems with T7 variants tuned synthesis. New parts are under iGEM Registry safety review. Despite uncompleted lyophilization and field deployment, the project offers valuable design data and protocols for future teams.

title: IXPOSE: unlocking DNA detection potential of TIGR-Tas
text: IXPOSE: unlocking DNA detection potential of TIGR-Tas. Lithuania is a hotspot in Europe for tick-borne diseases, with thousands of people exposed to Lyme disease and tick-borne encephalitis annually. However, despite awareness of these common infections, a significant gap remains: we lack vital data on other pathogens circulating in wild tick populations. This missing information forces researchers, doctors, and public health officials to make educated guesses. To address this, we present a breakthrough solution using TIGR-Tas—a novel RNA-guided, DNA-targeting system. Unlike CRISPR-Cas, TIGR-Tas operates in a PAM-independent manner, expanding the range of detectable DNA sequences. By integrating TIGR-Tas with lateral flow assays and isothermal DNA amplification methods such as RPA, it becomes a powerful, field-ready diagnostic tool. With this system, we aim to uncover the hidden diversity of tick-borne pathogens, empowering healthcare, enhancing prevention, advancing research, and protecting communities throughout Lithuania and beyond.

title: Engineering Cupriavidus necator H16 for In-Situ Production of Alpha-Lactalbumin in Space
text: Engineering Cupriavidus necator H16 for In-Situ Production of Alpha-Lactalbumin in Space. As deep-space missions lengthen, sustaining astronaut nutrition becomes critical. We present a synthetic-biology platform using the hydrogen-oxidizing bacterium Cupriavidus necator H16 for in-situ production of human α-lactalbumin aboard spacecraft. The strain was engineered to autotrophically convert astronaut metabolic wastes (CO₂, urea) into active α-lactalbumin. Guided by genome-scale metabolic modeling, pathway optimization enabled a closed-loop production system. To improve nutritional performance, we rationally inserted optimized trypsin-cleavage sites to enhance gastrointestinal digestibility. We also designed a microgravity-adapted bioreactor that addresses gas–liquid mass-transfer limitations, facilitating efficient cultivation and product recovery. Together, these advances demonstrate the feasibility of microbial biomanufacturing for space life-support and provide a technical foundation for sustainable extraterrestrial nutrition.

title: Insights into Molecular Interactions ─ Predicting and Validating PFOA Binding to Human Proteins
text: Insights into Molecular Interactions ─ Predicting and Validating PFOA Binding to Human Proteins. PFAS (per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances) are chemicals used in several manufactured products. They have been called “forever chemicals” for their inability to break down in our environment and have accumulated to an extent that at least 97% of Americans have traceable amounts in their blood (NHANES 2015).  However, while the full spectrum of their effects is not entirely understood, they have been implicated in several cancers and liver conditions.  Current detection methods like mass spectrometry and liquid or gas chromatography are expensive and inaccessible to the general public. Our project aims to develop a cost-effective protein-based detection system for PFAS. Using a reverse-screening approach across multiple protein-ligand databases, we identified candidate human proteins predicted to bind perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA), a representative PFAS. Among these, we purified and characterized a key DNA repair protein that is significantly destabilized in the presence of PFOA based on results from differential scanning fluorimetry (DSF).

title: Dual-Action Oral Vaccine Platform: Engineered Probiotics Synthesizing Nanocyclobodies and Membrane-Displayed Antigens
text: Dual-Action Oral Vaccine Platform: Engineered Probiotics Synthesizing Nanocyclobodies and Membrane-Displayed Antigens. AvianGuard is an innovative proposal based on a modular platform, designed to be effective against different viruses. In this opportunity, it was validated against the challenge of avian influenza (H5N1), a disease that threatens food security and poultry production. In Ecuador, the vaccines currently available do not fit the small-scale producer model; therefore, our solution consists of a dual-action oral probiotic vaccine, formulated in alginate-chitosan microcapsules that protect its immunological components and ensure their release in the bird’s intestine. The system combines two protection mechanisms: active immunity, generated from conserved antigens expressed in Lactococcus lactis, and passive immunity, through cyclobodies produced in E. coli. Thanks to its easy administration mixed with feed, AvianGuard emerges as an accessible, effective, and low-cost alternative for controlling avian influenza in small-scale poultry production systems.

title: meduCA: Microbes Enabling Decarbonized-Urbanization via Carbonic Anhydrase
text: meduCA: Microbes Enabling Decarbonized-Urbanization via Carbonic Anhydrase. Space exploration is rapidly advancing, accelerating the need to protect explorers and equipment from harsh extraterrestrial environments. Building infrastructure in space is challenging, as transporting construction materials to other planets is both costly and environmentally unsustainable. meduCA addresses this by harnessing the power of microbially-induced calcium carbonate precipitation using carbonic anhydrase (CA) enzymes to turn atmospheric CO₂ into carbon-negative bricks via biocementation. Our system employs Synechococcus elongatus, engineered to surface display CA, enabling efficient CO₂ sequestration and calcite precipitation. Complementary efforts on Earth employ Caulobacter crescentus to biocement hazardous mine tailings, mitigating toxic dust and leaching. Together, these applications demonstrate the versatility of living building materials in both extraterrestrial and terrestrial settings. To empower future teams, we developed innovative software tools, a custom bioink-bioprinting platform, and an inclusivity framework to expand accessibility in synthetic biology in hopes of building a resilient future on Earth, and one day, on Mars.

title: iGEM Concordia Montreal: ToastBusters
text: iGEM Concordia Montreal: ToastBusters. The only effective treatment for celiac disease is a strict gluten-free diet. While this approach allows individuals to manage their symptoms, it does not eliminate the risk of accidental gluten exposure due to cross-contamination. Our team is developing an approach centered around engineered probiotic bacteria capable of secreting gluten-degrading enzymes directly in the gut. Delivering enzymes capable of break down the immunogenic peptides responsible for triggering the immune response in individuals with celiac disease. In parallel, we investigated peptide caps that can bind to residual gliadin fragments, masking the key epitopes and preventing the immune system from recognizing uncleaved gluten. Together, these strategies highlight complementary ways to significantly reduce the concentration of harmful gluten fragments before they can activate the immune system, offering a potential layer of protection beyond the limitations of a gluten-free diet.

title: Magnolyse: Engineered Magnetotactic Bacteria for Ovarian Cancer Therapy
text: Magnolyse: Engineered Magnetotactic Bacteria for Ovarian Cancer Therapy. We have aimed to develop a targeted, bacterial-based cancer therapeutic platform to enhance treatment options for ovarian cancer patients. This system will employ Magnetospirillum magneticum AMB-1, a bacterial strain which exhibits magnetotaxis and aerotaxis. We are engineering AMB-1 to produce the cytotoxic agent Cytolysin A to serve as a tumor-eliminating therapeutic. Cytolysin A production will be regulated by a heat shock promoter which is inducible by increased temperature as a result of an external alternating magnetic field. In addition, we aim to maximize the specificity of the therapeutic system by implementing a ligand on the surface of AMB-1 to the folate receptor alpha which is highly expressed in ovarian cancer cells. Our ultimate goal is to develop an innovative and targeted therapeutic option for those suffering with ovarian cancer. Ultimately, we hope to develop a platform that is generalizable to all cancers forming solid tumors.

title: MethaNO: Synthetic Biology-Based Biosensors for Rapid Methanol Detection in Alcoholic Beverages
text: MethaNO: Synthetic Biology-Based Biosensors for Rapid Methanol Detection in Alcoholic Beverages. Methanol contamination in alcoholic beverages is a serious global health risk, yet accessible detection methods are lacking. Team MethaNO from Macquarie University proposes two synthetic biology-based biosensors for low-cost, rapid methanol detection. The first design uses a whole-cell E. coli sensor featuring a chimeric histidine kinase combining MxaY (from Paracoccus denitrificans) with CusS (from E. coli), activating a kinase phosphorylation pathway to express a visible blue chromoprotein (AmilCP) in response to methanol. The second design employs a Ca²⁺-PQQ-dependent methanol dehydrogenase (MDH) from Methylorubrum extorquens, expressed and isolated from E. coli to create a cell-free system. MDH oxidizes methanol to formaldehyde, detectable via colorimetric assays. Both biosensors offer scalable, specific, and visual detection of hazardous methanol levels in beverages.

title: Fluoro-free: A Probiotic to Capture and Remove Harmful PFAS from the GI Tract
text: Fluoro-free: A Probiotic to Capture and Remove Harmful PFAS from the GI Tract. Perfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are synthetic contaminants that bioaccumulate and are associated with adverse health effects. While remediation efforts target environmental cleanup, strategies to lower PFAS levels within the human body remain limited. We propose a probiotic-based therapeutic approach using engineered Escherichia coli Nissle 1917 (EcN) to sequester PFAS in the gastrointestinal tract. By capturing PFAS before absorption, EcN could reduce systemic exposure and enhance excretion. Our hypothesis is that bacterial PFAS uptake is primarily transporter-mediated. To maximize intracellular retention, we disrupted the TolC-AcrB efflux system. As a proof of concept, we inhibited AcrB using small molecule inhibitor Phenylalanine–Arginine Beta-Naphthylamide. Subsequently, we created a stable AcrB knockout via recA-mediated recombination.This work lays the foundation for probiotic therapeutics targeting PFAS exposure. Beyond the lab, we advance public outreach initiatives to educate and raise PFAS awareness and promote STEM accessibility in our community.

title: ReguSAMe
text: ReguSAMe. The global incidence of cirrhosis is on the rise, and current therapies can only delay disease progression, often requiring lifelong medication. Existing studies have confirmed that S-adenosylmethionine (SAM) has unique value in restoring hepatocyte metabolism and function. However, its clinical application faces challenges such as low oral bioavailability and the risk of inducing the transition from cirrhosis to hepatocellular carcinoma due to sustained elevation of hepatic SAM concentrations beyond physiological levels with long-term use. To precisely regulate SAM in cirrhosis, we engineered a SAM-responsive aptazyme, ReguSAMe, by fusing a SAM riboswitch to the HDV ribozyme followed by multicycle evolution. By embedding ReguSAMe into the 3'UTR of MAT1A mRNA, we established a negative feedback circuit for SAM homeostasis in hepatocytes. it expresses MAT1A to synthesize SAM when levels are low and self-cleaves to terminate expression when levels normalize. This precise control offers a promising therapeutic strategy with reduced side effects.

title: A Pichia pastoris factory for efficient production of lipase
text: A Pichia pastoris factory for efficient production of lipase. With the intensification of the energy crisis and the rising demand for environmental protection, biodiesel, as a clean energy source, has attracted much attention. Every year, our country generates hundreds of millions of tons of waste oils such as used cooking oil. If not handled properly, it may cause food safety and environmental risks. The traditional chemical method for producing biodiesel has problems such as high energy consumption and pollution; while the biological enzyme method, with advantages like environmental friendliness and mild conditions, has become a new direction, but it also has disadvantages such as low enzyme activity and high cost. This project aims to improve the reaction efficiency and stability of the biological enzyme method, converting waste oils into environmentally friendly biodiesel, contributing to the "dual carbon" goal, promoting the transformation of the energy structure and sustainable development.

title: KINETiC: Kynurenine-depleting Immuno-reversal Network in E. coli for Therapy in Colorectal cancer
text: KINETiC: Kynurenine-depleting Immuno-reversal Network in E. coli for Therapy in Colorectal cancer. Our project is expected to provide a new idea and method for cancer treatment. In recent years, kynureninase (KYNase) has gradually attracted extensive attention in the field of cancer immunotherapy. We utilized synthetic biology methods and engineered bacteria to express KY Nase, regulating the metabolism of the KP pathway within tumor cells, consuming its downstream metabolite Kyn. This inhibits tumor immune escape, enhances the host's immune system response, and achieves tumor cell death. We utilized Escherichia coli BL21 (DE3) as the chassis cell and the hypoxic and high-lactic-acid regulatory ALPaGA subsystem as promoter, to express KYNase in the tumor microenvironment. We also made semi-rational modifications to KYNase, hoping to obtain an enzyme with better catalytic effect. We designed and built a PhiX174E lysis protein module to release KYNase extracellularly at the right time. For biosafety, we designed a suicide switch to prevent engineered strains from being released into the environment.

title: BRIGHT: Bile Acid Responsive Indicator for Gut Health Tracking
text: BRIGHT: Bile Acid Responsive Indicator for Gut Health Tracking. Chronic diarrhea affects millions worldwide, yet its underlying causes often remain undiagnosed due to the lack of accessible diagnostic tools. One of the most overlooked conditions is Bile Acid Malabsorption (BAM), a disorder in which excess bile acids reach the colon, leading to persistent diarrhea, abdominal pain, and impaired quality of life. Current diagnostic methods for BAM are either too invasive, expensive, or impractical for routine clinical use, resulting in long diagnostic delays and misclassification as irritable bowel syndrome. To address this gap, we developed BRIGHT, a novel bioluminescent biosensor that detects bile acids in stool samples. BRIGHT provides a simple, fast, and affordable readout that can be quantified with a smartphone camera, opening the door to a home based point-of-care test. By lowering barriers for both patients and clinicians, BRIGHT aims to empower individuals, accelerate diagnosis, and pave the way toward improved treatment outcomes.

title: VeriFied
text: VeriFied. Forensic science is a field that lacks reliable methods for determining the age of bloodstains, a key factor in reconstructing timelines for crimes. To address this issue, in our project we are developing an innovative, on-site forensic investigation tool – VeriFied – that allows crime scene investigators to quickly and reliably assess the age of bloodstains. The method is based on an enzyme fragment complementation assay that produces a bioluminescence signal. The signal intensity correlates with the levels of oxidized albumin that increase over time as bloodstains are exposed to air. Our aim is to introduce a scientifically robust, quantitative method that reduces reliance on individual interpretation and improves the accuracy of investigation done at a crime scene. This enables criminal investigators to establish more precise timelines and identify relevant bloodstains to the case, guiding the investigation with a scientific basis and solving crimes that would have previously gone unsolved.

title: GutFeeling: Fishing for Solutions
text: GutFeeling: Fishing for Solutions. Chronic diseases often require lifelong medication, yet poor adherence remains a major barrier to effective treatment. This leads to increased mortality, higher healthcare costs, and reduced quality of life. In Parkinsons disease lack of adherence is caused by the symptoms of the disease, like memory loss and dyskinesia.  Therefore, we propose the development of a self-sustaining drug delivery platform using engineered commensal gut bacteria. As a proof of concept, we aim to modify Pseudomonas alcaligenes to autonomously produce and secrete L-DOPA within the gut. To validate the constructs we used fluorescent reporter proteins and L-DOPA biosynthesis. To visualize P. alcaligenes colonization, protein expression and secretion we will use its host: zebrafish. To test our bacteria in a mammalian system we used a gut transwell system. We envision that our project contributes to a living microbial biofactory approach to drug delivery, reducing the need for continuous self-administration.

title: LATCH "Live Adhesion Tool for Candida Hunting"
text: LATCH "Live Adhesion Tool for Candida Hunting". Candida albicans, responsible for about 65% of Candida infections and 200,000 deaths annually, mainly affects immunocompromised individuals. Current treatments are often ineffective or toxic. In project LATCH, we aimed to improve antifungal therapy by engineering Bacillus subtilis, a generally non-pathogenic human commensal with natural antifungal properties, to target C. albicans. By expressing chitinase and SP1 on its membrane via a linking sequence, B. subtilis can bind to chitin on the fungal surface, increasing local antifungal concentration. Computational modeling guided adhesion dynamics, binding specificity, and expression optimization. Although only the plasmid design was verified and no binding data obtained, the project provided valuable insights and inspired local education on fungal infections and synthetic biology through outreach in Gothenburg.

title: GenOMe: the genome LEGO baseplate for iGEM teams.
text: GenOMe: the genome LEGO baseplate for iGEM teams.. GenOMe is a next-generation, plasmid-free genome engineering platform that enables iGEM teams to integrate BioBrick components directly into specific E. coli chromosomal sites within just two days, achieving up to 80% efficiency. At its core, Bxb1 integrase mediates precise recombination between chromosomal attB and cassette attP sites, allowing seamless and site-specific DNA integration. The LandingPad module establishes reusable genomic slots that enable multi-round, marker-free insertions, while the GenOMe Parts Collection offers standardized attB/attP modules for scalable and modular construction. Combined with GenOMe Navigator, which predicts optimal integration sites and success rates, this system transforms genome editing into a fast, reliable, and standardized workflow—a true “genome LEGO baseplate” that empowers iGEM teams to build stable, creative, and inheritable genetic architectures, advancing synthetic biology into a new era of genome engineering.

title: AshBloom: A rhamnolipid-derived foam offering a sustainable, non-toxic alternative to traditional firefighting solutions.
text: AshBloom: A rhamnolipid-derived foam offering a sustainable, non-toxic alternative to traditional firefighting solutions.. Wildfires in Canada’s boreal forests are increasing in frequency and severity, creating landscapes that struggle to recover. Current wildfire suppression uses plain water or chemical foams that prioritize flame control but overlook ecological impacts. Class A foams, commonly used in wildland firefighting, are petrochemical-based, produced via non-sustainable processes, and harm soil and aquatic health. Ammonium-based retardants also disrupt seed germination and microbial communities, with potential nutrient runoff risks. AshBloom presents an eco-friendly alternative: a bio-based, biodegradable fire-suppressant foam made from microbial rhamnolipids via sustainable fermentation. This foam matches the performance of traditional products while enhancing post-fire soil function by promoting water infiltration, beneficial microbes, and seed germination. Being made from renewable feedstocks like waste cooking oil, it rapidly degrades without toxic residues. AshBloom supports both fire suppression and ecological restoration, offering a tool that helps landscapes regenerate sustainably and aids firefighters and forest managers in protecting ecosystems with nature-aligned technology.

title: CamiRa - Crop Assessment via microRNA Analysis
text: CamiRa - Crop Assessment via microRNA Analysis. CamiRa, Crop Assessment via microRNA Analysis, is an affordable, easy-to-use, all-in-one miRNA extraction and analysis kit which detects nutrient deficiencies before crops show visible signs for early intervention (i.e. before crop yield is affected). Due to its ease of use, CamiRa can also be used to check the crops after nutrient supplementation to check if they have recovered, to prevent overapplication resulting in eutrophication. Our extraction protocol combines an isopropanol-based chemical precipitation with a hand centrifuge, designed to make a cheap, easy-to-operate and safe extraction procedure that could be carried out by farmers, without needing extensive laboratory equipment and training. After extraction, our analysis tool involves a method of detecting miRNAs from our plant extracts. Three different detection methods have been considered: two using rolling circle amplification (RCA) as a form of isothermal signal amplification (G-quadruplex and Bioluminescence resonance energy transfer (BRET)), and one without amplification based on sandwich hybridisation.

title: Foundations for an AHL-Responsive Genetic Circuit in Eukaryotic Cells: A Biofilm-Disrupting Therapeutic
text: Foundations for an AHL-Responsive Genetic Circuit in Eukaryotic Cells: A Biofilm-Disrupting Therapeutic. Pseudomonas aeruginosa biofilms drive chronic lung infections in cystic fibrosis (CF) by resisting antibiotics and immune clearance. Biofilm development is regulated by quorum sensing (QS) via acyl-homoserine lactones (AHLs), making QS an appealing therapeutic target. While AHL detection has been engineered in bacteria, its use in eukaryotic systems remains unexplored. We developed early-stage eukaryotic genetic circuits linking AHL sensing to gene expression using chimeric LasR and RhlR receptors. In silico docking (HADDOCK) guided variant selection based on ligand binding and dimerization stability. Complementary biofilm assays using AiiA lactonase, alginate lyase, and α-amylase demonstrated measureable inhibition of P. aeruginosa PAO1 biofilms. Together, these results lay the groundwork for AHL-responsive genetic circuits in mammalian cells, supporting future synthetic biology-based therapies where engineered immune cells could detect bacterial QS signals and secrete biofilm-degrading enzymes for targeted CF treatment.

title: LiRA - A dual-input RNA logic system for precise detection and treatment of HBV-driven HCC.
text: LiRA - A dual-input RNA logic system for precise detection and treatment of HBV-driven HCC.. Most cancer treatments, from chemotherapy to targeted inhibitors, act systemically, killing cancer cells but also damaging healthy ones. This is due to a central problem in oncology: few cancers have a single biomarker both unique and abundant enough to be safely used as a therapeutic trigger. Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), especially when driven by hepatitis B virus (HBV), exemplifies this challenge. Markers such as GPC3, AKR1B10, and RP11 are elevated in tumors but also appear in healthy tissues, making single-signal therapies inherently risky. LiRA overcomes this through a programmable intracellular RNA logic gate inspired by Boolean computation. Built on the RADAR technology, LiRA activates only when two biomarker transcripts are detected together within the same cell, ensuring precise activation. In HEK293T, LiRA sensors achieved up to 23-fold activation and demonstrated strict AND-gate behavior. By replacing reporters with a therapeutic output, LiRA allows for targeted treatment, paving the way for next-generation therapeutics.

title: （BUFFER）Bioremediation of Unwieldy Organic Compounds Featuring Functionalized Escherichia coli Regulated by a Quorum Sensing System
text: （BUFFER）Bioremediation of Unwieldy Organic Compounds Featuring Functionalized Escherichia coli Regulated by a Quorum Sensing System. Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) are persistent organic pollutants in the urban environment, because of their hydrophobic and lipophilic character, PAHs is an easily enriched in sludge, which is by-product of sewage treatment and widely used in cultivated land . The accumulation of PAHs can pose huge threats to the water bodies. According to Guangzhou WWTP, the concentration of several PAHs in local effluent, even after wastewater treatment, still remained approximately 10 to 15 times above China’s acceptable risk levels. Due to the numerous drawbacks of the existing approaches, such as low efficiency and significant side effects, we come up with a more comprehensive solution to this problem: constructing an engineered E.coli which is integrated with plasmids containing diverse gene clusters, endowing it with higher degradation capability, enhanced environmental resistance, and safer switch control. The goal of the project is to provide a safer and more efficient mean of treating PAHs.

title: yeast SMART（yeast Synthetic Modulatory Adaptation for stress Resistant based on TCM）
text: yeast SMART（yeast Synthetic Modulatory Adaptation for stress Resistant based on TCM）. Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) employs "pulse diagnosis" to identify bodily imbalance via dynamic patterns—such as the speed, strength, and rhythm of the wrist pulse—and facilitate precise interventions. Industrial yeast cell factories also encounter intermittent, multi-source stresses analogous to physiological imbalances in human body, yet they lack a pulse-diagnosis-like technique to pinpoint stress disturbances and implement tailored regulation. Such stresses reduce product yield and compromise batch stability, becoming a major bottleneck for large-scale production. Inspired by TCM, we propose visualizing the spatiotemporal responses of yeast strains as "stress pulse patterns," and designing targeted genetic regulatory modules accordingly. Specifically, we developed a tripartite genetic oscillator that transforms stress inputs into quantifiable “fluorescent pulses” (to analyze stress sources/intensities) and paired it with a toolkit of multi-stress resistance genetic elements and a pulse regulation strategy. This low-metabolic-burden, customizable platform enables dynamic diagnosis and precise regulation in fermentation, boosting process robustness and efficiency.

title: Mining of Marine PET-Degrading Enzymes
text: Mining of Marine PET-Degrading Enzymes. The marine metagenome harbors numerous functional genes that have yet to be discovered and engineered for utilization. Currently, most of the known wild-type PET-degrading enzymes and engineered high-activity PET-degrading enzymes such as IsPETase and ICCG are derived from terrestrial sources and are suitable for functioning in low-salt concentration conditions, thus their application scenarios are greatly restricted by salt concentration. At present, microplastic pollution in marine environments is severe, and one major source of marine microplastics is high salinity wastewater. The main objective of our project is to solve the degradation problem of PET microplastics in high-salt water bodies by mining PET-degrading enzymes from the ocean and conducting targeted modifications to enhance their activity.

title: PENgUIN—Prime Editor and Novel prime editing guideRNAs for Understanding Intracellular Narratives—
text: PENgUIN—Prime Editor and Novel prime editing guideRNAs for Understanding Intracellular Narratives—. While current biological tools can identify molecules, they cannot track the precise order of microRNA (miRNA) expression in single cells, creating a critical research bottleneck. Our technology, PENgUIN, overcomes this challenge. It uses a novel “miRNA switch Prime Editing” technique to sequentially record miRNA activity onto a “DNA Tape.” This tape can then be analyzed to reconstruct a complete timeline of expression at the single-cell level. PENgUIN holds the promise of unraveling the mechanisms behind complex medical problems, such as the heterogeneous differentiation of iPS cells and the acquisition of drug resistance in cancer. As a highly adaptable gene circuit component, it is also positioned to become a foundational tool that will drive the next generation of synthetic biology.

title: RareAmine Forge: Engineering ThermoFactories for Specialized Polyamines
text: RareAmine Forge: Engineering ThermoFactories for Specialized Polyamines. This project establishes a thermotolerant microbial platform for the biosynthesis of specialized polyamines—long-chain and branched molecules with significant potential in medicine, agriculture, and advanced materials. The workflow began with collecting hot spring samples across a temperature gradient. Metagenomic analysis confirmed temperature as a core driver of microbial community structure and function, revealing a significant enrichment of polyamine synthesis pathways, especially spermidine synthase, which enabled the mining of key synthase genes. Subsequent multi-omics analysis of isolated thermophilic Bacillus strains under temperature stress revealed a coordinated cellular adaptation strategy involving metabolic reprogramming, protein homeostasis, and membrane regulation. Morphological analysis visually confirmed these adaptations. Crucially, polyamine biosynthesis pathways were consistently upregulated under heat stress, underscoring their integral role in thermotolerance. This project successfully validated native thermotolerant Bacillus as an ideal chassis, decoded the mechanisms of heat resistance and polyamine biosynthesis, and identified key synthetic biology elements. Future research will focus on developing synthetic biology tools for this chassis, genetically engineering the strain to optimize the production of target polyamines via modular pathway assembly and flux optimization, and expanding the portfolio of accessible bioactive polyamines by discovering novel enzymes from the established platforms.

title: PetPeptide Antibacterial Dressing
text: PetPeptide Antibacterial Dressing. In today's society, over one million people die each year from antibiotic-resistant bacteria [1], which is largely attributed to the excessive use of antibiotics over the past few decades. Moreover, globally, as people's living standards improve, keeping pets has gradually become a common lifestyle. Pets not only provide emotional companionship but also improve the quality of human life to a certain extent. However, as the number of pets continues to grow, health issues related to pets are becoming increasingly prominent, among which bacterial infections are particularly notable.

title: TasAnchor:A Whole-Cell Immobilization Platform
text: TasAnchor:A Whole-Cell Immobilization Platform. Although engineered bacteria hold great potential for wastewater remediation, their practical application is constrained by operational challenges such as easy washout, poor stability, and low cell density. To overcome these limitations, we developed TasAnchor, a whole-cell immobilization platform built on the chassis of Bacillus subtilis. By repurposing the endogenous biofilm protein TasA as a genetically engineered molecular anchor, TasAnchor dramatically enhances cellular adhesion and biofilm formation capacity of the engineered host on surfaces such as polystyrene filters.We further engineered TasAnchor into a multifunctional cadmium-management platform capable of the simultaneous monitoring, adsorption, and recovery of Cd²⁺ ions in real-time. For biocontainment, a quorum sensing-activated suicide circuit was integrated to trigger cell death upon accidental release. Central to its design is modularity, allowing for the exchange of adhesive proteins to facilitate flexible adaptation to diverse remediation scenarios, thereby underscoring the platform's versatility and broad application potential.

title: SALTY: A Salt-Inducible TYDV System for Efficient DENV-2 Subunit Vaccine Production in Tobacco
text: SALTY: A Salt-Inducible TYDV System for Efficient DENV-2 Subunit Vaccine Production in Tobacco. Biomanufacturing of therapeutic proteins and vaccines faces high costs and scalability limitations, posing challenges for dengue vaccine production in low- and middle-income countries such as Indonesia. To address this, we designed an expression system that enables spatially and temporally controlled, high-yield vaccine production by combining the replication mechanism of the Tobacco Yellow Dwarf Virus (TYDV) with the salt-inducible promoter pPdDREG1B for the controlled expression of the DENV-2 envelope protein subunit domain III (EDIII). To expand our repertoire of salt-inducible promoters, we developed NiSPOT, a software tool that classifies and identifies promoters inducible by various stressors, including salt stress. The vaccine protein was optimized using an ESM2-based mutagenesis model to enhance stability. Construct assembly was performed using Golden Gate Assembly and verified via Oxford Nanopore sequencing, followed by transient expression in Nicotiana tabacum through Agrobacterium-mediated agroinfiltration. This system enables precise, inducible control of vaccine protein production in plants.

title: Oral Health Guardian: Engineered Lactobacillus for Real-Time Monitoring of Dental Caries and Biofilm Removal
text: Oral Health Guardian: Engineered Lactobacillus for Real-Time Monitoring of Dental Caries and Biofilm Removal. Dental caries is the most common oral disease, with an incidence rate exceeding 70% in the population. The biofilm of dental plaque, formed by Streptococcus mutans (S.m.) and other bacteria, minerals, and food debris through co-aggregation adhesion, is the main culprit in the development of caries. It is particularly concerning that due to a lack of oral health education, the public often fails to recognize the early symptoms of caries. Early caries in hidden areas are even harder to detect, exacerbating the problem. To address these issues, our team has designed a biological system capable of locating and eliminating high-risk plaque biofilms. Specifically, we've integrated the signal reception module of the quorum sensing system, Com system, from S.m. into probiotics (Lactobacilli), creating engineered bacteria. Additionally, we've developed a unique signal amplification system. When the co-aggregated engineered bacteria within the biofilm receive virulence signals from S.m., they trigger the expression of fluorescent proteins and antimicrobial peptides, thereby enabling the localization and elimination of plaque.

title: DiagSyn: Synthetic Multiepitope Proteins for the Accurate Diagnosis of Arboviral Infections
text: DiagSyn: Synthetic Multiepitope Proteins for the Accurate Diagnosis of Arboviral Infections. Dengue, Zika and chikungunya are serious diseases that are spreading worldwide. Although they are currently most prominent in tropical countries, outside travelers can get back home with the disease. Diagnosis is still challenging due to the genetic similarity among Zika (ZIKV), Dengue (DENV), and Chikungunya (CHKV), which cause similar symptoms (fever, muscle pain), and current serological assays are non-specific, significantly hindering proper patient treatment and effective epidemiological control. In this project, by utilizing synthetic biology, we will eliminate the non-specific interactions that cause cross-reactivity in current serological tests. The design of DiagSyn integrates bioinformatics-driven epitope selection with rational linker design, together with the use of structural biology and molecular dynamics tools,  to generate diagnostic antigens that accurately reflect the circulating strains while excluding conserved cross-reactive sequences, enabling highly specific detection.

title: VERDE
text: VERDE. Soilless agriculture has been an agricultural market on the rise, which yields up to 50% higher efficiency than soil-based cultivation.  VERDE is an antifungal detector that works against fusarium, a common fungus that causes fungal root rot, which poses a significant threat to soilless agriculture. To enhance the specificity of detection and mitigate the scale constraints, VERDE engineers plasmid of E.coli  detects low acidity below 4.5 and indicates the infection of Fusarium. The acid-inducible E. coli asr promoter drives co-expression of genes glutaminase (glsA), β-1-3 glucanase (BGL2), and RsAFP2. These variants in the assembly allows the biosensor to not only detect the presence of Fusarium, but also facilitates its death by producing proteins that disrupts the diffusion of Fusarium: BGL2 and RsAFP2.

title: AQus-HIM - A Quorum-Sensing Biosensor Kit For Hunting Invisible Microplastics
text: AQus-HIM - A Quorum-Sensing Biosensor Kit For Hunting Invisible Microplastics. Identification of microplastics in complex environmental matrices remains a challenge. In this study, we engineered a whole-cell biosensor based on the quorum sensing regulatory circuit LasI-LasR in P. aeruginosa with a reporting module that expressed a LacZ gene. The results demonstrated that our engineered biosensor pSB1C3-LasR-pLasR3-LacZ was highly sensitive to the AHLs with EC50 values as low as 1.0 X 10-8M with N-3-oxo-decanoyl L-homoserine lactone (C10-HSL) and 3.2 X 10-8M with N-3-oxo-dodecanoyl L-homoserine lactone (3OC12-HSL) upon 2 h incubation. The values lie within the average range of AHL concentrations in water environments. Besides, the engineered biosensor is found to be functional in the real tap water environment and seawater without significant matrix effect. In addition, we engineered negative control biosensors by removing the sensing module to reduce background expression of β-galactosidase activity. Moreover, we developed protocol of quantitative X-gal assay which can be used as a testing kit.

title: TRIAGNOSTICS: Spotting Remission is our Mission
text: TRIAGNOSTICS: Spotting Remission is our Mission. Breast cancer incidence is rising, primarily in women under 44. Despite being 10% of breast cancer cases, TNBC, a rare and aggressive form, has a higher rate of death (40% of breast cancer-related deaths) and recurrence (~40% of patients) compared to other breast cancers. The absence of progesterone, estrogen, and HER2 receptors means that traditional therapies are ineffective against TNBC. Patients have the best prognosis if the disease is diagnosed early, so to help detect TNBC recurrence, our team is creating a reusable, efficient, and accessible detector system. Our simple liquid biopsy test has a TNBC patient in remission pricks their finger and apply a droplet of blood to a tube with a simple detection device. In the presence of miRNAs 21 and 155 that are indicative of TNBC, toehold switches allow translation of a fluorescent reporter. Our device will be a significant step forward for at-home diagnostic tools.

title: CoreSpin: Modified Spidroin Proteins as Thermally Conductive Biomaterials for Heat Exchanger Enhancement
text: CoreSpin: Modified Spidroin Proteins as Thermally Conductive Biomaterials for Heat Exchanger Enhancement. Heat exchanger biofouling drives global energy usage and greenhouse-gas emissions. Found in essential infrastructure, heat exchangers contain thermally conductive copper plates prone to biofilm formation, which reduces thermal conductivity by up to 98%, increasing energy consumption. Our solution entails coating copper plates with modified spider silk proteins, produced in E. coli, which maintain plate conductivity and repel bacterial adhesion through their nanostructure. Crystalline β-sheets, flagged by amorphous terminal domains, confer high tensile strength and thermal conductivity to spidroins. β-sheets were modified to maximise thermal conductivity by increasing size. Terminal domains were modified for copper adhesion through addition of cysteine residues. Protein expression was confirmed with fluorescence imaging, and tested by mass determination and sequencing via LC-MS. Copper adhesion and resulting nanostructure were tested with SEM imaging and ATR-FTIR analysis. This research demonstrates spidroin potential beyond biomedical contexts, providing a sustainable, energy-efficient coating contributing to a cleaner climate and sustainable economy.

title: High-Folate Soybeans - Designing the Next Generation of Folate-fortified Crops
text: High-Folate Soybeans - Designing the Next Generation of Folate-fortified Crops. Folate is a vitamin that functions in DNA synthesis, amino acid metabolism, and various biosynthetic pathways. Folate deficiency is directly associated with diseases like neural tube defects, megaloblastic anemia, cleft lip and palate. Globally, folate deficiency has become a serious public health problem. Industrially synthesized folic acid has poor metabolic efficiency, and the synthesis process causes serious environmental pollution. However, plant folate has high active derivatives, good absorption efficiency, and is sustainable. Therefore, the most effective way to supplement folate is food fortification. This project proposes a scheme for creating high-folate soybeans by integrating biosynthetic elements. Four key folate synthetases were over-expressed in soybean seeds. HPLC-MS detection showed that the enzyme HDFR can double the content of 5-methyl-tetrahydrofolate, the active folate component, which is good for people with genetic defects. Our project has successfully achieved expected goals and exerted extensive impacts in scientific research and society.

title: SPARK: Signal inducible protein secretion in mammalian cells
text: SPARK: Signal inducible protein secretion in mammalian cells. Precise control of protein activity is fundamental to cell engineering and underpins the development of advanced cell-based therapies. While transcriptional and translational regulation provide powerful means of control in mammalian cells, post-translational regulation offers distinct advantages by enabling immediate and reversible responses to external stimuli. Here, we present SPARK (Signal-Programmable Activation of Regulated seCretion), which employs engineered molecular anchors to tether secretory vesicles carrying the target protein to the actin cytoskeleton and release them upon signal induction through protein dissociation or cleavage. We demonstrated that SPARK enabled efficient light- and chemically induced secretion of reporter proteins in HEK293T cells, exhibiting a markedly faster response than traditional transcriptional control systems. This platform provides rapid, tunable, and precise control of protein secretion, establishing a versatile foundation for on-demand therapeutic protein production and other applications that require fast and programmable protein release.

title: BioScent: Transforming Lignin Waste into Vanillin through Synthetic Biology
text: BioScent: Transforming Lignin Waste into Vanillin through Synthetic Biology. Our daily lives depend heavily on paper, yet its production and recycling processes inevitably lead to significant lignin waste. We aimed to harness synthetic biology to transform these wasted resources into valuable products. After extensive consultations with experts in policy, industry, and experimental technologies, we engineered Escherichia coli to convert ferulic acid—a representative lignin degradation product—into high-value compounds. We first demonstrated that E. coli could be adapted, via laboratory-accelerated adaptive evolution, to tolerate simulated lignin degradation liquor. Subsequently, by introducing two key enzymes, CtFCS and CUS, into E. coli, we successfully achieved the bioconversion of ferulic acid into vanillin. Our approach features modularity, transferability, and cost efficiency, making it not only technically feasible but also highly promising for practical application. It highlights the potential of engineered microbes as green and efficient tools for resource recovery, contributing meaningfully to the advancement of circular bioeconomy and sustainable development.

title: Developing a self-protecting, peptide-presenting and self-eliminating EcN (PPSE)
text: Developing a self-protecting, peptide-presenting and self-eliminating EcN (PPSE). The microbiome plays multiple functional roles in human health, sparking interest in utilizing probiotics for disease treatment. As microorganisms can be engineered into intelligent living drugs capable of sensing and responding to their environment, they can colonize the gastrointestinal tract, oral cavity, skin, lungs, and tumors to locally deliver therapeutic agents or transport antigens to activate immune responses. However, bacterial toxicity may limit the dosage and efficacy of engineered bacteria. Therefore, we integrated a microbial encapsulation system, an antigen (drug) delivery platform, and a suicide switch within EcN to construct an engineered EcN system capable of self-protection, peptide drug-presentation, and self-elimination (PPSE).

title: ExoAPT-CRISPR: A Targeted Detection Platform for Breast Cancer Exosome Biomarkers
text: ExoAPT-CRISPR: A Targeted Detection Platform for Breast Cancer Exosome Biomarkers. To enable early liquid biopsy for breast cancer, this project developed ExoAPT-CRISPR, an ultra-sensitive and specific integrated detection platform targeting four exosomal proteins (HER-2, PD-L1, MMP-9, EPCAM). The modular platform integrates exosome capture with multistage signal amplification. Magnetic beads conjugated with CD63-specific aptamers achieve efficient, broad-spectrum exosome isolation. Highly active Cas14a protein is expressed and purified via a prokaryotic system, serving as the core detection enzyme. Two isothermal amplification modules, Hybridization Chain Reaction (HCR) and Rolling Circle Amplification (RCA), are designed for each target, converting protein binding events into amplified DNA products. These products function as trigger signals: HCR activates the Cas12a–crRNA complex, while RCA activates the Cas14a–sgRNA complex, enabling reporter cleavage and robust fluorescence generation. This strategy achieves precise molecular recognition and signal conversion, providing an innovative, clinically applicable solution for early breast cancer diagnosis and prognostic monitoring.

title: Floraguard
text: Floraguard. In order to address the rising enviromental crisis of wildfires we set out to create biological flame retardants. We created complexes consisting of a biological flame retardant, a linker domain and then a cellulose binding domain from the cellulosome of Clostridium Thermocellum. These complexes were then expressed in E.coli before being purified and applied to cotton to test their relative flame retardancy.

title: ExoSPY : Exosomes Solutions for Pancreatic cancer
text: ExoSPY : Exosomes Solutions for Pancreatic cancer. Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is one of the deadliest cancers, with a five-year survival rate below 10%. Its silent progression and late diagnosis make early detection extremely difficult, leaving patients with limited therapeutic options. Addressing this major clinical challenge, ExoSPY introduces a novel theranostic approach that combines diagnosis and therapy in a single system. Our project uses engineered extracellular vesicles (EVs) produced from HEK293 cells and loaded with nanoparticles that enable both MRI-based detection and X-ray–activated treatment. These vesicles are designed to specifically recognize precancerous pancreatic cells, allowing precise and less invasive targeting. By detecting pancreatic cancer at its earliest stages and providing localized therapy, ExoSPY offers a promising new avenue to improve survival rates and revolutionize PDAC management through synthetic biology and nanotechnology.

title: Oral, Ultra-long-acting GLP-1-based Therapy with Enhanced Patient Compliance via Gut Probiotics
text: Oral, Ultra-long-acting GLP-1-based Therapy with Enhanced Patient Compliance via Gut Probiotics. This project develops an ultra-long-acting anti-diabetic and anti-obesity therapeutic by engineering the gut probiotic Escherichia coli Nissle 1917 to produce stabilized human-derived GLP-1. Our integrated system employs an AAF sensing circuit for spatiotemporally controlled synthesis, protein engineering with (unnatural) amino acids to enhance circulation stability, an OR-gate biosafety module for programmable biocontainment, and dedicated hardware for intestinal delivery and in vitro characterization. Together, these components enable safe, efficient, and sustained GLP-1 production, offering a novel oral living therapeutic strategy with improved patient compliance.

title: ARALEX - Autocatalyst Recycling via Advanced Leaching Extraction using oXalate
text: ARALEX - Autocatalyst Recycling via Advanced Leaching Extraction using oXalate. Platinum-group metals (PGMs) are critical resources with low recycling rates due to environmentally hazardous and costly conventional leaching processes that rely on harsh chemicals. This project presents an innovative, sustainable approach to PGM recycling using oxalate as a green leaching agent. Our interdisciplinary method combines biotechnological and chemical strategies: genetically modified Corynebacterium glutamicum is engineered to produce and export oxalate into the extracellular environment, providing a biological source of the leaching agent. The chemical process involves dissolving catalyst residues in water, adding the biologically produced oxalate to form PGM-oxalate complexes, and isolating these complexes through water evaporation. This novel biotechnological-chemical approach offers a cost-effective and environmentally friendly alternative to traditional PGM recycling methods, potentially increasing recovery rates while reducing environmental impact. The integration of synthetic biology with green chemistry principles demonstrates a promising pathway toward sustainable critical metal recovery from exhausted automotive catalysts.

title: SynTropica - Biomanufacturing of Pineapple Stem Bromelain Across Three Microbial Hosts for Diverse Industries
text: SynTropica - Biomanufacturing of Pineapple Stem Bromelain Across Three Microbial Hosts for Diverse Industries. Bromelain is a pineapple-derived enzyme mixture with powerful medical, industrial, and cosmetic applications, most notably its ability to selectively remove necrotic tissue in burn wounds through enzymatic debridement. However, extraction of the enzymes from the pineapple stems is costly, inefficient, environmentally unsustainable, and limited by agricultural dependence. SynTropica aims to solve this by producing recombinant stem Bromelain, the main proteolytic enzyme in the mixture, in engineered microbial hosts — Escherichia coli, Pichia pastoris, and Bacillus subtilis. This production approach has the potential to drastically reduce costs, simplify purification, and enable scalable, consistent manufacturing. In the long term, the team envisions programmable microbial systems that not only secrete Bromelain on demand, but can serve as living bio-platforms for medicine, agriculture, and research.

title: The Living Pentacone
text: The Living Pentacone. Coastal defense structures are important in protecting coastal communities from harsh sea conditions, including huge waves and erosion. However, these structures develop microcracks that progressively expand into larger cavities, compromising structural integrity and endangering coastal populations. Our team addresses this challenge through a multi-faceted approach centered on engineered Vibrio natriegens bacteria that employ biocementation to repair microcracks before they develop into structural failures. We have also designed an optimized coastal structure with enhanced hydrodynamic properties to mitigate erosion more effectively. Our pentacone structure features biosensing capabilities that detect changes in ocean pH and the presence of heavy metals, including mercury, cadmium, and arsenic, providing early warning of environmental deterioration. Coastal degradation often occurs in conjunction with plastic pollution and inadequate ecological monitoring. Our solution integrates educational initiatives to address marine plastic waste. This project integrates synthetic biology and community engagement to design systems that work in harmony with natural processes.

title: Rebuilding Babel: Decode Chaos, Unleash Biosynthetic Treasures
text: Rebuilding Babel: Decode Chaos, Unleash Biosynthetic Treasures. In the ancient tale of Babel, a unified language shattered into chaos, mirroring DNA's evolutionary fragmentation across trillions of species. This "genetic Babel" hinders discovering Biosynthetic Gene Clusters (BGCs), vast reservoirs of untapped potential hidden in microbes. NJU-China 2025 defies this curse by rebuilding Babel through two towers: the Genetic Tower (BioSHINAR) and the Cognition Tower (Education Space). BioSHINAR leverages AI for a deeper understanding of DNA across three modules—NIMROD for BGC detection, ORACLE for functional prediction, and PENTECOSTA for cluster integration. Validated via DBTL cycles, it excels in mining terpenoid BGCs that elude traditional benchmarks, enabling the discovery of previously unrecognized secondary metabolites. We've completed a robust business plan, with positive company feedback highlighting commercial promise. Complementing this, Education Space enables designing education programs and exchanges to popularize synthetic biology. Through these innovations, we have successfully rebuilt the Tower of Babel of life, unleashing biosynthetic treasures.

title: Programmable circRNA Switches for Cell‑Type‑Specific Gasdermin‑Based Cancer Therapy
text: Programmable circRNA Switches for Cell‑Type‑Specific Gasdermin‑Based Cancer Therapy. We present Cellective: a riboswitch-based therapeutic platform that selectively targets cancer cells by detecting specific microRNAs and mRNAs, subsequently translating a cellular kill system. This platform is intended to be further developed specifically for the treatment of triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), a particularly aggressive and hard-to-treat form of breast cancer. The selective detection of cancer-specific marker RNAs using the engineered riboswitch RNAs enables a highly specific, minimally invasive therapy that spares healthy cells and is only activated in tumor-relevant contexts. The modular design allows for flexible adaptation to different tumor types and RNA profiles, allowing personalized medicine. We successfully engineered this therapeutic system and confirmed its functionality.

title: Aechmi
text: Aechmi. Sepsis is a life-threatening condition caused by the body’s extreme response to infection. Each year, it affects 49 million people worldwide and causes 11 million deaths, but early diagnosis greatly improves survival. Aechmi emphasizes patient autonomy, equitable access, and well-being. Its design was shaped through engagement with survivors, clinicians, bioethicists, and marginalized communities. Aechmi integrates a CRISPR/Cas13a-based microRNA detection mechanism with a Catalytic Hairpin Assembly (CHA) amplification circuit. In the presence of bacterial sepsis-associated microRNA biomarkers, selected through machine learning-based data analysis, Cas13a triggers CHA. This produces an electrochemical signal, making our system suitable for future integration into an electrochemical biosensor for real-time monitoring of the biomarkers. The proper functioning of the biological mechanism is verified through modeling based on thermodynamic and kinetic analyses of all the reactions involved.

title: The PFAS simple detection and degradation system based on engineered E. coli BL21(DE3)
text: The PFAS simple detection and degradation system based on engineered E. coli BL21(DE3). Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), recognized as "persistent chemicals", exhibit remarkable environmental recalcitrance and widespread distribution in potable water and soil matrices. These compounds pose substantial risks to both human health and ecological equilibrium. Conventional detection methodologies rely on sophisticated instrumental platforms (e.g., liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry, LC-MS), whereas degradation protocols necessitate harsh conditions (e.g., high temperature and pressure), limiting their feasibility for low-cost implementation. Here, we constructed a synthetic biological system in E. coli BL21(DE3) chassis, comprising a PFAS-specific dehalogenation module, a fluoride ion-selective transport apparatus, and a dual-fluorescent reporting system (GFP/mCherry) for integrated real-time visual detection and degradation of PFAS. Furthermore, biosafety is ensured by an arabinose-inducible regulatory circuit controlling the ccdB toxin gene to prevent engineered bacterial dissemination. This approach presents a promising strategy for in-situ bioremediation of PFAS-contaminated wastewater, enabling simultaneous detection and detoxification of these persistent pollutants.

title: Harnessing Synthetic Biology for Healthier Flavors: Expression and Validation of Saltiness-Enhancing Peptides in E. coli
text: Harnessing Synthetic Biology for Healthier Flavors: Expression and Validation of Saltiness-Enhancing Peptides in E. coli. The SaltEnPep project leverages synthetic biology to address the global health challenge of excessive sodium consumption by developing saltiness-enhancing peptides that boost salt perception, enabling sodium reduction in food products without compromising taste. Peptides identified from literature were analyzed using molecular docking and dynamics to predict their interactions with human taste receptors. Selected peptides were cloned into a novel dual-intein chitin-binding domain (CBD) “sandwich” system within the pET-Blank(Kan) vector and expressed in E. coli. The system enabled efficient expression and purification via a thiol-mediated self-cleavage mechanism. Expression conditions were optimized using various IPTG concentrations, and peptide identity and purity were confirmed using Ultra-High-Performance Liquid Chromatography (UHPLC). Sensory evaluation with the ASTREE II electronic tongue showed distinct taste fingerprints and confirmed that peptides enhanced saltiness, especially when combined with NaCl. This work presents the first recombinant, scalable platform for producing salt-enhancing peptides, offering a sustainable solution for sodium reduction in foods.

title: FluBlockers : Synthetic sentry at the nasal gate-variant-proof armor against Influenza
text: FluBlockers : Synthetic sentry at the nasal gate-variant-proof armor against Influenza. Influenza A virus (IAV), characterized by its high mutability and cross-species transmission capability, has triggered multiple global pandemics. Existing vaccines and antiviral drugs face limitations such as short-lived protection, target escape, and drug resistance. To address the critical challenges in respiratory infection prevention, this project employs synthetic biology to engineer nasal-colonizing probiotics (Lactobacillus rhamnosus LGG). By sensing the virus, triggering a cascade response, and ultimately realizing virus neutralization, a multi-module synergistic chain closed-loop defense system is constructed with these probiotics. Additionally, a dual biosafety mechanism is also incorporated, which enables rapid self-destruction triggered by environmental leakage or clinical risk while giving the population the freedom to control intervention. This innovative strategy pioneers a novel synthetic biology-driven approach for influenza control, offering significant public health implications.

title: GRACE: Ginsenoside-Rh1 from Red Algae to Cosmetic Essence
text: GRACE: Ginsenoside-Rh1 from Red Algae to Cosmetic Essence. We developed an innovative, eco-friendly method to produce rare ginsenoside Rh1 using synthetic biology. By engineering yeast with metabolic pathways from red algae, we efficiently synthesize Rh1, avoiding the environmental harm and high costs of traditional plant extraction or chemical synthesis. This sustainable approach leverages abundant marine resources, ensuring high-quality, affordable skincare products like serums. Our breakthrough paves the way for greener cosmetics and unlocks the potential of marine bioresources.

title: R-Home: mRNA Hepatic Optimized Modules for liver cancer
text: R-Home: mRNA Hepatic Optimized Modules for liver cancer. Hepatocellular carcinoma poses a severe global burden, with China accounting for nearly half of all cases. Current therapies face challenges in specificity, resistance, and cost. To overcome these limitations, R‑Home presents an integrated mRNA platform for precise HCC treatment. Our unified mRNA system enables dual-protein regulation, restoring tumor suppressor HNF4α while degrading oncogenic TGF‑β via p-PROTAC. We enhance specificity through GPC3-targeted LNPs and miR-21-responsive RNA switches (exCAG and eukaryotic toehold), ensuring tumor-selective expression. The platform also features optimized 5′UTRs and a spatial PK/PD model predicting drug behavior in tumors. We provide this complete system to the iGEM community, including a standardized Part Collection with optimized UTRs, eukaryotic RNA switches, and targeted delivery components, along with open-source computational models and hardware specifications - collectively advancing the development of accessible and precise cancer therapies,paving the way for accessible and precise cancer therapies.

title: Antibacterial Blue Light Therapy for Gastric Cancer
text: Antibacterial Blue Light Therapy for Gastric Cancer. To combat Helicobacter pylori antibiotic resistance and gastric cancer, we developed an engineered living therapeutic platform. It uses an attenuated H. pylori chassis with natural gastric targeting, integrating luminescence, quorum sensing, and bio-safety modules. Surface-loaded with Chlorin e6 (Ce6) and a lux operon, the bacteria are activated by near-infrared light to generate reactive oxygen species and blue-light phototoxicity, inducing tumor cell apoptosis. A quorum-sensing circuit triggers light emission at a high population density, activating endogenous porphyrins in wild-type H. pylori for a “bystander killing” effect, which also self-regulates the engineered population. For bio-safety, a hypoxia-responsive suicide switch ensures bacterial survival in the stomach but causes programmed death in oxygenated environments. Encapsulated in an oral liposomal delivery system, this platform offers a novel paradigm for overcoming antibiotic resistance and achieving precision gastric cancer therapy.

title: PhAgri
text: PhAgri. Bacteria are widespread, and bacterial crop diseases cause annual devastating agricultural damage. CAU-China 2025 builds PhAgri, a SMART phage-like particle (PLP) platform：it can precisely target and kill pathogenic bacteria without accidentally harming other. Meanwhile, since PhAgri has no self-replication ability, its safety is effectively guaranteed. Using E. coli MG1655, we developed a delivery system, tail fiber replacement platform, and Alphage software for flexible antibacterial spectrum reprogramming. We hope that when PhAgri moves beyond the laboratory, it can be cultivated and used independently by farmers. By providing them with eco-friendly and highly effective pesticides, PhAgri will align with multiple Sustainable Development Goals. In the future, we anticipate that PhAgri will not only safeguard food security, but also enable the synthesis of artificially designed bacteriophages through predictive modification of tail fiber proteins—ultimately solving all potential bacterial problems.

title: Enteroplastivore
text: Enteroplastivore. With the widespread use of plastic products, a large amount of plastic waste gradually decomposes and breaks down, forming plastic fragments with a diameter of less than 5 millimeters, namely microplastics. Microplastics are difficult to decompose naturally and gradually accumulate in the human body. Microplastics can cause imbalance in the intestinal flora, trigger systemic inflammatory responses, and even potentially lead to tumors and cancers. Regarding the issue of how to remove microplastics from the human body, our team proposed to construct a symbiotic system of lactic acid bacteria and yeast, which secretes degrading enzymes to degrade the microplastic particles in the intestinal tract. In addition, this system can also regulate the balance of intestinal flora, enhance the intestinal barrier function, and reduce the oxidative stress caused by microplastics through antioxidant effects, thereby minimizing the possible damage to the body caused by microplastics.

title: A.L.G.E.A
text: A.L.G.E.A. Heavy metal pollution poses a growing threat to both ecosystems and human health due to industrial activity. To address this challenge, our iGEM team is engineering the cyanobacterium Synechocystis sp. PCC 6803 as a sustainable platform for heavy metal bioremediation. We have introduced genes encoding phytochelatin synthases (PCSs) and metallothioneins (MTs) under a urea-inducible promoter, enabling the cells to efficiently chelate and reduce metals ions such as cadmium, lead, zinc, and copper into nano particles. To reduce the harvest cost, we developed a self-aggregation system by inducing limonene production, allowing for energy-efficient and chemical-free biomass recovery. In parallel, we are expressing PCS and MT genes in the moss Physcomitrella patens to compare bioremediation performance in different chassis.

title: The development of a proof of concept for a continuous lactate monitor
text: The development of a proof of concept for a continuous lactate monitor. Our aim is to develop a wearable biosensor that continuously monitors lactate concentration in the interstitial fluid. The current method to measure lactate levels widely used by professional athletes requires blood sampling through invasive needles and the use of disposable strips, disrupting training flow. Building on the success of continuous glucose monitors, our device will embed lactate‐oxidizing enzymes (e.g., lactate dehydrogenase) within a microneedle array to catalyze lactate in dermal interstitial fluid into pyruvate and hydrogen peroxide. An integrated electrode will then oxidize the generated hydrogen peroxide, producing electrons whose current correlates directly with lactate concentration. By tracking these electrical signals in real time, athletes can optimize training and recovery on the run while reducing recurring costs and biological waste. During our project, we have expressed and immobilized the enzyme and verified them through electrochemical detection techniques to present a proof on concept.

title: CinderLight——Enzymatic Upcycling of PET Waste and Kitchen Waste to Supramolecular Phosphorescent Materials
text: CinderLight——Enzymatic Upcycling of PET Waste and Kitchen Waste to Supramolecular Phosphorescent Materials. Facing the dual environmental challenges of plastic pollution and food waste, this project proposes an innovative green upcycling strategy. We employ highly efficient biocatalysts—TurboPETase and cyclodextrin glycosyltransferase (CGTase)—to depolymerize waste PET plastic into a terephthalic acid (TPA) derivative and convert starchy kitchen waste into β-cyclodextrin (β-CD), respectively. Subsequently, these two products are assembled via supramolecular host-guest interactions to form a novel PPA-CD supramolecular phosphorescent material. This entire process operates under mild conditions, achieving the green and high-value valorization of two low-value waste streams into a functional material. It pioneers the simultaneous integration of plastic and food waste within a single system, offering a new pathway for sustainable material development and waste resource utilization.

title: Detective  engineering bacteria: Let Pseudomonas aeruginosa have no place to hide in water.
text: Detective  engineering bacteria: Let Pseudomonas aeruginosa have no place to hide in water.. Escherichia coli was genetically engineered to construct a dual-modal biosensor responsive to quorum sensing signaling molecules. The engineered bacteria carry a Pseudomonas aeruginosa-specific promoter that drives the expression of β-galactosidase and β-glucuronidase, which hydrolyze the substrates ONPG (o-nitrophenyl-β-D-galactopyranoside) to produce a yellow color and MUG (4-methylumbelliferyl-β-D-glucuronide) to emit fluorescence, respectively. This enables the qualitative and quantitative detection of Pseudomonas aeruginosa.

title: AGEs Robber: Restoring Freedom for Diabetic Foot Ulcer Patients
text: AGEs Robber: Restoring Freedom for Diabetic Foot Ulcer Patients. Diabetes affects 589 million people globally, with 18.6 million new DFU cases yearly. DFUs cause infection, necrosis, and amputations, severely impacting life quality. Our project, AGEs Robber, integrates treatment and prevention. We created a hydrogel patch using soluble RAGE (sRAGE) to capture AGEs, reduce chronic inflammation, and promote healing while offering antibacterial and exudate-absorbing functions. For prevention, we conducted community outreach and designed a simple foot-monitoring device for early wound detection. This approach aims to reduce infection and amputation risks, healthcare costs, and improve DFU patients’ quality of life.

title: Temperature-controlled One-step Synthesis of Colored Bacterial Cellulose
text: Temperature-controlled One-step Synthesis of Colored Bacterial Cellulose. The textile industry, as an important sector of fashion industry, is the second largest pollution source in the world. Traditional textile manufacturing processes, which separate fiber production from dyeing, are highly water-intensive and incompatible with the principles of sustainable fashion. To address these challenges, our project developed an integrated system for bacterial cellulose weaving and dyeing using E.coli. We have achieved one-step synthesis of colored bacterial cellulose through temperature regulation. This project aims to overcome the limitations of bacterial cellulose expressed in E.coli and endow it with hydrophobic properties. It provides a solution for the fashion industry that integrates functional aesthetics with environmentally friendly choices.

title: REACT - A Highly Sensitive Aptamer Based Biosensor for the Detection of Renal Distress
text: REACT - A Highly Sensitive Aptamer Based Biosensor for the Detection of Renal Distress. Globally, 15% of all kidney transplants face acute rejection, often before symptoms are noticeable. Contemporary detection methods are often done too late and face tradeoffs between invasiveness, accuracy, portability, and cost-effectiveness. We present REACT, a portable and highly sensitive point of care diagnostic for the early-onset detection of kidney rejection. REACT senses two known biomarkers of kidney distress, NGAL and CXCL-9, and uses Rolling Circle Amplification to boost signal output. A G4 DNAzyme functionalized on a reduced Graphene Oxide surface coupled with paper microfluidics allows for a multiplexed colorimetric detection, facilitated by our smartphone app to quantify and interpret the readout. Given the portable nature of REACT, users can use it outside of a hospital setting, allowing for early at-home detection of kidney rejection. This shortens the length of post-transplant hospital stay and decreases the risk of complications resulting from an untreated rejection.

title: A Bio Synthesis Ode to Van Gogh's Irises
text: A Bio Synthesis Ode to Van Gogh's Irises. iRIS is a living ode to Van Gogh's Irises—where synthetic biology becomes a brushstroke, and engineered E.coli bloom in chromatic light. Guided by refined RGB-sensing circuits, these microscopic artists synthesize 6,6'-dibromoindigo, 4,4'-dinitroindigo and indigo, under precise red/green/blue illumination, painting not merely pigments, but a symphony of co-creation with life. Beyond its aesthetic beauty, iRIS bridges synthetic biology and aesthetic education, transforming laboratories into studios where genes and colors compose together. By lowering the threshold of art-making through living systems, we seek to reimagine bio-art as a democratic form of creativity, accessible to diverse communities. Our project thus highlights both the technical feasibility of programmable pigments and the cultural value of engaging the public in a dialogue between life sciences and the arts.

title: EnzyCaps
text: EnzyCaps. Digestive health disorders affect millions worldwide, posing a major public health challenge. While digestive enzyme supplements offer temporary relief, they are often unsustainable, unscalable, and may trigger allergenicity.
