To address this, we developed EnzyCaps—a biomanufacturing platform that uses bacterial microcompartments (BMCs) within recombinant E. coli to produce and encapsulate digestive enzymes. Our system integrates three key features: a tightly inducible promoter for precise gene regulation, BMC-based compartmentalization, and peptide tags for targeted enzyme encapsulation. This living micro-factory enables modular, tunable, and sustainable enzyme production, overcoming limitations of traditional plant- or animal-based sources. EnzyCaps represents a step forward in sustainable synthetic biology, combining stability, efficiency, and scalability for improved digestive wellness and energy enhancement.

title: Enzymatic Control using Logic-Based Inducible Promoter System Engineering
text: Enzymatic Control using Logic-Based Inducible Promoter System Engineering. Many biological systems are limited by regulation and functionality. Conventional inducible systems that rely on conditional control tend to be stochastic and offer little tunability. Furthermore, many wild-type enzymes display poor catalytic efficiency or stability when expressed in heterologous hosts.  Here, we present ECLIPSE (Enzymatic Control using Logic-Based Inducible Promoter System Engineering), a genetic framework that integrates multi-layered regulation with synthetic enzymology. We combine inducible repressor-operator systems with CRISPRi-based dCas9-sgRNA repression to achieve both conditional ON/OFF switching and fine-tuned, graded control of gene expression respectively. We also optimised our effector enzyme through two complementary approaches – host optimization and rational mutagenesis.  We then apply this framework to treat hypercholesterolemia, engineering E. coli Nissle to express ECOP170 for the in-situ breakdown of dietary cholesterol. Our probiotic platform thereby acts as a proof-of-concept that bridges precise genetic regulation with optimized enzymatic function, offering a generalizable strategy for designing programmable and robust systems.

title: Hepzero: supressing the expression of HBV genes
text: Hepzero: supressing the expression of HBV genes. 254 million people are living with chronic HBV. Every thirty seconds, HBV silently takes one life. A vaccine exists, and it works. But what about people already living with HBV? For them, there is no cure. The reason lies in a molecular structure called cccDNA, it can persist for years in the nucleus and is untouched by immune responses or existing therapies. This persistence is what makes HBV so difficult to cure. But we’ve engineered a system to change that. Hepzero is a dual-CRISPR design that targets cccDNA. Two engineered guide RNAs pair through a kissing loop to bring two dCas proteins to key regulatory regions. These RNA–RNA interactions greatly increase the chance of precise, simultaneous binding, enabling safer repression of viral activity. In this way, we block HBV gene expression and replication without cutting DNA, leaving the host genome unharmed, aiming for a one‑time intervention rather than life‑long therapy.

title: SynBeeGee
text: SynBeeGee. Bees are vital to global food production, yet their populations are collapsing at alarming rates. One of the main culprits is organophosphate pesticides, which disrupt bees' nervous systems and drive widespread colony losses.  Our project, SynBeeGee, tackles this crisis by working directly with the bee gut microbiome. We focus on Snodgrassella alvi, a natural and stable gut symbiont, and engineer it using recombinant DNA methods to carry the organophosphate degradation (opd) gene. This gene encodes an enzyme that breaks down toxic pesticides into harmless byproducts, reducing their deadly impact on bees.  Through Golden Gate Assembly and electroporation, we introduce this genetic circuit into S. alvi, creating a living pesticide-detoxifying partner. Unlike external treatments, this microbial ally persists inside the bee, spreads throughout the hive, and transfers engineered traits to offspring microbiomes, extending protection across generations. SynBeeGee offers a sustainable, self-sustaining defense for pollinators, agriculture, and the ecosystems we all depend on.

title: MAMORI: Modular Agricultural Monitoring for On-Site Rapid Pest Identification
text: MAMORI: Modular Agricultural Monitoring for On-Site Rapid Pest Identification. Mangoes are both culturally and economically vital for Okinawa, small islands in southern Japan. However, Okinawan mango production is now under serious threat from yellow tea thrips. To address this challenge, our team developed MAMORI: Modular Agricultural Monitoring for On-site Rapid Pest Identification.   MAMORI enables strain-level discrimination of thrips—essential for selecting effective pesticides—as well as early, unmanned detection, outbreak prediction, and coordinated island-wide strategy formulation.   Our system combines LAMP-based molecular detection with a paper-based microfluidic device. We also designed automated hardware to trap insects, extract DNA, analyze results, transmit data, and replace test papers without human intervention. Furthermore, we built a predictive model that integrates outbreak data across Okinawa to forecast thrips population dynamics.   With MAMORI, we aim to protect Okinawan mangoes, support sustainable agriculture on small islands, and provide a model for scalable, community-driven pest management.

title: Microbial Biosynthesis of Triterpenoid Ambrein Using Engineered Escherichia coli
text: Microbial Biosynthesis of Triterpenoid Ambrein Using Engineered Escherichia coli. Ambergris, a rare fragrance fixative produced in the digestive tract of sperm whales (Physeter macrocephalus), is highly valued in perfumery but raises ethical and environmental concerns due to its scarcity and link to illegal trade. To address this, Team VIT-Vellore aims to biosynthesize ambrein, the key triterpenoid component of ambergris, using engineered Escherichia coli. By integrating squalene synthase, squalene-hopene cyclase, and tetraprenyl β-curcumene cyclase into the MEP pathway, our system converts farnesyl pyrophosphate (FPP) into ambrein through a renewable, controlled process. This bio-based approach provides an ethical, consistent, and eco-friendly alternative to whale-derived ambergris. Aligned with UN SDGs 12, 14, 4, and 17, our project fosters responsible innovation, marine conservation, education, and inclusivity. Through open-access learning and interdisciplinary collaboration, VIT-Vellore envisions a future where biotechnology unites sustainability, ethics, and creativity to transform the fragrance industry.

title: HepaSwitch
text: HepaSwitch. Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is one of the most common and lethal cancers, with limited effective therapies. Our project, HepaSwitch, aims to develop a selective mRNA-based therapeutic system that induces pyroptosis exclusively in HCC cells. The system utilizes a toehold switch—a synthetic RNA regulator—designed to recognize HCC-specific biomarkers, such as alpha-fetoprotein mRNA. Upon detection, the switch activates translation of gasdermin, a pore-forming protein that triggers pyroptotic cell death. Using computational modeling, we optimized the toehold switch structure for minimal leakiness and high dynamic range. Experimental validation in vitro demonstrated specific activation in the presence of the target RNA and no significant expression in its absence, confirming its precision and safety potential. HepaSwitch represents a novel approach to RNA-based precision oncology, offering a programmable and modular framework for targeted cancer treatment adaptable to various tumor types.

title: FABRIC——Fabrication through Advanced Bioengineered Resources and Integrated Chromatics
text: FABRIC——Fabrication through Advanced Bioengineered Resources and Integrated Chromatics. The expression of style and personality through fashion colors is often shadowed by the heavy discharge of wastewater and the reliance on toxic fixatives. Our FABRIC project, however, utilizes synthetic biology to envision a cleaner, greener future. We engineered yeast strains to synthesize primary bio-dyes and developed a protein mordant that binds these dyes tightly to the fabric, effectively replacing chemical fixatives. Finally, the yeast's light-inducible system work in concert with our custom-developed hardware to empower users in realizing their ultimate fashion vision, establishing a truly sustainable dyeing solution.

title: REDAPT: Retron-Engineered Degranulation Alleviation Platform for Therapeutics
text: REDAPT: Retron-Engineered Degranulation Alleviation Platform for Therapeutics. The University of Oregon iGEM 2025 team introduces REDAPT, a novel therapeutic platform that uses retrons to synthesize therapeutic DNA aptamers in-vivo to mitigate gut inflammation in Mast Cell Activation Disorders (MCAD). The project involves three engineering goals. First, a histamine-sensing circuit regulates aptamer secretion using a characterized histamine riboswitch in a cell lysis system. Second, retrons are engineered to reverse transcribe ssDNA aptamers inside bacterial cells; a fluorescent aptamer expressed within a modular Eco-2 retron cassette serves as proof of concept. Third, a histidine permease from Pseudomonas putida is expressed to transport histamine into cells, triggering aptamer release. Together, these components allow engineered bacteria to accumulate and secrete ssDNA aptamers in response to high levels of histamine. With further refinement, REDAPT could be used to deliver therapeutic aptamers such as X35 in situ in the gastrointestinal tract.

title: Metabolic Engineering of Saccharomyces cerevisiae for the Biosynthesis of Linalool (3,7-dimethylocta-1,6-dien-3-ol) and Nerolidol (3,7,11-trimethyl-1,6,10-dodecatrien-3-ol)
text: Metabolic Engineering of Saccharomyces cerevisiae for the Biosynthesis of Linalool (3,7-dimethylocta-1,6-dien-3-ol) and Nerolidol (3,7,11-trimethyl-1,6,10-dodecatrien-3-ol). Adolescent anxiety has become a pressing public health concern, with Greece reporting the highest rates of anxiety in the European Union. Current pharmacological and therapeutic approaches are often limited by side effects, accessibility, or cost, highlighting the need for innovative alternatives. We aimed to engineer Saccharomyces cerevisiae to produce linalool and nerolidol, two naturally occurring terpene alcohols, known for their anxiolytic properties. We introduced overexpressed Erg20p and AcNES1 into Saccharomyces cerevisiae BY4741. Following fractional distillation between 78–131 °C the desired compounds were purified and steamed for our essential oil. This exploration provided insights into the feasibility of producing these terpenoids in yeast and highlighted considerations for further optimization. This approach offers a potential foundation for developing cost-effective and sustainable methods to support natural interventions for adolescent anxiety.

title: LumaManta: a one-stop, continuous, spatiotemporal aquatic information-detecting device for ecological system.
text: LumaManta: a one-stop, continuous, spatiotemporal aquatic information-detecting device for ecological system.. To better PROTECT, we must first DETECT. LumaManta, developed by ZJU-China, is an all-in-one bio-intelligent underwater device for continuous spatiotemporal detection and treatment of aquatic environments. Aiming to advance environmental conservation, it integrates four biological modules—Detection, aTF Production, Treatment, and Algae–Bacteria Symbiosis—within a manta-ray-inspired body to achieve autonomous ecosystem monitoring. The Detection Module employs a cell-free biosensing system using DNA strand displacement, and PSR amplification to detect metal ions, biomolecules, and eDNA in real time. The aTF Production Module applies AI-assisted protein reprogramming to expand sensing specificity, while the Treatment Module uses protein scaffolds for pollutant absorption and molecular collection. The Symbiosis System maintains a cyanobacteria–E. coli co-culture for CO₂ fixation and nutrient cycling, enabling sustainable, long-term operation. LumaManta represents a new paradigm for bio-driven conservation technology—turning detection into the first step toward sustainable protection of aquatic life.

title: HpBusters: Engineered Probiotic Yeast Equipped with the Target–Adhere–Eradicate System
text: HpBusters: Engineered Probiotic Yeast Equipped with the Target–Adhere–Eradicate System. Halitosis, nausea, and bloating—these are discomforts that people with Helicobacter pylori (Hp) infection suffer from every day. As the culprit of chronic gastric diseases, Hp has infected over half of the global population. In 2025, integrating probiotic engineering with micromotor delivery, the Peking team constructed HpBusters. The sensing-and-therapy system and the adhesion system were designed and implemented in genetically modified Saccharomyces boulardii to sense the biomarker Nα-methylhistamine, and while adhered to Hp, to secrete the biofilm-degrading enzyme AiiA. Micromotors, based on calcium carbonate, propel the encapsulating pH-responsive microgels through the gastric mucus barrier, releasing probiotics directly at infection sites. Models were established to comprehensively evaluate and simulate the efficiency of HpBusters across all processes. Human practices were conducted to forge connections between our project and society. We hope this antibiotic-free strategy enables targeted reaction, biofilm eradication and long-term protection, offering Hp-infected patients a comfortable yet effective therapeutic alternative.

title: Healing Fish Hearts with Leech Medicine
text: Healing Fish Hearts with Leech Medicine. Heart disease is the number one cause of death in humans. But fish can also suffer from heart problems-especially in fish farms, where sick fish often go unnoticed. Many fish die from blood clots inside their bodies, and farmers cannot easily tell what caused it. Our team is studying a special molecule called hirudin, which comes from leeches. Hirudin stops blood from clotting and has been used to treat human heart disease for over 100 years. We want to know: can hirudin also help fish? We Identified hirudin genes from 12 types of leeches. We then converted these genes into genetic parts that can be used by all iGEM teams to do research on. Our own research shows that synthetic hirudin from these genes have the potential to help fish live longer and healthier lives in farms. We hope it will improve fish farming around the world.

title: V-CHARGEs: VLP-Coupled High-efficiency ATP Re-Generating Enzyme system
text: V-CHARGEs: VLP-Coupled High-efficiency ATP Re-Generating Enzyme system. ATP is essential for biosynthetic reactions but costly for large-scale applications. Polyphosphate kinase (PPK) can regenerate ATP from inexpensive polyphosphate (PolyP), yet its industrial use is limited by phosphate inhibition and poor stability. The BNU iGEM team developed V-CHARGEs (VLP-Coupled High-efficiency ATP Re-Generating Enzyme system), an innovative platform that integrates SlPPK with P22 virus-like particles (VLPs) and SpyTag/SpyCatcher coupling to achieve efficient ATP regeneration. By encapsulating SlPPK inside VLPs for protection and anchoring ATP-consuming enzymes outside, V-CHARGEs enables continuous ATP cycling with enhanced pH, portease and phosphate tolerance. This nanoconfined system provides a low-cost, stable, and modular solution for powering diverse ATP-dependent biosynthetic reactions, advancing sustainable biomanufacturing.

title: The Elf Catcher of "Super Fungus"
text: The Elf Catcher of "Super Fungus". To address the "super fungus" Candida auris (multidrug-resistant, highly pathogenic, high mortality), this project uses Acidovorax citrulli’s unique fungus-killing T6SS—unlike most T6SS that only target Gram-negative bacteria. Its structural components are reconstructed in E. coli BL21 as anti-C. auris engineered bacteria, formulated as lyophilized powder and activated via arabinose-containing hydrogel. A pH-sensitive promoter (Pasr) enhances specificity in C. auris’ acidic environment. A pBAD/pDUSK-regulated suicide switch controlling T6SS immunity proteins restricts survival to the hydrogel’s dark, arabinose-rich environment (blue light induces death), ensuring self-elimination outside and allowing controlled death timing. Wet-lab models predict optimal parameters; improved effector delivery boosts targeting, offering an innovative treatment.

title: FloraSynse: Personalized Detection of Vaginal Dysbiosis Using Whole-Cell Biosensors and Electronic Sensing
text: FloraSynse: Personalized Detection of Vaginal Dysbiosis Using Whole-Cell Biosensors and Electronic Sensing. This project aims to advance women’s health by developing an at-home diagnostic tool for continuous monitoring of vaginal health, with a specific focus on bacterial vaginosis (BV), a condition impacting nearly one in three women. Current diagnostic methods provide only a single-timepoint assessment, failing to capture the dynamic fluctuations of the vaginal microbiome. To address this gap, we propose a longitudinal monitoring approach that enables daily sampling and trend analysis. Our prototype integrates two key sensing modalities: a biosensor that detects putrescine, a biological amine associated with BV, and an optical pH sensor that provides complementary information about overall vaginal health. By tracking these biomarkers over time, we aim to generate a data-driven and personalized model of vaginal health, offering users deeper insight into microbiome dynamics and earlier detection of vaginal dysbiosis.

title: Smart Biosensor for Early Detection and Control of Bacterial Wilt
text: Smart Biosensor for Early Detection and Control of Bacterial Wilt. Bacterial wilt, caused by Ralstonia solanacearum, devastates over 400 crops including tomatoes and peppers, with field incidence rates reaching 50–80% in southern China. To address the challenge of hidden early infection, we engineered a smart biosensor that detects the pathogen’s AHL signaling molecules and produces a visible blue signal（indigo） for rapid field diagnosis. In addition, a companion strain synthesizes salicylic acid (SA), a natural plant immune signal, to enhance crop resistance. This low-cost, portable, and farmer-friendly system enables early detection and targeted intervention, providing an innovative solution for managing bacterial wilt and reducing agricultural losses.

title: ReGenstitch：Triple-Engineered Bio-Sutures—Revolutionizing Wound Closure with Strength, Antimicrobial & Anti-Inflammatory Synergy via Synthetic Biology
text: ReGenstitch：Triple-Engineered Bio-Sutures—Revolutionizing Wound Closure with Strength, Antimicrobial & Anti-Inflammatory Synergy via Synthetic Biology. SynSuture addresses the limitations of traditional sutures—poor biocompatibility, infection risks, and non-degradability—through a synthetic biology-driven integration of three functional modules: Bacterial Cellulose (BC) for mechanical strength and biocompatibility; Chitosan/Chitooligosaccharides (COS) derived from shrimp shell waste for antimicrobial and wound-healing effects; and microbially synthesized Curcumin for targeted anti-inflammatory regulation. Using engineered E. coli strains, we produce these components efficiently, creating a multifunctional suture that synergizes structural support, infection control, and anti-inflammatory modulation—all while enabling sustainable biom manufacturing.

title: Strawberry Spoilage Full-Process Prevention and Real-Time Monitoring System
text: Strawberry Spoilage Full-Process Prevention and Real-Time Monitoring System. This project addresses the high spoilage rate of strawberries during post-harvest transportation, where current preservation methods are costly or have limited effectiveness, by proposing an integrated “prevention + real-time monitoring” solution. After harvest, strawberries are sprayed with chitinase and endo-β-1,3-glucanase to degrade fungal cell walls and inhibit infection. During transportation, a VOCs-based whole-cell biosensor constructed from Escherichia coli BL21 (BE3) detects spoilage-related volatile compounds and triggers a fluorescent warning, enabling logistics operators to adjust conditions or remove damaged fruit in time to prevent further spread. This approach leaves no chemical residues, has low production costs, can be integrated with IoT systems, and is suitable for large-scale application—significantly reducing spoilage rates and transport losses, improving freshness, and enhancing both economic returns and food safety.

title: Knotaut – Combating the spread of Japanese knotweed by hijacking its RNAi-pathway
text: Knotaut – Combating the spread of Japanese knotweed by hijacking its RNAi-pathway. Reynoutria japonica, commonly known as Japanese knotweed, is a fast growing and propagating neophyte present in most of Europe, North America and New Zealand that poses a severe risk to local ecosystems and communities. While this invasive plant species is generally susceptible to chemical-herbicidal-agents and physical control methods, both come with 3 key drawbacks. They are either unable to guarantee long term removal, damage surrounding ecosystems or are highly cost, time and/or labor intensive.  Using a modified Escherichia coli strain and a specifically designed dsRNA expression system our goal was to produce dsRNA that is able to post-transcriptionally silence essential genes of R. japonica, ultimately leading to plant death. Additionally, dsRNA encapsulation into liposomes enhances its environmental stability as well as its uptake into and distribution in the plant. Our work had one clear objective: Create an environmentally friendly, species-specific herbicide formulation with dsRNA as its active ingredient - Knotaut!

title: One-Cell Monodrama:Synchronized synthesis of cadaverine-succinate for bio-based polyamide 54 in one E. coli cell
text: One-Cell Monodrama:Synchronized synthesis of cadaverine-succinate for bio-based polyamide 54 in one E. coli cell. Polyamide 54 (PA54)—synthesized from bio-based cadaverine and succinate—is an essential polymer with a wide range of market demand. Conventional biosynthesis requires two separate bacterial strains, leading to complex processes and substantial waste salt generation.  To overcome this, we selected a lysine-producing strain E. coli NT1003 as a basal cell to engineer co-producing cadaverine and succinate from glucose. This enables acid–base neutralization and in situ CO₂ fixation, minimizing neutralizing agents and waste salt. We constructed genetic switches to regulate lysine decarboxylase (CadA) and optimized CadA for efficient lysine-to-cadaverine conversion. Cofactor engineering further enhanced succinate synthesis. By integrating these modules, we created an intelligent cell factory that simultaneously generates cadaverine and succinate from glucose. This sustainable strategy supports green production of bio-PA, promotes public familiarity with bio-based materials, and encourages greener lifestyles.

title: Opio-Rx: Transforming Opioid Diagnostics Through Rapid, Non-Invasive Biosensing Technology
text: Opio-Rx: Transforming Opioid Diagnostics Through Rapid, Non-Invasive Biosensing Technology. The global opioid epidemic kills 600+ people daily—over 500,000 American lives lost since 1999. In India, 2.3+ million people suffer from opioid addiction, with Punjab and Haryana experiencing alarming proliferation. This $500+ billion global economic disaster demands immediate action, yet current detection methods fail when seconds matter most. Existing diagnostics are too slow, expensive, and complex for real-time emergency response, addiction treatment, and law enforcement—creating a critical gap between urgent need and available solutions. Opio-Rx revolutionizes opioid detection with the world's first rapid, point-of-care platform detecting multiple synthetic opioids—fentanyl, oxycodone, methadone, tramadol, and codeine—from saliva in under 5 minutes. Our breakthrough combines computationally designed aptamers with FRET-based biosensing and AI-powered mobile integration, delivering laboratory-grade accuracy anywhere, anytime. This commercial solution healthcare workers, first responders, and treatment providers need. Opio-Rx saves lives by enabling instant, life-or-death decisions preventing overdoses, transforming addiction recovery. Molecular diagnostics starts here.

title: Pullomunch-An E. coli System for Combating Phenanthrene and Naphthalene Pollution
text: Pullomunch-An E. coli System for Combating Phenanthrene and Naphthalene Pollution. PAHs exert persistent toxic effects on both humans and animals. Taking two relatively simple PAHs—naphthalene and phenanthrene—as examples, we aim to engineer Escherichia coli with the nah, phn, and rhl gene clusters from Pseudomonas and other species to establish a more efficient pathway for their degradation.

title: Designing a thermostable monellin variant: A next generation protein sweetener
text: Designing a thermostable monellin variant: A next generation protein sweetener. Sweet proteins offer a natural route to cutting added sugar. Monellin is a protein that is 90,000 times sweeter than sucrose but has limited use due to poor heat and pH stability. Our project aims to modify MNEI, a single-chain engineered variant of monellin, to create a thermostable sweetener that is applicable in real-world situations. An in silico protein design pipeline was developed for systematic design of thermostable MNEI variants. In brief, an exhaustive Rosetta point mutation scan was performed to assess all possible single and double mutations of MNEI. The resulting ΔΔG values were then used to rank mutations by predicting the folding free energy. Subsequently, molecular dynamics simulations were performed to assess the conformational stability of MNEI and its variants. The most stable variants were then cloned into pET-28a(+) and expressed in E. coli NiCo21(DE3) for future experimental validations.

title: NPM Zero
text: NPM Zero. Facing unsustainable traditional hydrogen production, our project pioneers a biological alternative by engineering E. coli into a light-driven biofactory. We integrate synthetic light-harvesting complexes to capture energy, enabling the conversion of formate into clean hydrogen gas through optimized metabolic pathways. Rigorous safety measures, including kill switches, ensure biocontainment. Our integrated approach combines computational modeling with active stakeholder engagement—consulting energy experts, industries, and educators in Hong Kong—to align our solution, "NPM Zero," with urban energy needs and SDGs. By transforming renewable light into sustainable fuel, we advance green biotechnology and contribute to a decarbonized, hydrogen-based future.

title: Plastipeutics - Plastics Shouldn't Come at the Cost of Health
text: Plastipeutics - Plastics Shouldn't Come at the Cost of Health. As plastic waste increases, so does the breakdown of larger plastics into smaller pieces called microplastics. Microplastics can be small enough to be absorbed by the human body and cause harm. Microplastics enter our bodies in three ways: skin absorption, inhalation, and ingestion. The primary mode of absorption is oral ingestion. In the small intestine, microplastics transit through the lining of the intestine and enter the bloodstream to be distributed to other organs. Therefore, we have designed and tested peptides that bind to the plastic polystyrene with the goal of eventually expressing them on the surface of a microorganism which will “grab” plastic particles in the small intestine before they can cause harm.

title: Eco-friendly Bioremediation of Chlorimuron-ethyl Residues for Sustainable Crop Rotation
text: Eco-friendly Bioremediation of Chlorimuron-ethyl Residues for Sustainable Crop Rotation. Chlorimuron-ethyl is a herbicide commonly applied in soybean fields to control weeds. However, its residues can persist in the soil, harming wheat seedlings in subsequent rotations by disrupting root growth, photosynthesis, and nutrient uptake. To address this issue, we engineered E. coli to express the PnBA enzyme, which de-esterifies chlorimuron-ethyl into a harmless benzoic acid derivative. Our product is formulated as a freeze-dried bacterial powder, designed for application after soybean harvest and before wheat planting. By reducing herbicide residues, this solution supports healthy wheat growth, protects soil ecosystems, and promotes sustainable crop rotation practices.

title: PLASMOPROTECTOR
text: PLASMOPROTECTOR. To address the severe harm of exogenous bacterial plant diseases and the issues of drug resistance and pollution associated with traditional chemical control, this project has transformed Escherichia coli (E. coli) into a "cell factory" using synthetic biology. It introduces the PtsG, FabH, and GlnA genes (regulated by T7 promoters and RBS) to construct a synthetic pathway that converts glucose to acetyl-CoA, then to erucic acid, and finally to erucamide. Meanwhile, we developed ErucaBead, which uses high-alcoholysis water-soluble polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) to encapsulate the engineered bacteria and boasts advantages such as rapid dissolution, degradability, and soil improvement.

title: De novo Design, Screening and Application of D-Tagatose-3-Epimerase (DTE) for D-Allulose Production
text: De novo Design, Screening and Application of D-Tagatose-3-Epimerase (DTE) for D-Allulose Production. D-Allulose, a low-calorie sugar with multiple functions, is regarded as a revolutionary natural sweetener. The synthesis of D-allulose from fructose is catalyzed by D-tagatose-3-epimerase (DTE), while the low activity and poor stability of DTE have remained key bottlenecks for industrialization of D-allulose. Our study integrated artificial intelligence models such as LigandMPNN and AlphaFold3 for the de novo design of DTE. A novel RNA-mediated fluorescence system was developed for the high-throughput screening these AI-generated variants, resulting in a novel DTE enzyme with enhanced catalytic activity. The optimized DTE was subsequently applied to the production of D-allulose and other broader societal applications. This study establishes a applicable platform based on “AI Design-Efficient Screening-Application Validation” for enzyme development. It provides a breakthrough enzyme for D-allulose production, benefiting its industrialization and broad social applications in the food and pharmaceutical. It also offers a safe sugar-alternative solution to address obesity and diabetes etc.

title: siREN: A Targeted RNAi Therapeutic Approach Against Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia
text: siREN: A Targeted RNAi Therapeutic Approach Against Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia. siREN is a novel RNAi therapeutic approach for the treatment and management of Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (CLL). By targeting overexpressed proteins (ΒCL2 and BTK) through siRNA-mediated gene silencing, we aim to inhibit the uncontrolled proliferation of leukemic cells and induce apoptosis. Our goal is to suppress the survival pathways driving disease progression, thereby restoring normal cell death mechanisms. This gene silencing will be achieved by delivering siRNAs into cancerous cells via lipid nanoparticles, engineered with antibodies specifically targeting CLL cells. These modified nanocarriers are designed to target ROR1, a protein highly expressed on the surface of target cells, and to release the siRNAs inside them, effectively silencing the genes responsible for CLL pathogenesis, while minimizing interaction with healthy cells.

title: LactoLock
text: LactoLock. The project aims to develop a dual-action oral health therapy by engineering a probiotic bacterium (Limosilalactobacillus reuteri) to produce antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) that selectively inhibit Streptococcus mutans, the primary bacterium responsible for dental caries. AMP production genes will be integrated into the bacterial chromosome using plasmid vectors to express AMPs, with a quorum-sensing synthetic gene circuit regulating expression so that AMPs are only produced in the presence of S. mutans, minimizing disruption to the natural oral microbiome.

title: R.E.Y.N.A. : Radiation-Resistant Engineered Yeast for Nutrition from Astronaut's waste
text: R.E.Y.N.A. : Radiation-Resistant Engineered Yeast for Nutrition from Astronaut's waste. To enable self-sufficient long-term space exploration, regenerative life-support systems must minimize reliance on Earth resupply. While oxygen and water are recycled on the ISS, sustainable nutrient and food production remain challenges. Our project, R.E.Y.N.A, pioneers cellular agriculture for in-situ protein generation from astronaut waste streams, contributing to a closed-loop bioregenerative system. We engineered Saccharomyces cerevisiae to convert urea-rich urine into single-cell protein by deleting the nitrogen catabolite repression regulator GAT1 and overexpressing GLN1 and GDH1, enhancing nitrogen assimilation and amino acid biosynthesis. To ensure resilience under Galactic Cosmic Radiation, we introduced RAD51 and the tardigrade-derived Dsup protein to improve DNA repair and oxidative damage resistance. Additionally, a polyvinyl alcohol–melanin bioreactor lining provides passive radioprotection. Together, these innovations enable a self-sustaining microbial protein production system that promotes regenerative nitrogen recycling and strengthens mission autonomy for deep-space habitation.

title: KUN PENG-The Guardian of Beauty in Cold Conditions
text: KUN PENG-The Guardian of Beauty in Cold Conditions. Cold weather often poses significant challenges to beauty and fashion—from skincare products freezing solid outdoors to concealed door handles becoming stubbornly stuck. Inspired by the freeze-resistance strategies of polar organisms and traditional Chinese culture, the Tianjin team "KUNPENG - The Guardian of Beauty in Cold Conditions" has developed a novel solution. Leveraging synthetic biology and computational modeling, they designed an "Antifreeze Protein-Trehalose Synergistic Defense System." We displayed Antifreeze Protein(AFP) extracellularly via a yeast surface display system. Computational models were then employed to optimize the performance of these proteins and to design novel AFP variants. Through the screening strategy, we identified the trehalose pathway as critical for enhancing yeast frost resistance. Finally, we integrated these elements into a single system, achieving combined intracellular and extracellular frost resistance.  The team's ultimate goal is to integrate this system into cosmetic formulations.

title: Lactate-Induced Vector for Engineered Retinoid Supply & Hepatocellular Onco-Therapy
text: Lactate-Induced Vector for Engineered Retinoid Supply & Hepatocellular Onco-Therapy. Advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) with extrahepatic metastasis has a poor prognosis and limited treatment options. This study evaluated All-trans retinoic acid (ATRA) combined with FOLFOX4 chemotherapy in a nationwide, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial. Prior to the clinical trial, AIVC (Artificial Intelligence Virtual Cell) modeling predicted that ATRA would induce differentiation of tumor-initiating cells (TICs) and reverse chemoresistance. The ATRA+FOLFOX4 cohort showed significantly improved median overall survival (16.2 vs. 10.7 months) and progression-free survival (7.1 vs. 4.2 months) compared to the placebo arm. Experimental validation confirmed that ATRA drives TIC differentiation, remodels the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment by repolarizing M2 macrophages to an M1 phenotype, and inhibits PI3K/AKT signaling. This study establishes ATRA+FOLFOX4 as a novel, effective, and safe first-line regimen for advanced HCC, with its mechanism rationally guided by initial AIVC predictions.

title: LUCID: Lung Cancer Integrated Diagnostics
text: LUCID: Lung Cancer Integrated Diagnostics. LUCID is a two-component diagnostic tool for the early detection of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), consisting of biosensor - OncoSense and AI model - Cancerna.  OncoSense is a optical fiber biosensor for the detection of biomarkers AGR2 and CEA elevated in patients with NSCLC at early stages. Optical fiber base allows for the immobilization of binding ligands, as antibodies or aptamers. Cheap cost of fabrication and rapid detection time make OncoSense promising novel tool for the cancer detection. Cancerna is an AI assistant tool for the analysis of computer tomography (CT) scans. Analyzing CT scans as the 3D image via Lung-RADS implemented classification, Cancerna becomes the everyday tool for the radiologists. Additionally, to explain and justify its output Fuzzy logic is implemented. LUCID has its impact on diagnostic world not only by presenting a new way of diagnostics, but also by improving the work experience with already established ones.

title: SyntcoLAB
text: SyntcoLAB. Human milk oligosaccharides (HMOs) are essential bioactive components of breast milk that support infant immunity, cognitive development, and long-term health, yet current infant formulas provide only a small fraction of their natural diversity. To address this gap, we developed a synthetic biology platform using a modular bacterial consortium of Streptococcus thermophilus, a GRAS (Generally Recognized As Safe), dairy-adapted, and naturally competent chassis. By dividing the HMO biosynthetic pathway among complementary strains, implementing controlled cell aggregation, and establishing metabolic interdependence, we aim to reduce metabolic burden, enhance intermediate sharing, and maintain population balance. This approach is expected to enable the scalable production of a broader spectrum of HMOs than currently available, improving the nutritional quality of formula and establishing a flexible platform for other complex biomolecules.

title: Coliguard: the New Era of UC Treatment
text: Coliguard: the New Era of UC Treatment. Ulcerative colitis (UC) is driven in part by the IL-23 → JAK2/STAT3 axis. Approved anti-IL-23 monoclonal antibodies work but require injections, are costly, and carry systemic immunosuppression risks. We propose localized mucosal neutralization: three de-patented anti-IL-23p19 scFv prototypes (A/B/C) designed by motif-guided CDR engineering with AlphaFold checks, plus two mAb-derived scFv (risankizumab-p19, ustekinumab-p40) as performance baselines. Validation: recombinant-protein ELISA for binding and a Caco-2 inflammation model measuring p-JAK2^Y1007/1008 and p-STAT3^Y705 inhibition. Long-term, the best prototype will be secreted by engineered '''Lactobacillus acidophilus''' to reduce cost and systemic exposure.

title: EcoCasein
text: EcoCasein. In recent years, the environmental impact of greenhouse gas emissions from livestock has drawn increasing global attention, particularly methane released during cattle digestion. To address this issue, the NCHU iGEM team developed EcoCasein, a sustainable microbial milk alternative. Our project employs Kluyveromyces marxianus as a host to produce A2 β-casein, a naturally digestible variant of milk protein, using the PGASO multi-gene assembly system. By introducing carbon-fixation pathways such as the Calvin–Benson–Bassham cycle, we hope to reduce the net carbon footprint of protein production. EcoCasein not only provides a cow-less, easily digestible source of dairy protein but also demonstrates how synthetic biology can contribute to climate-friendly food innovation. Through integrated wet-lab construction, gas analysis, and human practices outreach, our project envisions a new model for sustainable nutrition and low-carbon dairy development.

title: Empowering MTHFR Mutation Diagnosis for Global Healthcare
text: Empowering MTHFR Mutation Diagnosis for Global Healthcare. Birth defects represent a significant challenge in the field of global public health. Among the contributing factors, folic acid deficiency is one of the primary preventable causes. These defects not only endanger individual health but also impose a heavy burden on healthcare systems and society.  Methylenetetrahydrofolate reductase (MTHFR) is a critical enzyme in the folic acid metabolic pathway. Mutations in the MTHFR gene can impair folic acid metabolism, increasing the risk of adverse pregnancy outcomes such as miscarriage and fetal malformations. As a result, MTHFR testing has become an essential component of prenatal screening.   This project is dedicated to developing faster, more cost-effective, and convenient diagnostic methods for folic acid testing and formulating personalized intervention plans for different populations. Through in-depth research on folic acid metabolism and related genes, we aim to reduce the incidence of birth defects associated with folic acid deficiency and safeguard maternal and child health.

title: AleChemy
text: AleChemy. Beer is an important part of our culture, so we began our project by talking with brewers to understand their challenges. From these discussions, we learned that hops are essential mainly for providing bitterness. Guided by their feedback, we focused on reproducing this bitterness in yeast. Using untargeted metabolomics, we identified α-acids as our target molecules for biosynthesis. Through iterative Design–Build–Test–Learn cycles, we introduced a construct into S. cerevisiae that enables the production of phlorisovalerophenone—the precursor of α- and β-acids—verified using both targeted and untargeted metabolomics. Our work was carried out in close contact with breweries, scientists, and the public to ensure responsible design and realistic applications. For the future, we plan to implement additional brewer-desired compounds such as xanthohumol and anthocyanins. Our project demonstrates how synthetic biology can merge innovation with brewing tradition by empowering yeast to produce hop-derived flavor precursors in an environmentally responsible way.

title: R-DetoX 2.0: Synthetic RDX-Induced Biodegradation Genetic Circuit in Escherichia coli within a Serial Bioreactor System
text: R-DetoX 2.0: Synthetic RDX-Induced Biodegradation Genetic Circuit in Escherichia coli within a Serial Bioreactor System. The island municipality of Puerto Rico, Vieques, remains contaminated from decades of military activity with the high-energy compound RDX (hexahydro-1,3,5-trinitroso-1,3, 5-triazine), posing severe risks to human health and local ecosystems. To address this issue, we engineered a genetic circuit in Escherichia coli for RDX biodegradation and biocontainment. The system integrates two modules: (1) a biodegradation module containing an RDX-inducible riboswitch that regulates xplA and xplB, encoding cytochrome P450 and its flavodoxin reductase responsible for degrading RDX into formaldehyde and nitrite, and (2) a killswitch module that detects these byproducts to trigger colicin-mediated cell lysis. The circuit will be implemented in a four-stage Serial Bioreactor System designed to promote bacterial growth, induce degradation, treat byproducts, and ensure safe environmental discharge. Our system provides a controlled and sustainable synthetic biology approach for mitigating RDX contamination and supporting environmental restoration in Vieques.

title: Cas Advancement via Synthetic Protein Engineering and RNA knockdown (CASPER)
text: Cas Advancement via Synthetic Protein Engineering and RNA knockdown (CASPER). CASPER aims to build a standardized backbone for Cas13-based RNA knockdown, enabling fair comparisons across Cas13 variants. For knockdown, we cloned several Cas13b (bt1, bt3, pgu, Ran) and Cas13d (djCas13d) constructs into the xPERT backbone to test RNA cleavage efficiency using ANXA4 and BGALNT1 as the target. Guide RNAs were designed, cloned, and verified through restriction digestion, ligation, transformation, and sequencing. Confirmed plasmids will be transfected for RT-qPCR and editing assays to evaluate both knockdown and editing performance within a unified framework. On the computing side, we built a motif-guided protein generation model showing that conserved motifs reliably mark Cas13 subtypes. The first version (v1) used ESM-2 to generate realistic Cas13d variants that passed structural checks. A second version (v2) incorporated reinforcement learning for subtype precision but produced less natural sequences. v1 offers a practical baseline, while v2 points toward more controlled protein design.

title: Rational modification of HpCrtZ to construct cell factory for astaxanthin synthesis
text: Rational modification of HpCrtZ to construct cell factory for astaxanthin synthesis. Astaxanthin is a potent antioxidant with anti-aging properties and is widely sought after by manufacturers of cosmetics and skin care products. However, current production is low, resulting in high market prices. Our solution is to improve astaxanthin production using Escherichia coli as a cellular factory. For astaxanthin synthesis, the astaxanthin synthesis pathway including seven genes were chosen and they were expressed in E. coli using two T7 promoters of the pET-Duet-1 vector. In addition, we modified β-carotene hydroxylase using rational design, achieving four HpCrtZ mutants with high catalytic activities.Then we induced the expression by IPTG to synthesize astaxanthin in E. coli efficiently. Finally  we obtained astaxanthin powder by freeze-drying, made astaxanthin-containing oil. For applications, we designed three target products including essence, face mask and opera makeup pigments. Our technology is mature, cost-effective and environmentally sustainable. We aim to meet the market demand for high quality astaxanthin through this approach.

title: Engineered MHC Protein for Enhanced Tumor Antigen Visibility
text: Engineered MHC Protein for Enhanced Tumor Antigen Visibility. Current cancer immunotherapies often fail when tumor cells evade detection by downregulating or modifying peptide-MHC presentation. In this project, we present a modular, quantitative engineering platform based on rationally modified HLA-A*02:01 molecules to improve tumor antigen visibility to T cells. We designed and built three heavy-chain constructs (wild type, single mutant W167A, and quadruple Tyr→Ala variant) plus a constant β2-microglobulin part, all with biotinylation tags for tetramerization. Our approach combined in silico structural modeling (diffdock-guided residue selection) with wet-lab validation (SDS-PAGE, BCA quantification, ELISA binding assays). We demonstrated that engineered variants can meaningfully alter peptide binding affinity, confirmed through rigorous measurement pipelines. Alongside experimental work, we conducted public surveys and expert interviews to align our scientific goals with societal perceptions, developing educational modules to bridge knowledge gaps. This project integrates synthetic biology, immunology, measurement rigor, and human practices into a coherent toolkit for future MHC engineering.

title: Avisptosis
text: Avisptosis. Our project aims to construct a novel defense system against avian influenza viruses that currently threaten global food security, utilizing synthetic biology as our primary approach. Rather than developing orthodox defense systems such as drugs or vaccines that inhabit viral entry into cells or viral replication, we are developing an innovative mechanism that prevents viral amplification within animal hosts by "actively inducing apoptosis in cells infected with influenza virus." Our ultimate goal is to suppress highly pathogenic avian influenza(HPAI) pandemics, thereby making significant contributions to improving food security issues and maintaining public health.

title: Epilepsy Shield：BHBio＆EEGSense
text: Epilepsy Shield：BHBio＆EEGSense. Per WHO 2024 data, around 50 million people globally are suffering from epilepsy. The ketogenic diet is effective for epilepsy by prompting the body to synthesize ketone bodies, yet long-term adherence may cause side effects. To avoid these side effects, we use synthetic biology to synthesize ketone bodies for epilepsy treatment. We engineered Escherichia coli Nissle 1917 with a pathway to produce the ketone body β-hydroxybutyrate (BHB), plus dynamic regulation and safety modules. Encapsulated in hydrogel as a drug, the engineered bacteria colonize the intestines after oral administration to synthesize BHB for therapy. We also developed an intelligent epilepsy monitoring system: a concealed behind-the-ear device (cEEGrid) collects EEG signals, which are Bluetooth-transmitted to a model. After software processing, seizure risk is visualized.  Our project aims to provide insights into epilepsy prevention and treatment via synthetic biology, caring for patients.

title: PROMNESIS
text: PROMNESIS. PROMNESIS is a synthetic biology therapeutic platform targeting multiple aspects of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) pathology: (i) intracellular tau pathology, addressed by Tau Tuner  and (ii) extracellular tau “seeds” that spread neurofibrillary tangles, targeted by TRI-LYTAC. Our system's third component, a logic gate for the detection of cellular stress environment, is used as a safety precaution, activating downstream therapeutic expression only in disease-relevant contexts. The TauTuner consists of an optogenetically controlled phosphatase, which performs dephosphorylation of intracellular tau, preventing its aggregation and restore microtubule stability. The TRI-LYTAC is a lysosome-targeting chimera which combines antibodies with TfR-binding peptide and IGF-2(F19L) dimer. Its development was primarily driven by the need to target and degrade extracellular tau seed, as well as to achieve blood–brain barrier (BBB) transcytosis. The experiments performed and models we developed show that PROMNESIS can work as a complete, modular treatment system.

title: FoCas: A Novel Antimicrobial-Resistance Treatment and Infectivity Inhibition Platform
text: FoCas: A Novel Antimicrobial-Resistance Treatment and Infectivity Inhibition Platform. The escalating crisis of transmissible antimicrobial-resistant bacterial infections demands innovative therapeutic approaches that move beyond traditional antibiotics. In response, our team presented the concept of FoCas, a novel platform engineered to directly address the dual challenges of drug resistance and infectivity. FoCas leverages a two-component system: the CRISPR-Cas9 gene-editing system for precise genetic targeting and cleavage, and a DNA origami nanostructure as a smart delivery and targeting vehicle. The DNA origami is programmed to recruit and protect the sgRNA/Cas9 complex, selectively bind to specific pathogen (e.g. MRSA), efficiently enter the cell with subsequent CRISPR-Cas9 activation to precisely cleaves and disables the gene responsible for antibiotic resistance (e.g. mecA). By combining precise genetic disruption with targeted delivery, FoCas may possess great potential as a candidate for future antimicrobial therapy, holding immense promise for dealing with superbug infections.

title: PolyGone: A Synthetically Engineered Fish Feed Additive that Fights Microplastic
text: PolyGone: A Synthetically Engineered Fish Feed Additive that Fights Microplastic. Polygone seeks to improve human health by eliminating the microplastics that have accumulated in our seafood. With synthetic biology, Polygone engineered probiotics can enzymatically degrade plastic in fish guts, helping to create a cleaner diet and a cleaner world.

title: A Protein Engineering Platform for Valuable Plant Metabolite Synthesis
text: A Protein Engineering Platform for Valuable Plant Metabolite Synthesis. Plant natural products are vital sources of medicines and health supplements, but plant extraction results in high costs and limited accessibility. Microbial production offers a sustainable alternative, yet poor stability and low activity of plant enzymes in heterologous hosts remain major bottlenecks. To solve this problem, we here developed REvoDesign, a rational evolutionary-guided workflow that integrates structural modeling with co-evolutionary data to optimize minimal key residues. REvoDesign synergistically enhances enzyme stability and activity with minimal experiments and mitigates negative epistasis via cross-region mutations. A user-friendly interface with customizable modules makes the tool easy to use. REvoDesign’s effectiveness was validated by improving bifunctional phytoene synthase/lycopene cyclase(CarRP) and taxadiene-5α-hydroxylase(T5αH), leading to collaborations with multiple research teams and companies, including a signed strategic partnership. This data-driven, structure-guided approach provides a powerful solution for engineering enzymes to enable efficient microbial production of plant natural products.

title: Team Imperial College London
text: Team Imperial College London. The current model of meat production is environmentally unsustainable. Cultivated meat offers an alternative, yet remains hindered by high production costs, particularly by recombinant growth factors that constitute up to 70% of expenses. We tackle this by engineering a Komagataella phaffii chassis, Mannoless, designed to reduce exopolysaccharide secretion and improve yield through targeted modifications in Hoc1, Rho1, and PMI. We also developed BioKernel, an open-access, no-code Bayesian optimisation framework that accelerates design and strain engineering. Guided by our conversations with world-leading experts across different sectors, we explored unspoken pitfalls of scaling in yeast chassis. Our education efforts addressed skepticism toward synthetic biology, as innovation cannot scale without public trust and investor confidence. Finally, we were on a mission to make our outputs fully open-access reaffirming our belief that science cannot scale without non-proprietary technology. We aimed to remove cost and licensing barriers in biomanufacturing, accelerating a sustainable future for food.

title: No Grain, No Gain: Ferulic-Acid-Induced GLP-1 Secretion for Metabolic Health
text: No Grain, No Gain: Ferulic-Acid-Induced GLP-1 Secretion for Metabolic Health. To advance sustainable and programmable genetic regulation in synthetic biology, we engineered an orally deliverable microbial platform that functionally couple gene expression to dietary metabolites, embodying the principle of Medicine-Food Homology. By incorporating a ferulic acid-responsive regulatory circuit, our system achieves diet-inducible control of target gene expression under physiologically relevant conditions. A stabilized GLP-1 analogue was employed as a model payload to verify the system’s responsiveness and molecular reliability. Operational safety was ensured through a dual-layer safeguard that integrates an engineered bacterial delivery system and a quorum-sensing-based self-limitation mechanism.  Guided by our 5C Human Practices framework, emphasizing co-design and reflective integration, our project demonstrates a responsible and modular approach to system construction. Collectively, this work establishes a versatile and robust platform for translating dietary signals into programmable genetic responses, offering new possibilities for foundational research in metabolic regulation and precision biodesign.

title: HemorrEaser: A Novel Strategy for Treating Hemorrhoids
text: HemorrEaser: A Novel Strategy for Treating Hemorrhoids. Hemorrhoids present significant treatment challenges such as symptomatic relief, surgical pain, and high recurrence rates. Based on sociological research, we developed "HemorrEaser", a synthetic biology therapy. Using engineered E. coli Nissle 1917 in oral and topical formulations, our design features three innovations: OMV-delieverying bioPROTAC-mediated HIF-1α degradation combined with an activatable anti-VEGF nanobody to suppress pathological angiogenesis; ROS-responsive release of anti-inflammatory peptides for rapid pain relief;  a dietary-component-responsive riboswitch enabling medicine-food collaboration for treatment regulation and safety control. HemorrEaser provides a precise, minimally invasive therapeutic strategy while establishing a new chronic disease management paradigm through lifestyle-integrated therapy.

title: NONERGY
text: NONERGY. Our project focuses on hay fever (allergic rhinitis) which is a major burden in our country Japan. We propose two solutions: the biosynthesis of narirutin and the engineering of a fusion peptide. Narirutin is a flavonoid compound found in Jabara, which is a citrus fruit grown mainly in Wakayama prefecture in Japan. This compound has anti-allergic properties, and is proven to be effective for hay fever. Our fusion peptide is mainly made out of three immunomodulatory peptides, connected with cleavable linkers. The fusion peptide is designed so that the linkers cleave at specific parts of the pathway of allergic rhinitis, dropping off certain peptides at certain parts of the mechanism. We also created a new, 100% recyclable nasal spray, as well as conducted many human practices and education initiatives targeting a wide range of people.

title: ChronoKolla
text: ChronoKolla. We have designed a fusion peptide sequence aimed at addressing issues in the field of medical aesthetics. The fusion peptide primarily comprises several functional peptide segments. Firstly, to inhibit melanin production in the skin, we employed computer-aided methods to design a competitive peptide analog of the melanocyte-stimulating hormone receptor (α-MSH), which serves to block melanin synthesis. To delay skin aging and promote collagen synthesis, we incorporated segments that mimic growth factors into the fusion peptide sequence, which can stimulate skin cells to produce collagen. Additionally, we added a cell-penetrating peptide segment to the end of the fusion peptide to facilitate the entry of these compounds into skin cells for effective action. We utilize Escherichia coli DH5α for the production of these fusion peptides and have designed a microneedle-based delivery system to administer these compounds effectively.

title: Seawolves
text: Seawolves. Excessive nitrogen pollution from agricultural runoff, atmospheric deposition (which have increased because of fossil fuel), and other anthropologic activities have led to significant environmental challenges for the marine environment through eutrophication, the overflow of nutrients. Microorganisms reproduce rapidly in the presence of eutrophication to create HABs, or harmful algae blooms. These algae blooms can cover up to hundreds of kilometers, depriving the environment of oxygen and suffocating species into local extinction. Our review of existing nitrogen reduction methods suggests that they are of limited effectiveness.   To address this problem, we formulated a solution to modify marine diatom Phaeodactylum tricornutumlum with a synthetic construct of pPha-T1 and NR gene, which increases the efficiency of nitrate degradation. By enhancing the ability of diatoms to process excess nitrogen, our approach seeks to reduce the nutrient load in marine environments and prevent the uncontrolled growth of harmful algal blooms.

title: RectomeDy FotoZymogen：A Red Light-Programmed Microbial Therapeutic System for Targeted Colorectal Cancer Treatment
text: RectomeDy FotoZymogen：A Red Light-Programmed Microbial Therapeutic System for Targeted Colorectal Cancer Treatment. Colorectal cancer treatment faces challenges such as severe side effects from conventional therapies and a lack of precise, controllable localized treatment methods. To address these issues, we developed RectomeDy FotoZymogen—an engineered bacterial therapeutic system for colorectal cancer based on red light-controlled precise induction. Using the probiotic E. coli Nissle 1917 (EcN) as the chassis, we constructed four core modules: a Targeting Module (INP-HlpA) for tumor-specific anchoring; a Red Light-Induction Module (PadC-MrkH) that enables precise activation of gene expression via 660 nm irradiation; a Therapeutic Module delivering multi-mechanism anticancer molecules such as Coagulase and PD-L1 nanobodies; and a Safety Module ensuring automatic bacterial inactivation post-treatment. RectomeDy FotoZymogen is administered via a suppository with an embedded LED, achieving full-process precision control of "delivery-localization-activation-clearance." This system provides a localized, safe, and highly effective novel treatment strategy for colorectal cancer.

title: Low-burden Dairy Products: Reduced lactose, lowered sugar and Increased fiber
text: Low-burden Dairy Products: Reduced lactose, lowered sugar and Increased fiber. Dairy products are essential for human health. Our project utilizes enzyme engineering and synthetic biology to express two recombinant enzymes: transgalactosidase and glucose oxidase. Transgalactosidase catalyzes the conversion of lactose into galactooligosaccharides (GOS) and glucose, whereas glucose oxidase converts glucose into gluconic acid.  This process not only alleviates lactose intolerance symptoms but also reduces sugar content and enriches prebiotics in dairy products. Ultimately, it achieves lower carbohydrate intake and higher dietary fiber content, providing a healthier dairy option for consumers.

title: Selective Proteolytic Botulinum Toxin Bioassay Based on Yeast (S.P.Y.)
text: Selective Proteolytic Botulinum Toxin Bioassay Based on Yeast (S.P.Y.). Botulinum toxin type A (BoNT/A), needing high-demand detection in medical aesthetics and food safety, prompts us to develop a simplified, accurate, fast, low-cost detection method to replace the traditional mouse bioassay. We use Saccharomyces cerevisiae to build a dual-yeast system: one acts as substrate to sense BoNT activity and release ligands, the other receives signals to express pigments for visualizing BoNT concentration, with coupled GPCR pathway and GAL system for signal amplification. It applies to quality inspection of medical aesthetic products and food safety, boosting efficiency and offering public accessible safety verification. This project can be applied in the quality inspection of medical aesthetic products and food safety testing. It not only improves the quality inspection efficiency of relevant institutions but also provides the general public with an accessible means to verify the safety of daily food products.

title: Development and Functional Analysis of a Lab-on-a-Chip Model for NRAS^G12D Mutant Multiple Myeloma
text: Development and Functional Analysis of a Lab-on-a-Chip Model for NRAS^G12D Mutant Multiple Myeloma. Multiple myeloma progression is driven by genetic alterations; RAS-pathway mutations (e.g., NRAS^G12D) increase proliferation and motility. Conventional 2D cultures miss these behaviors, and animal models are slow, costly, and ethically constrained. We engineered NIH3T3 cells expressing control, NRAS^WT, or NRAS^G12D with an mCherry reporter for direct visualization and genotype validation. Using a PDMS lab-on-a-chip that mimics a bone-marrow-like matrix, we quantified growth (CCK-8) and migration (scratch wound healing vs on-chip Matrigel infiltration). NRAS^G12D accelerated wound closure and enhanced 3D invasion. Treatment with the MEK inhibitor U0126 produced mutation-dependent growth suppression, confirming pathway involvement. Overall, this reproducible 3D chip links genotype to pharmacologic response in a tissue-like context, offering a scalable route to reduce animal use and to speed evaluation of AI-nominated compounds and future co-cultures with stromal or endothelial cells for both mechanism and screening.

title: Glutamate-driven Ferroptosis Induction by Recombinant E.coli in tumor-specific environment
text: Glutamate-driven Ferroptosis Induction by Recombinant E.coli in tumor-specific environment. Current cancer therapies are limited by chemotherapy resistance, target mutations in precision drugs and severe side effects. As synthetic biology develops rapidly in recent decades, bacterial therapy has emerged as a promising alternative. Meanwhile, ferroptosis—a form of regulated cell death driven by iron-dependent lipid peroxidation—has shown significant potential based on previous studies. Our study integrates bacterial therapy with ferroptosis induction by engineering Escherichia coli to overexpress glutamate specifically in tumor microenvironments. Glutamate can disrupt cellular redox homeostasis by depleting glutathione and accumulating lipid peroxides, thus selectively triggering ferroptosis in tumor cells, with colorectal cancer involved in this study. This approach combines synthetic biology with the potency of ferroptosis, aiming to enhance therapeutic efficacy while minimizing off-target effects through microenvironment-responsive expression. We anticipate that it will provide new insights into bacterial cancer treatments, for innovative combination therapies that improve tumor targeting, reduce side effects, and achieve better clinical outcomes.

title: FeliSilence
text: FeliSilence. Cat allergies affect a substantial population globally and are mainly caused by a few feline proteins (e.g., Fel d 1, Fel d 2, Fel d 4, Fel d 7). We developed FeliSilence, an RNA interference (RNAi) approach that silences allergen transcripts to reduce allergy at the source. To quickly and safely test RNAi efficiency, we created an accessible yeast shRNA reporter platform through simple fluorescence readouts—ideal for student teams. Candidate shRNAs were filtered to minimize off-target effects, and in the yeast assay, twelve of fifteen shRNAs demonstrated active knockdown, presenting candidates for further implementation. Human Practices guided our project priority of reversible RNAi over gene editing, and we assessed delivery feasibility through modeling of siRNA activity and lipid nanoparticle (LNP) targeting. To tackle the challenge uniting private sectors, our entrepreneurship plan outlines a feasible pathway, emphasizing safety, regulatory alignment, and clear advantages over symptom-based allergy treatments.

title: Protovate
text: Protovate. Protein engineering underpins modern biotechnology, yet turning designed sequences into robustly functional biomolecules remains inefficient because datasets are small, screening is costly, and sequence–function mappings are uncertain. While the development of large protein models such as Alphafold has advanced structure prediction, consistent performance across diverse conditions is still difficult to achieve. We built a data-free active-learning generative protein-language model framework, Seed & Seek, cooperating with biological directed-evolution (using a coarse-to-fine tuning strategy), spanning both in vitro ePCR mutations and in vivo EcoRep systems. Using the SpyTag/SpyCatcher pair as a testbed, we targeted improved association rates and iteratively validated candidates with split-luciferase assays. By uniting computation with biological selection, our framework accelerates discovery of adaptable, high-performing protein variants.

title: KERBEROS: Key Engineered Response for Binding and Elimination of Residual Orally-internalized Synthetic particles
text: KERBEROS: Key Engineered Response for Binding and Elimination of Residual Orally-internalized Synthetic particles. Microplastics, plastic particles smaller than 5 mm, can bind harmful molecules and commonly cause inflammation and oxidative stress in cells. Due to their polymeric structure, they show high affinity for Carbohydrate-Binding Modules (CBMs), domains found in carbohydrate-active enzymes (CAZymes) that normally bind polysaccharides. The effects of PET, LDPE, and PS microplastics are being studied in Drosophila melanogaster fed with microplastic-enriched food. A genetically modified Saccharomyces boulardii CNCM I-745 strain, engineered to display CBM on its surface using the Aga2p system, is added to the flies’ food to test in vivo microplastic binding and excretion. Yeast viability is evaluated in a bioreactor simulating the large intestine, supporting its potential as a live therapeutic delivery system. Adsorption kinetics are modeled in an in silico intestinal environment, and molecular docking and machine learning (Pythia) are used to predict and optimize CBM–polymer interactions for future experimental validation.

title: GreenAqura
text: GreenAqura. Runoff carries nitrate, ammonium, and orthophosphate that drive eutrophication and waste fertilizer. We propose a modular biocartridge seeded with engineered E. coli encapsulated in alginate. In Capture mode, cells overexpress high-affinity transporters (NarK/P, AmtB, PstSCAB) and polymerize intracellular cyanophycin (CphA) for nitrogen and polyphosphate (PPK1/PPK2) for phosphorus. A burden-aware controller routes ATP and reducing power to storage only when external nutrients exceed setpoints sensed by PhoB/PhoR and NtrC networks. In Recover mode, orthogonal inducers activate CphB and PPX to depolymerize stores; a short elution concentrates N and P into a reusable stream for fertilizer blending. Encapsulation plus genetic biocontainment (auxotrophy + kill switch) prevents escape. Bench targets: 80% NO₃⁻-N removal and 90% PO₄³⁻-P removal within 6–12 h HRT at 10–50 mg/L influent, ≥10 reuse cycles with <5% activity loss per cycle. The system provides edge-of-field polishing with low reagents, nutrient recycling, and strong safety.

title: Living Scaffolds
text: Living Scaffolds. Osteoporosis, which affects hundreds of millions of people, requires safer treatments. To address the serious side effects and high cost of current options, we have engineered E. coli bacteria as a localized, in situ drug factory. Our system uses surface-displayed tyrosinase to continuously produce melanin, a powerful antioxidant that reduces inflammation and promotes bone regeneration at fracture sites. To ensure complete biological containment, the bacteria are encapsulated in a alginate hydrogel and are metabolically auxotrophic, making them dependent on the carrier. A toxin-antitoxin system also prevents plasmid loss and survival outside the niche. This work establishes a foundational platform for a new class of living medicines aimed at bone regeneration. By enabling localized, sustained, and controllable drug delivery, this paves the way for intelligent and sustainable solutions to a wide array of diseases.

title: Project PHoeBe - Achieving a Feasible Plastic Alternative in the Form of PHB
text: Project PHoeBe - Achieving a Feasible Plastic Alternative in the Form of PHB. The growing use of non-biodegradable plastics has caused major environmental harm, as these materials persist for centuries and resist recycling. Polyhydroxybutyrate (PHB) offers a biodegradable alternative, but its slow degradation and recycling limit its effectiveness. In Project PHoeBe, the Westview iGEM team investigates two newly identified enzymes, a PHB depolymerase and a dehydrogenase, found through metagenomic analysis, to improve PHB breakdown. Level 1 plasmids containing these genes were conjugated into knockout Alteromonas macleodii, and tests in a simulated ocean environment showed evidence of PHB degradation. Computational modeling also identified a potential catalytic triad in the depolymerase. Through outreach, we educated the public on plastic pollution, waste reduction, and the environmental promise of PHB. Our project represents an early step toward more effective, sustainable management of biodegradable plastics.

title: SmokeOff: Engineering Enzymes to Block TSNAs Formation from Third-Hand Smoke
text: SmokeOff: Engineering Enzymes to Block TSNAs Formation from Third-Hand Smoke. Globally, more than 1.3 billion people use tobacco. While the dangers of first- and second-hand smoke are widely recognized, third-hand smoke—residual pollutants that settle on clothing, furniture, walls, and dust—remains an underappreciated health threat. Among its most hazardous constituents are tobacco-specific nitrosamines (TSNAs), formed through the reaction of residual nicotine with airborne nitrite. TSNAs are strongly carcinogenic and highly resistant to degradation. To address this, we propose a dual-enzyme strategy: NicA, NicB, and NicC for the degradation of surface nicotine, and NirS, NorB, and NosZ for the removal of environmental nitrite. By preventing TSNA formation at the source, this biosafe and sustainable enzyme-based spray presents a novel synthetic biology approach to indoor environmental detoxification.

title: AbsorBuddy: Cross-Species Recombinant Intrinsic Factors for Enhanced Vitamin B12 Absorption
text: AbsorBuddy: Cross-Species Recombinant Intrinsic Factors for Enhanced Vitamin B12 Absorption. Vitamin B12 is essential for red blood cell formation, neurological function, and DNA synthesis. However, millions of people worldwide suffer from vitamin B12 malabsorption. The most effective treatment currently available is lifelong intramuscular B12 injections, which are often painful, inconvenient, and associated with hidden costs, accessibility challenges, and environmental impact. Our iGEM project, AbsorBuddy, aims to develop a safe and effective alternative oral B12+IF supplement by identifying the most efficient and least immunogenic IF variant across five species. Results of our project reveal that bovine and human IF exhibit the highest vitamin B12 binding efficiency with rat IF showing minimal binding. Antibody interference test indicates markedly lower cross-reactivity for bovine and platypus IF compared to human IF, suggesting reduced immunogenic potential. Circular dichroism confirms native-like α-helical folding in bovine IF. Complementary dry lab analyses, shows experimental binding trends and identify favourable geometric complementarity for bovine and human IF.

title: PATRONUM: PAThogen-Resistant Organisms engineered for NatUral root rot Management
text: PATRONUM: PAThogen-Resistant Organisms engineered for NatUral root rot Management. Soybean root rot, a soil-borne disease primarily caused by Fusarium spp., poses a severe threat to China’s soybean industry—with annual yield losses exceeding 50,000 tons. Conventional controls are inadequate: agricultural measures are slow-acting, chemical pesticides carry risks of residues and pathogen resistance, and biocontrol exhibits weak efficacy. To address this gap, our approach employs two engineered strains: the chitinase-expressing strain degrades existing chitin, destroying mature pathogens; the β-amyrin-synthesizing strain blocks chitin synthesis by inhibiting chitin synthase, suppressing pathogen proliferation. Our team achieved key results: establishing an in-silico workflow to screen 2000 secretory peptides; verifying the chitin-degrading ability of chitinases; constructing and optimizing β-amyrin-producing strains; developing a biosafety screening tool and a measurement tool based on safer antifungal indicator strains; confirming antifungal effects of chitinases and β-amyrin. In the future, we will promote the large-scale application of this synthetic biology-driven strategy, further supporting long-term agricultural health and food security.

title: BEDMAN: Bio-Engineered Design for Microbial Antipest Neutralization
text: BEDMAN: Bio-Engineered Design for Microbial Antipest Neutralization. The project aims to deliver a safe, effective green mosquito repellent "bio-fermented citral". It constructed the IPP/DMAPP→GPP→geraniol→citral synthetic pathway in E. coli using three enzymes for modular expression on 3 vectors, and screened mutants like GeDH-54883 to boost catalytic stability. Engineered strains showed normal growth. QPCR confirmed upregulated transcription of target genes; WB verified successful protein expression. TB medium fermentation yielded 0.89-1.36 g/L citral, with yield-improving synergy identified via multi-factor optimization. Non-spray sustained-release prototypes were designed. Surveys confirmed core demands, guiding compliance strategies. A closed-loop validation from pathway construction to product definition was completed, proving bio-fermented citral’s scalability.

title: ReSET: Reprogramming the Suppressive Environment of TME
text: ReSET: Reprogramming the Suppressive Environment of TME. Colorectal Cancer (CRC), the second leading cause of cancer deaths, lacks specific and effective treatments. Our engineered ReSET system uses the probiotic E. coli Nissle 1917 to detect lactate and hypoxia—key tumour microenvironment cues—and secrete an Anti-CD38 Nanobody-Fc fusion, reprogramming immunosuppressive Tregs into healthy cells. Simultaneously, it produces salicylate, a harmless reporter detected via our ReSense paper strip assay, indicating bacterial colonisation and active therapy. This dual-action system combines targeted immunomodulation with real-time monitoring, offering a precise and adaptive therapeutic platform for CRC treatment.

title: Engineered Streptomyces by alkB gene for Agricultural PE Mulch Degradation
text: Engineered Streptomyces by alkB gene for Agricultural PE Mulch Degradation. Plastic mulching is widely applied to enhance crop yield, yet the accumulation of non-degradable polyethylene (PE) films has led to severe soil pollution and fertility loss. To address this challenge, our project engineered Streptomyces to express optimized alkane hydroxylase enzymes, accelerating the degradation of PE under agricultural conditions. Using AlphaFold2-based protein modeling, we predicted and refined enzyme structures to improve catalytic activity and stability. Moreover, we developed an environmental prediction model that recommends the most suitable mulch type according to local temperature and rainfall, promoting rational use of plastic films. In parallel, a field survey among farmers in Henan Province revealed that nearly half believed traditional PE films reduce yields, underscoring the urgency of biodegradable alternatives. By integrating synthetic biology, computational modeling, and social investigation, our project provides a comprehensive and sustainable solution to agricultural plastic pollution.

title: Y.E.P. - Yeast Electron Production
text: Y.E.P. - Yeast Electron Production. To reduce harmful greenhouse gas emissions, renewable energy storage is critical. Lithium-ion batteries dominate but pose environmental risks from mining, production, and disposal. Microbial fuel cells (MFCs) offer a greener alternative: microorganisms oxidize organic waste, generating electricity while cleaning wastewater, providing sustained, low-carbon energy with fewer ecological impacts. In this project, we engineer yeast MFCs with enhanced electron storage and electron transfer capacity. We achieve that goal by elevating the Saccharomyces cerevisiae intracellular NADH pool and enhancing their extracellular electron transfer. Using the CRISPR/Cas9 genetic editing tool, we deleted genes encoding the key enzymes of glycerol and ethanol biosynthesis, and external mitochondrial NADH dehydrogenase. Engineered strains were tested in custom MFC hardware. To fully leverage the increased intracellular NADH levels, we propose the heterologous expression of fungal cellobiose dehydrogenase (CDH) on the yeast cell surface to enhance the cell’s ability to transfer electrons to electrodes.

title: PlasticSense Neo--Microplastic Detection-Degradation System
text: PlasticSense Neo--Microplastic Detection-Degradation System. Microplastic pollution has emerged as a significant global environmental issue.
