Preliminary research conducted by the HP group indicates that the public is increasingly concerned about its widespread distribution, hidden forms, and potential for ingestion. In response to elevated concentrations of microplastics, such as polyethylene terephthalate (PET), in the environment, this study utilizes synthetic biology techniques to develop various biological modules for detection and degradation. To ensure biosafety, we designed a "OR" gate lysis module that facilitates the self-lysis of microorganisms. This research aims to provide systematic solutions for the precise detection and sustainable management of microplastics, thereby contributing to bioremediation strategies.

title: Bactolyze
text: Bactolyze. Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a rapidly escalating global crisis that threatens the efficacy of life-saving antibiotics and undermines years of medical and agricultural progress. Beyond the direct health toll projected to reach millions of deaths annually by 2050, the consequences extend to food security, livestock production and trade, underscoring the interconnected One Health perspective in this regard. To address this challenge, our iGEM project Bactolyze develops a modular platform for the discovery, optimization, and application of bacteriophage-derived endolysins as novel enzyme-based antimicrobials. Combining cell-free production for rapid screening, computational modeling of antimicrobial peptide–membrane interactions, and fusion-based engineering, we target clinically relevant Gram-negative pathogens and biofilm-associated infections. By integrating experimental workflows with regulatory insights and stakeholder engagement, Bactolyze lays the groundwork for next-generation enzyme-based therapeutics, complementing antibiotics and widening our arsenal against AMR.

title: CadmiCatch
text: CadmiCatch. Cadmium (Cd) is a toxic heavy metal released through industrial processes that persists in soil and water, posing serious environmental and neurotoxic risks. Chronic exposure is linked to oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer’s and Parkinson’s. Conventional Cd remediation methods are costly and unsustainable, creating demand for biological alternatives. This project explores Pseudomonas putida KT2440 as a chassis for Cd bioremediation. We engineered a Cd biosensor using the CadC repressor protein, which activates gene expression upon Cd binding. Preliminary assays in E. coli (NEB 10β) confirmed CadC responsiveness, though the ON/OFF dynamic range was limited. Promoter characterization (BBa_J23100–BBa_J23119) in P. putida showed most variants functional except BBa_J23109. These results demonstrate the feasibility of developing a P. putida-based biosensing and bioremediation system for Cd, supporting the creation of sustainable, field-deployable microbial solutions for heavy metal pollution.

title: BioVitalis
text: BioVitalis. Salidroside, the core component of Rhodiola, exhibits remarkable pharmacological effects in antioxidation, anti-fatigue, immune enhancement, and cardiovascular protection, holding significant market potential. However, traditional plant extraction methods face severe challenges, including resource scarcity, low yield, long growth cycles, and environmental pollution. To address these issues, our team has successfully developed an innovative synthetic biology approach by constructing a novel, sustainable, and cost-effective biosynthetic pathway in Escherichia coli. We have engineered a de novo pathway from glucose, incorporating key enzymes to efficiently convert precursors into salidroside. To further amplify the project's impact and ensure its market viability, we conducted extensive Human Practices and entrepreneurship initiatives. Through questionnaires, interviews, expert consultations, and multi-platform social media promotion, we deepened our understanding of public health needs, paving the way for the commercialization and sustainable development of salidroside products. Our work represents a significant step towards making salidroside more accessible for widespread health applications.

title: GlutaGuard: A Probiotic Shield Against Oxidative Stress
text: GlutaGuard: A Probiotic Shield Against Oxidative Stress. The project proposes using the commensal gut microbiome to enhance antioxidative defense through glutathione production. Glutathione, naturally produced in most mammalian cells and some bacteria, is essential for neutralizing reactive oxygen and nitrogen species (ROS/RNS). However, chronic pollutant exposure can overwhelm this system, contributing to physical and psychological health issues. Three Lactobacillus strains (L. plantarum, L. reuteri, and L. rhamnosus) will be engineered to sense oxidative stress and produce glutathione to neutralize ROS/RNS. Transformation will use plasmids carrying an oxyR transcription factor, a trxC promoter, and a gshF gene. Modified colonies will be screened via ROS exposure assays to confirm plasmid uptake. Successfully modified strains may be delivered through probiotic foods such as yogurt or kombucha. By strengthening the gut’s antioxidative capacity, this project aims to mitigate the adverse health effects of chronic air pollution exposure and improve overall resilience in both sensitive and general populations.

title: POSEIDON - Phytoprotein-Optimized System for Environmental Ion DetoxificatiON
text: POSEIDON - Phytoprotein-Optimized System for Environmental Ion DetoxificatiON. Toxic metal contamination in drinking water disproportionately affects rural and industrial communities exposed to mercury, aluminum, iron, and hexavalent chromium. Conventional remediation methods are energy-intensive and often inaccessible. POSEIDON (Phytoprotein-Optimized System for Environmental Ion Detoxification) offers a synthetic biology solution, using metal-binding peptides for selective ion removal. Phytochelatin synthase (PCS) and engineered metallothionein (MT) are expressed in safe E. coli, purified, and immobilized onto biodegradable alginate hydrogel beads via EDC/NHS chemistry. Packed into modular cartridges, these reusable, gravity-operated units are optimized through modeling for efficient mixed-metal removal. POSEIDON promotes sustainability, local fabrication, and modularity while supporting SDGs 3, 6, 8, 9, 11, 14, 15, and 17.

title: CardioGuard: Dual-System Biosynthesis of Leonurine for Cardiovascular and Cerebrovascular Protection
text: CardioGuard: Dual-System Biosynthesis of Leonurine for Cardiovascular and Cerebrovascular Protection. Cardiovascular and cerebrovascular diseases claim over 17 million lives annually, accounting for 32% of global deaths (WHO, 2019). Leonurine, an alkaloid from Leonurus japonicus, shows preclinical protective effects by reducing oxidative stress, improving circulation, and inhibiting platelet aggregation. To enable sustainable production, we established a dual-platform biosynthesis strategy in Escherichia coli and Nicotiana tabacum hairy root systems. Both platforms heterologously express the final two pathway enzymes, LjUGT5 and LjSCPL, enabling conversion of the supplemented precursors sinapic acid (SA) and 4-guanidinobutanol into leonurine. We compare yield and cost efficiency across systems to identify an optimal, scalable route, providing a stable source of leonurine for cardiovascular protection.

title: Latent Tuberculosis Diagnosis - Infecheck
text: Latent Tuberculosis Diagnosis - Infecheck. One disease. Two billion lives affected. Tuberculosis (TB) remains humanity’s most persistent infectious killer - and its hidden form, latent TB, can strike without warning. Yet current tests are slow, costly, and often out of reach for the communities hit hardest.  Infecheck addresses the problem with early detection of LTB. We are developing a cheap, paper-strip diagnostic that uses a simple finger-prick blood sample to detect upregulated miRNAs specific to LTB. We explored two promising methods for exosomal miRNA detection: Toehold Switches and CCDR. We envision our end-product to be in the form of a lateral flow test and to use microfluidics as the extraction method. The test delivers easy-to-read results without requiring lab-based equipment. Our approach prevents the progression from latent to active TB, therefore reducing patient suffering and TB spread. INFECHECK - because we can’t cure what we can’t find.

title: Engineered EcN for Neoeriocitrin Production in Colorectal Cancer Therapy
text: Engineered EcN for Neoeriocitrin Production in Colorectal Cancer Therapy. Colorectal cancer (CRC) incidence is rising globally and increasingly affects people under 40. Current therapies are invasive and often cause severe side effects. We developed a precision therapeutic strategy using engineered Escherichia coli Nissle 1917 (EcN). Neoeriocitrin, a natural flavonoid with antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and immunomodulatory activities, shows promise in CRC prevention and adjuvant therapy but faces limitations of low yield and high extraction cost. To overcome this, we reconstructed its complete biosynthetic pathway in EcN by introducing VvRHM, UGT73B2, and Cm1,2RhaT, enabling efficient and controlled production. To ensure biosafety, we designed a dual suicide system: arabinose-inducible pBAD triggers in vivo lysis, while low-temperature-inducible pCspA provides environmental containment, both cooperating with MazF. This engineered probiotic integrates high-yield biosynthesis with strict biocontainment, offering a safe, controllable, and effective adjuvant strategy for CRC therapy, particularly for young patients with early-onset disease.

title: NANODEN - Nanobodies for Dengue
text: NANODEN - Nanobodies for Dengue. In 2024, Brazil recorded the world’s highest number of dengue cases, with over 6 million suspected and 3 million confirmed infections. Foz do Iguaçu, in western Paraná, faced a severe outbreak, with more than 10,000 reported cases, 1,280 confirmed infections, and 22 deaths, leading to a State of Emergency. To address this situation, Nanoden proposes an innovative synthetic biology solution: to develop nanobodies capable of binding to the dengue virus envelope protein, followed by the genetic modification of the mosquito’s natural bacterium, Serratia marcescens, to produce these nanobodies. This interaction prevents the virus from entering mosquito cells, interrupting its transmission and offering a sustainable, long-term strategy for vector control.

title: A High-Yield Plectasin Yeast Cell Factory: Constructing Efficient Plectasin-Producing P. Pastoris
text: A High-Yield Plectasin Yeast Cell Factory: Constructing Efficient Plectasin-Producing P. Pastoris. Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) are naturally occurring defense molecules with broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity, low resistance induction, and high stability. Plectasin, a fungal AMP, effectively inhibits Gram-positive bacteria and is used in feed additives. Current production methods such as extraction and chemical synthesis remain limited by low yield and high cost. Genetically engineered microorganisms offer a promising alternative, enabling scalable, cost-effective AMP production with tailored design. The yeast Pichia pastorisis a particularly suitable host due to its safety, efficient secretion machinery, and simple cultivation. In this study, we engineer P. pastorisby integrating the plectasin NZ2114 gene and optimizing regulatory elements to generate a high-yield strain, thereby facilitating its commercial-scale production.

title: SynNotch-Engineered Macrophages for Enhanced Liver Cancer Therapy (SYNERGY) - A Precision Immunotherapy
text: SynNotch-Engineered Macrophages for Enhanced Liver Cancer Therapy (SYNERGY) - A Precision Immunotherapy. The AFMU-China 2025 team has developed SYNERGY, a synthetic Notch system (SynNotch)-based engineered macrophage therapy designed to address two critical challenges in liver cancer treatment: tumor antigen heterogeneity and the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. SYNERGY employs a team-developed anti-SLC17A2 single-chain variable fragment (scFv) as an INPUT module to specifically recognize the SLC17A2 protein on hepatocyte surfaces, enabling liver microenvironment-specific activation. Simultaneously, a P65-SIRPα shRNA bicistronic system serves as the OUTPUT module, reprogramming macrophages into an anti-tumor M1 phenotype while blocking the "don't eat me" signal, thereby synergistically enhancing therapeutic efficacy. To reduce costs, we further established an in vivo gene editing platform using lipid nanoparticles (LNP) for tumor-associated macrophage (TAM) reprogramming, offering a "single-injection" therapeutic strategy for liver cancer. This technology holds broad potential for applications in hepatitis, liver fibrosis, and other liver diseases, providing a novel avenue for precision liver cancer therapy.

title: Generative Design of Osteocalcin Binder Protein for Point-of-Care Based Sensor
text: Generative Design of Osteocalcin Binder Protein for Point-of-Care Based Sensor. Long-duration spaceflight causes accelerated bone loss, increasing astronauts’ risk of skeletal weakening. Existing bone monitoring methods rely on invasive sampling, underscoring the need for a rapid, non-invasive diagnostic suitable for microgravity. Targeting osteocalcin, a key marker of bone turnover, our team is developing a de novo protein binder as the foundation for a biosensor. Using BindCraft, an AI-based protein design platform, we generated and refined binder candidates, ranking interactions through HADDOCK3 docking simulations. Top designs were codon-optimized, cloned into E. coli, and purified for testing. Binding kinetics and affinities will be assessed via Bio-Layer Interferometry (BLI). This project integrates computational and experimental approaches to create a modular workflow for selective protein binder development, enabling future biosensors that can monitor astronaut bone health and other biomarkers in both space and clinical settings.

title: Eucaplyn - Biosynthesis of 1,8-Cineole: A Sustainable Approach to Anti-Acne Skincare
text: Eucaplyn - Biosynthesis of 1,8-Cineole: A Sustainable Approach to Anti-Acne Skincare. Currently, the primary market applications of 1,8-cineole (Eucalyptol) are concentrated in perfumes, essential oils, and food processing. However, few have utilized 1,8-cineole for producing pharmaceuticals or skincare products. The key issue lies in the current bottleneck of purifying the component from plants (purity generally only reaches 80%-85%), coupled with the fact that the active component is highly prone to thermal decomposition, and traditional extraction processes are costly. In contrast, our production of 1,8-cineole using synthetic biology methods theoretically enables high purity, high efficiency, stable, and controllable production. This is precisely the key to addressing the pain points of traditional processes and enhancing product quality. Freed from the constraints of high cost and low purity, 1,8-cineole, leveraging its multi-target anti-acne capabilities including inhibiting Cutibacterium acnes, reducing inflammatory responses, and clearing excess sebum, holds promise as a novel anti-acne product superior to current single-mechanism options on the market.

title: FLUversal
text: FLUversal. Influenza remains a major global health challenge, infecting up to 10% of the population annually and causing significant morbidity and mortality, especially among vulnerable groups. Current vaccines require yearly reformulation due to rapid viral mutation, often resulting in reduced effectiveness. Our iGEM project aims to design a universal influenza vaccine that targets the highly conserved HA2 region of the hemagglutinin protein.

title: Wukong SmartDrive: A Micro-Biohybrid Robotic System for Precision Delivery of Engineered Bacterial Vaccines in Aquaculture
text: Wukong SmartDrive: A Micro-Biohybrid Robotic System for Precision Delivery of Engineered Bacterial Vaccines in Aquaculture. China's classical novel “Journey to the West”, the project transforms his "72 transformations" of adaptability and breakthrough spirit into technical design concepts, demonstrating the deep integration of traditional wisdom and modern technology. Technically, our team successfully developed a novel vaccine delivery system responsive to specific light signals using gene editing technology. This system utilizes a biomimetic vaccine robot to achieve targeted penetration of fish immune barriers and precise activation of immune responses, thereby significantly enhancing disease resistance in fish. Meanwhile, the automated immersion inoculation equipment adopts high-efficiency, non-destructive designs to ensure high precision and scalability during inoculation, making it suitable for large-scale farming scenarios. Practice has shown that this technological system effectively reduces antibiotic usage and decreases disease outbreak frequency. The project's achievements provide innovative solutions for marine ecological protection and global food security, showcasing the potential of interdisciplinary collaboration in addressing agricultural challenges.

title: GoutBuster: Intestine-Targeted Engineered Bacteria for Purine-Urate Transport & Degradation and Hyperuricemia Prevention-Treatment System
text: GoutBuster: Intestine-Targeted Engineered Bacteria for Purine-Urate Transport & Degradation and Hyperuricemia Prevention-Treatment System. Gout, driven by hyperuricemia, now affects about 55.8 million people worldwide and is projected to reach 95.8 million by 2050. East Asia bears a disproportionate burden, with a 175.9% increase in cases and 26.4% higher age-standardized prevalence. Current drugs targeting liver/kidney function often cause severe side effects, necessitating safer alternatives. Our project GoutBuster develops an engineered probiotic that modulates intestinal purine-urate metabolism. Biosafety is ensured by deleting the smr resistance gene and assessing gene transferability. Efficacy is enhanced through integration of a high-efficiency urate transporter (UacT) and a secretory uricase, enabling purine absorption blockade, urate transport, and degradation.  Support tools include a dynamic dosing model, multilingual voice assistant, public engagement platform (Suprobiotics), and inclusive science communication formats. GoutBuster aligns with WHO goals for safe, accessible non-communicable disease treatments and offers a novel, replicable model for metabolic disease management and probiotic innovation.

title: LignoDoc: Biocatalytic Conversion of Lignin-Derived Vanillic Acid to Paracetamol
text: LignoDoc: Biocatalytic Conversion of Lignin-Derived Vanillic Acid to Paracetamol. The utilization of lignin in straw remains challenging. Direct incineration not only exacerbates the climate crisis but also constitutes a waste of resources. To address this issue, we have successfully converted lignin into paracetamol while preserving its benzene ring structure. This approach helps mitigate environmental problems caused by straw burning and offers a sustainable pathway for pharmaceutical production. In the future, this project is expected to pave the way for more high-value applications of lignin, enabling the green synthesis of valuable benzene-ring-containing products.

title: Surfing TentaRobot: A Tide-Synchronized Biofilm Platform for Heavy-Metal Remediation in Mangrove Ecosystems
text: Surfing TentaRobot: A Tide-Synchronized Biofilm Platform for Heavy-Metal Remediation in Mangrove Ecosystems. Mangrove ecosystems face escalating heavy metal pollution threats. We developed "Surfing TentaRobot"—a tide-adaptive bioremediation platform using engineered Bacillus subtilis. Core innovations: (1) Self-assembling adsorption: TasA-ShMT3 fusion proteins and ΔsinR-tasA ΔepsA chassis achieve effective heavy metal capture. (2) Biomineralization: Dsp-aCA carbonic anhydrase catalyzes MICP, precipitating CaCO₃/MgCO₃ to permanently sequester adsorbed metals and prevent tidal re-mobilization. (3) Osmotic NOT gate enables tidal rhythm function switching: LLM-assisted workflow identified osmotic-responsive PproHJ promoter; TetR-based NOT gate design enables functional switching between adsorption and mineralization. (4) Cross-scale modeling: Six-layer framework spans molecular docking to field deployment, including competitive assembly models explaining capacity limitations, coupling kinetics quantifying mineralization interference, UTide tidal analysis determining optimal deployment parameters, and biofilm growth models guiding operational strategies. (5) Social responsibility: 215+ surveys and educational activities reaching 600+ students integrated stakeholder feedback. This work demonstrates transforming tidal salinity fluctuations from engineering constraints into regulatory signals for coastal ecosystem remediation.

title: Click. Customize. Cure. Engineering a Systematic Pipeline for Site-Specific Lipid Functionalization of Enzymes
text: Click. Customize. Cure. Engineering a Systematic Pipeline for Site-Specific Lipid Functionalization of Enzymes. Protein therapeutics have transformed medicine but often suffer from rapid clearance. L-asparaginase, used to treat childhood acute lymphoblastic leukemia, exemplifies this limitation. Conventional PEGylation extends its half-life but can trigger hypersensitivity and disrupt catalytic sites, highlighting the need for precise alternatives. Using genetically recoded E. coli and orthogonal translation systems, we incorporated nonstandard amino acids (nsAAs) enabling copper-catalyzed azide-alkyne click chemistry for site-specific fatty-acid conjugation. To identify tolerant positions, we combined sequence conservation analysis with Golden Gate–based construction of L-asparaginase variants and experimentally evaluated catalytic activity. Several nsAA incorporation sites preserved native bioactivity. These data trained a computational ensemble integrating molecular dynamics, docking, and stability metrics to predict functional outcomes of nsAA substitutions. This pipeline links experimental and computational protein engineering, reducing screening needs and improving therapeutic stability—offering a safer, longer-lasting alternative to PEGylation for more effective leukemia treatment.

title: Cleaning Up Oil Spills With the Help of Alcanivorax borkumensis
text: Cleaning Up Oil Spills With the Help of Alcanivorax borkumensis. Marine oil spills pose recurring threats to ocean ecosystems. Alcanivorax borkumensis, a halophic, hydrocarbonoclastic bacterium evolved to thrive around oil-contaminated environments, is promising for bioremediation. Its concentration increases naturally after oil spills, efficiently degrading alkanes, utilizing specialized enzymes including alkane monooxygenases, cytochrome P450s, and biosurfactant-producing pathways. We explored A. borkumensis's biofilm formation and alkane oxygenation, identifying its overall better performance over champion isolates. Through a proteomic study, we identified secreted proteins in alkane degradation's first steps, testing their degradation abilities through a biochemical NPD-hydrazine assay. We deem the flavin-binding monooxygenase AlmA promising in alkane degradation. We also focused on creating a genetic toolbox for A. borkumensis, studying conjugation and broad-host range plasmid transformation. The findings indicate the enzymes responsible for the degradation's first steps, setting the foundation to create more complex genetic toolboxes. Future implementation, more efficient oil spill cleanup, has potential to save marine life and protect coastal industries.

title: RE-PEAt：Recycling Ethylene glycol to PolyEsters And terephthalate to p-coumaric acid
text: RE-PEAt：Recycling Ethylene glycol to PolyEsters And terephthalate to p-coumaric acid. The UESTC-China team presents RE-PEAt, a platform that closes the PET loop by integrating enzymatic depolymerization with value-added biosynthesis. We synergistically hydrolyze PET into ethylene glycol (EG) and terephthalic acid (TPA) using magnetically immobilized PETase and Tfca. Through bioinformatics and synthetic biology, we engineered E. coli to consume EG as its sole carbon source, alleviating its competitive inhibition on PET hydrolases. Downstream, RE-PEAt converts EG into biodegradable polyesteramide and upgrades TPA into high-value p-coumaric acid, creating sustainable product streams. Furthermore, a colorimetric biosensor was constructed to monitor EG concentrations in real time, providing reliable guidance for both PET hydrolysis and EG conversion. By combining reusable biocatalysts with microbial upgrading, RE-PEAt offers an integrated framework for PET upcycling—from depolymerization to material and chemical regeneration.

title: A Single-Stranded DNA Biosensor in the Form of a Capillary Tube
text: A Single-Stranded DNA Biosensor in the Form of a Capillary Tube. The standard methods for detection of viruses in samples are expensive, time-consuming, and require access to specialized equipment. To address this problem, we aimed to design a point-of-care oligonucleotide sensor in the form of a capillary tube. This article discusses a proof-of-concept for this system as well as a modular phagemid system for us, and future iGEM teams, to safely validate viral-detection systems without the need to use pathogenic viruses.

title: Dual-Function Probiotic: Protecting Astronauts’ Muscle and Mental Health
text: Dual-Function Probiotic: Protecting Astronauts’ Muscle and Mental Health. Commercial spaceflight is rapidly evolving from experimental trials to large-scale operations, with companies like SpaceX, Blue Origin, and Virgin Galactic—and China’s own emerging space sector—driving down launch costs and opening the door to space tourism, lunar bases, and Mars colonization. Yet long-duration missions pose serious health risks, particularly microgravity-induced muscle loss and mood disorders. We address this challenge by engineering E. coli Nissle 1917 with a de novo HMB biosynthesis pathway to combat sarcopenia and a serotonin pathway to support mental well-being, creating a dual-function probiotic to safeguard astronaut health and enable sustainable human presence in space.

title: PROTEUS
text: PROTEUS. We have successfully developed PROTEUS—a universal AI-driven protein optimization platform based on ESM-2, employing MLM (Masked Language Modeling) for function-oriented fine-tuning. Sequences were categorized into high/low-performance groups based on metrics such as enzymatic activity and thermal stability, and a DMS scoring function was designed to build an intelligent optimization engine. This model can accurately identify key functional sites, perform targeted optimization of low-performance protein sequences (e.g., antimicrobial peptides or industrial enzyme variants), and utilize AlphaFold for structural prediction to validate design rationality. Based on this project, we have developed an open-source software tool that allows users to input a target protein sequence and obtain an optimized solution with one click, providing a universal AI-driven design platform for synthetic biology.

title: Turning Bacteria into Time Fighters: Sustainable NMN Production with Synthetic Biology
text: Turning Bacteria into Time Fighters: Sustainable NMN Production with Synthetic Biology. Current production methods face challenges such as high costs, harsh reaction conditions, complex processes, and environmental burdens. Using synthetic biology, we redesigned E. coli by introducing the genes NiaP, nadV, PnuC, and BaPRS, enabling efficient NMN production. Considering gender differences: for men, we engineered E. coli to produce GLP-1, which is combined with NMN to make capsules; for women, we engineered E. coli to produce glutathione, developed into oral solutions and antioxidant facial masks. Through this diversified design, our solution makes it easier for people to achieve healthier and more vibrant lives.

title: Probabyotics Infant Formula: Probiotic HMOs, Digestible Casein & Lactose-Free
text: Probabyotics Infant Formula: Probiotic HMOs, Digestible Casein & Lactose-Free. To address critical limitations in current infant formula—specifically the absence of immunomodulatory human milk oligosaccharides (HMOs), poor digestibility of casein micelles, and prevalent lactose intolerance—our team, Probabyotics,  developed "2-FLuxe" using Escherichia coli Nissle 1917（EcN） as a probiotic chassis for integrated bioengineering. We constructed three synergistic systems: (1) a de novo 2’-fucosyllactose (2’-FL) synthesis pathway (via manB-manC-gmd-fcl-futC overexpression) to produce breastmilk-mimetic HMOs at >80% reduced cost; (2) recombinant trypsinogen expression for precise casein hydrolysis, alleviating gastrointestinal burden; and (3) high-yield β-galactosidase (lacZ) fermentation to eliminate lactose. Manufacturing involves EcN-based fermentation with low-cost substrates (glycerol/lactose), enzymatic purification, and incorporation of 2’-FL with trypsin/β-galactosidase-treated milk. The resulting formulation eliminates key drawbacks of conventional formulas by providing 2’-FL-driven pathogen inhibition and microbiota support, enhanced protein digestibility, and lactose-free tolerance—enabling accessible, breastmilk-equivalent nutrition for infants with digestive vulnerabilities or limited breastfeeding access.

title: CerviX Spy: CRISPR-Powered Home Screening for Cervical Cancer
text: CerviX Spy: CRISPR-Powered Home Screening for Cervical Cancer. CerviX Spy is an innovative point-of-care testing (POCT) platform integrating CRISPR-Cas13a technology and microfluidics for early cervical cancer screening. Targeting the host-derived biomarker miR-155 - a key oncogenic miRNA upregulated in precancerous lesions—the system employs a modular toehold switch probe that undergoes conformational change upon target binding, activating a T7 promoter to transcribe sgRNA. This triggers Cas13a-mediated cis-cleavage of target RNA and collateral trans-cleavage of fluorescent reporters, enabling pM-level detection under isothermal conditions (37 ℃). Validated via rigorous DBTL (Design-Build-Test-Learn) cycles, the biosensor achieves single-base specificity and pM sensitivity, overcoming limitations of traditional HPV-DNA assays (e.g., inability to distinguish transient vs. oncogenic infections). Encapsulated in the user-friendly "CerviSure Scanner" - a 3D-printed, disposable microfluidic device - the system supports decentralized, non-invasive screening with rapid results (<60 min). This platform promises to reduce healthcare disparities by enabling accessible, high-accuracy screening in low-resource settings, advancing global cervical cancer elimination efforts.

title: SCG Detoxification: A Solution for Transforming Waste Coffee Grounds into Biofertilizers
text: SCG Detoxification: A Solution for Transforming Waste Coffee Grounds into Biofertilizers. The spent coffee ground (SCG) holds significant potential for producing organic fertilizers. Residual caffeine, however, inhibits plant growth due to its phytotoxicity, substantially limiting the application of SCG in bio-fertilizer production. Conventional decaffeination methods suffer from high costs and environmental concerns. Here, we genetically engineered Escherichia coli (E. coli) by integrating genes involved in caffeine degradation, aiming to remove the residual caffeine from SGG during fermentation while producing valuable biofertilizers. Our project provides an eco-friendly and cost-effective solution for the recycling of SCG. The safety and scalability of the engineered E. coli ensure its broad applicability in agriculture, horticulture, and environmental protection.

title: The Salidroside Initiative: Protecting the Plateau and Every Heartbeat with Synthetic Biology
text: The Salidroside Initiative: Protecting the Plateau and Every Heartbeat with Synthetic Biology. Cardiovascular diseases increasingly threaten young populations due to stress and unhealthy habits. Salidroside, a cardioprotective compound from Rhodiola rosea, shows antioxidant and anti-hypoxic effects but is difficult to source sustainably. To solve this, we engineered Escherichia coli to biosynthesize salidroside via an optimized tyrosol pathway and heterologous expression of a UDP-glucosyltransferase (UGT). In addition, we developed a whole-cell biosensor targeting 4-hydroxyphenylpyruvate (4HPP), a key intermediate in the microbial biosynthetic pathway of salidroside. By employing this sensor, we enhanced salidroside production through directed evolution. Our system provides an eco-friendly, scalable alternative to plant extraction, reducing pressure on fragile plateau ecosystems while supporting youth heart health through synthetic biology innovation.

title: CatWell: Oral Peptide Contraceptive System for Humane Feral Cat Control
text: CatWell: Oral Peptide Contraceptive System for Humane Feral Cat Control. As urban feral cat populations continue to grow, ecological balance, public health, and animal welfare are increasingly threatened. To address this, we designed an oral contraceptive peptide based on a sequence-modified cyclized GnRH antagonist that competitively blocks reproductive hormone signaling without affecting animal health. By optimizing peptide stability through sequence modification and disulfide ring formation, and co-administering with SNAC to enhance gastrointestinal absorption, we enable effective oral delivery. For safe and precise administration, we designed CatWell, an AI-powered smart feeder that provides controlled daily dosing to individual feral cats. Together, this integrated system offers a humane, scalable, and non-surgical solution for feral cat population control.

title: Modular attenuated vaccine development for sustainable aquaculture
text: Modular attenuated vaccine development for sustainable aquaculture. Our iGEM project addresses the critical challenge of Pseudomonas plecoglossicida-induced visceral white spot disease in large yellow croaker, which causes annual industry losses exceeding ¥600 million due to high mortality rates (70–80%), while traditional antibiotic therapies exacerbate drug resistance and ecological harm. We employ an integrated computational-experimental strategy to develop a novel live attenuated vaccine. Starting with the CLEF model, we screen effector proteins, then validate candidates using engineered E. coli BL21(DE3). These virulence factors serve as vaccine targets. We also use C. elegans for preliminary toxicity and protection studies. Mathematical modeling simulates immune responses and economic impact, linking predictions with practical efficacy. Our goal is to establish an efficient antigen screening system to accelerate novel aquaculture vaccine development, offering a sustainable strategy to reduce disease prevalence and enhance productivity.

title: SOD Shield: Novel Eye Drops Prevent Oxidative Cataracts
text: SOD Shield: Novel Eye Drops Prevent Oxidative Cataracts. Cataracts, a leading cause of global blindness, primarily result from oxidative damage to lens proteins. Current treatment relies on invasive surgery. Superoxide dismutase (SOD), a key antioxidant enzyme, neutralizes reactive oxygen species but suffers from instability and rapid degradation, limiting its therapeutic potential. Manganese superoxide dismutase (Mn-SOD) is an important subtype of the SOD family. This enzyme is closely related to the occurrence and development of cataracts. Our project employs computational biology and machine learning to engineer thermostable, high-activity Mn-SOD variants. These variants will be characterized in E. coli. Furthermore, a multi-scale mathematical model will be developed to simulate the spatiotemporal efficacy of Mn-SOD when delivered as an eye drop, from catalytic kinetics to reaction-diffusion within the eye. The goal is to develop engineered Mn-SOD as a core component of novel eye drops, offering a non-invasive strategy for cataract prevention and early intervention to alleviate the global disease burden.

title: Protective effect of ginseng on bioaccessibility and oxidative stress induced by microplastics during in-vitro digestion
text: Protective effect of ginseng on bioaccessibility and oxidative stress induced by microplastics during in-vitro digestion. This study investigated how Korean ginseng affects amine-functionalized polystyrene microplastics (MPs) using a simulated digestion model and liver cell cultures. Researchers found that ginsenosides, the active compounds in ginseng, promote the aggregation of MPs through electrostatic interactions. This clumping effect significantly reduced the bioaccessibility of the microplastics, with a 1:4 (MP:ginseng) ratio lowering it to just 6.52%. Dynamic light scattering and microscopy confirmed that a 1:2 ratio induced the greatest aggregation. Hyperspectral imaging showed a strong binding between ginsenosides and MPs. Critically, when human liver (HepG2) cells were exposed to MPs, co-treatment with ginseng significantly lowered the production of harmful reactive oxygen species (ROS). The findings suggest that ginseng can mitigate the potential harm of microplastics by decreasing their absorption in the gut and protecting hepatic cells from oxidative stress.

title: Chitinator et al.
text: Chitinator et al.. Chitinator et al. transforms seafood waste into growth. Chitin, the tough biopolymer found in shrimp and crab shells, is often discarded despite its vast potential. Our team engineered a powerful dual-enzyme fusion combining Endochitinase and Exochitinase through a flexible linker, enabling synergistic and continuous chitin degradation into chitooligosaccharides (COS),bioactive molecules that stimulate plant growth and immunity. Expressed in E. coli and optimized for secretion in Bacillus subtilis, our construct lays the foundation for a living bioconversion platform that upcycles chitin waste into a natural bioactivator. Applied to garlic crops, this eco-friendly solution helps combat fungal pathogens like Fusarium oxysporum and Sclerotium cepivorum, promoting sustainable yield and soil regeneration. Through synthetic biology, Chitinator et al. turns what nature discards into what agriculture needs most resilience, protection, and life.

title: Colors from bacteria: production of natural dyes with synthetic biology
text: Colors from bacteria: production of natural dyes with synthetic biology. Synthetic dyes are widely used in the textile industry but generate toxic effluents that cause serious environmental pollution. Our project seeks to provide a sustainable alternative by engineering Escherichia coli to biosynthesize several natural pigments, carotenoids (red, orange), violaceins (ranging from green to purple), and indigo (blue). We focus on optimizing tryptophan metabolism to efficiently channel precursors toward pigment biosynthesis, ensuring higher yields and consistent production. For indigo, we are also exploring novel flavin monooxygenases with enhanced catalytic activity and stability, aiming to overcome the limitations of existing enzymes. Through a combination of metabolic pathway engineering and enzyme discovery, we aim to create a robust microbial production platform capable of replacing harmful synthetic dye processes. By demonstrating the potential of microbial biosynthesis for natural dyes in E. coli, this project highlights synthetic biology’s ability to address environmental challenges and proposes an eco-friendly approach for the future of textile dyeing.

title: APOPTO-SENSE 2.0: Engineering a Dual-Cell Biosensor for Rapid, Personalized Chemotherapy Sensitivity Testing in Cancer
text: APOPTO-SENSE 2.0: Engineering a Dual-Cell Biosensor for Rapid, Personalized Chemotherapy Sensitivity Testing in Cancer. Cancer treatments often fail due to individual variability, with 40-60% of patients non-responsive to standard chemotherapies for leukemia, breast cancer, and non-small cell lung cancer. APOPTO-SENSE 2.0 addresses this with a synthetic biology platform for rapid ex vivo drug sensitivity testing. Our dual-cell system uses engineered HEK293T sensor cells with an Annexin V-fused synNotch receptor to detect phosphatidylserine on apoptotic target cells (e.g., HL-60). Activation releases Gal4-VP64, driving dose-dependent TagBFP expression normalized to mCherry. Iterative DBTL cycles optimized linearity (R²=0.95) and specificity (>95%) through wet lab co-cultures and dry lab ODE simulations. Human Practices integrated clinician feedback, pivoting to ethical patient-derived cell proxies. Education reached 500+ via workshops and a synthetic receptor toolkit.  This proof-of-concept enables personalized oncology, reducing ineffective treatments and extending to multiplexed cell death detection, advancing SDG 3 for equitable health.

title: Efficient conversion of biomass waste with biomimetic rumen microbiota to produce volatile fatty acids
text: Efficient conversion of biomass waste with biomimetic rumen microbiota to produce volatile fatty acids. Lignocellulose is a highly promising renewable resource, but its complex structure hinders degradation. The rumen of ruminants represents a naturally efficient degradation system. This study employed rumen-mimicking microbiota to ferment corn straw in a semi-continuous reactor for volatile fatty acid (VFA) production. Results showed that after 72 hours, VFA concentration reached 8.99 g/L, with hemicellulose, cellulose, and lignin degradation rates of 54.3%, 40.2%, and 8.61%, respectively. At corn straw loading rates of 2.5%, 5.0%, and 8.0%, average VFA concentrations were 8.5, 11.1, and 13.3 g/L, respectively. Metagenomic analysis indicated that low pH and VFA accumulation were the main factors affecting microbial communities, while core genera remained stable. This study provides a theoretical basis for the resource utilization of biomass waste.

title: MORPHE
text: MORPHE. The Morphe project proposes a new therapeutic approach for the treatment of obesity. A non-invasive gene therapy aiming to restore leptin and insulin sensitivity. By achieving conditional silencing of HDAC6, a protein, that in patients with obesity mainly disrupts insulin and leptin metabolic pathways in the hypothalamus, we manage to reverse the underlying neuroendocrine dysfunction. The HDAC6 knockdown will be facilitated by miRE, a microRNA-mimicking shRNA molecule designed to evade immune detection, while selectively silencing HDAC6 mRNA. We will introduce miRE into AgRP neurons using lentiviral vectors through intranasal administration for permanent genomic integration. This genetic circuit incorporates a three-tiered logic system. A transcriptional AND gate and a post-transcriptional failsafe using endogenous miR-7-5p to prevent activation during normal fasting states. These engineered neurons will continuously monitor metabolic signals and autonomously activate therapeutic intervention only during metabolic dysfunction, creating a living therapeutic system capable of long-term, adaptive regulation.

title: Developing a Continuous Wearable Sepsis Biosensor with Novel Electrically Active Aptamers
text: Developing a Continuous Wearable Sepsis Biosensor with Novel Electrically Active Aptamers. Early disease detection improves outcomes and reduces costs, yet current biomarker monitoring requires periodic blood draws, limiting continuous assessment. This proposal aims to develop a wearable, aptamer-based biosensor for critical care diseases like sepsis and kidney failure. A microfluidic device connected to a venous port would continuously monitor biomarkers such as procalcitonin (PCT) and creatinine, providing real-time data to guide treatment. SA 1: Using mutagenic SELEX, we will evolve aptamers with reversible binding under physiological conditions. Aptamers will be immobilized on microfluidic channels with gold electrodes; biomarker binding triggers conformational changes detected electrically and transmitted via Bluetooth. SA 2: A biocompatible port with a semipermeable membrane will exclude blood cells while allowing biomarker flow. Sterility will be maintained using antibiotic-eluting materials, minimizing infection risk during periodic microfluidic replacement. Impact: This platform enables continuous, modular biomarker monitoring, improving patient care, accelerating interventions, and advancing wearable diagnostics in critical care.

title: Plant waxes: a regulatory symphony of biosynthesis pathways
text: Plant waxes: a regulatory symphony of biosynthesis pathways. Our research is based on the idea of ​​synthetic biology to develop a high-efficiency and high-yield wax synthesis system. Using Nicotiana Benthamiana as a carrier, we increase the wax content in tobacco plants by modifying the wax synthesis and metabolic pathways in the plant. On the one hand, we improve the plant's own stress resistance and create new high-wax germplasm resource materials. On the other hand, we provide low-cost, green and sustainable industrial raw materials.

title: ByeFilm
text: ByeFilm. ByeFilm is a synthetic biology system using engineered *E. coli* to secrete Dispersin B, Proteinase K, and DNase I, degrading biofilm polysaccharides, proteins, and eDNA to enhance antibiotic action. A λcI857 thermal lysis switch triggers enzyme release at ≥37 °C, ensuring localized activity and biosafety. This approach offers a minimally invasive treatment for prosthetic joint infections and shows potential against other biofilm-related conditions such as catheter infections, chronic wounds, and dental plaque.

title: Development of a Non-Invasive Prenatal Detection Platform for Dystrophic Epidermolysis Bullosa (DEB)
text: Development of a Non-Invasive Prenatal Detection Platform for Dystrophic Epidermolysis Bullosa (DEB). This project combines synthetic biology with CRISPR-Cas12a technology to create a non-invasive prenatal diagnostic platform for DEB. We designed and constructed a novel plasmid vector for the expression of the Cas12a protein, which was successfully expressed and purified in E. coli through a streamlined synthetic biology workflow. The purified Cas12a enzyme was used in conjunction with Recombinase Polymerase Amplification (RPA) to detect two high-frequency mutations in the COL7A1 gene (c.520G>A and c.6745C>T), which are major causes of DEB. By extracting cell-free fetal DNA (cfDNA) from maternal blood, we were able to amplify and analyze the target mutations. Cas12a’s unique trans-cleavage activity enabled the detection of mutation-specific signals, providing high sensitivity and specificity.

title: Development of Antioxidant Formulations Based on the SOD-CAT Enzyme System
text: Development of Antioxidant Formulations Based on the SOD-CAT Enzyme System. With the exacerbation of environmental pollution and UV radiation, oxidative stress has become a major contributor to skin aging. The hierarchical antioxidant system comprising superoxide dismutase (SOD) and catalase (CAT) operates synergistically: SOD converts superoxide anions into hydrogen peroxide, which CAT then decomposes into water and oxygen. This system demonstrates superior stability and efficiency compared to single antioxidants like vitamin C or E. In this study, recombinant SOD and CAT were produced in Escherichia coli, purified, and their activities validated. Through in vitro assays including superoxide anion and ABTS⁺ radical scavenging, the optimal synergistic ratio of SOD to CAT was determined. The effects of temperature and pH on enzyme stability were evaluated, offering a promising strategy for developing advanced anti-aging cosmetics.

title: ARGUS-2440: Ammonium Rhizospheric Generation Using Soil Bacteria
text: ARGUS-2440: Ammonium Rhizospheric Generation Using Soil Bacteria. Nitrate leaching is a major environmental and human health concern. In our bioremediation-focused project, we aim to insert the nir and nrf operons expressing multiple nitrite reductase genes into Escherichia coli DH5-Alpha and Pseudomonas putida KT2440. We aim to determine the most efficient enzymes for the process via nitrite and ammonium measurement assays, under the XylS/Pm inducible promoter. Simultaneously, we will monitor the plant growth-promoting biofilm that P. putida forms to determine any relation with the aforementioned genes and enzymes. In the dry lab, we will model the ammonium production to predict wet lab results. The model will help us tailor the modified bacterium to specific crop and soil types to optimize efficiency, minimize nitrogen loss, and predict challenges like ammonium toxicity and bacterial overgrowth. We will also build a ML model to predict soil ammonium levels, and changes in ammonium content on application of the engineered bacterium.

title: POVANO: Engineering Pichia pastoris as a Circular, Nutritional Microbial Protein Platform for Sustainable Pet Food
text: POVANO: Engineering Pichia pastoris as a Circular, Nutritional Microbial Protein Platform for Sustainable Pet Food. POVANO aims to develop a circular, low-impact protein production platform by engineering the methylotrophic yeast Pichia pastoris to convert CO₂-derived green methanol into high-yield, nutritionally balanced protein for pet food, addressing sustainability challenges from conventional meat- and fish-based feeds. We constructed a pGAPZ-based ovalbumin expression cassette (pGAP–αMF–OVA–6×His–tAOX1), integrated and validated its expression & secretion, and implemented heterologous expression of inositol biosynthesis enzymes (ScIPS/INO1 and EcIMP) to produce myo-inositol for pet health benefits. To improve product quality and scale-up acceptability, we used CRISPR/Cas9 to knock out pyruvate decarboxylase (PpPDC1) and suppress alcoholic volatiles. POVANO demonstrates a controllable, scalable microbial route that can be tailored for amino-acid balance and reduced land, water and greenhouse gas footprints, aligning with SDGs for responsible consumption and climate action. Next steps include yield and nutritional optimization, pilot-scale fermentation, safety/nutritional testing, and life-cycle analysis to quantify environmental impact.

title: Protein Pre-Binding State Framework Enables Mechanistic Insights and Engineering of Robust Biocatalysts for Plastic Depolymerization
text: Protein Pre-Binding State Framework Enables Mechanistic Insights and Engineering of Robust Biocatalysts for Plastic Depolymerization. Plastic pollution has emerged as a pressing global issue, with plastics accumulating in diverse environments to disrupt ecosystems. While natural enzymes that degrade common plastic PET exist, current PET hydrolases are not optimized for efficient, economical industrial use, and many bio-based polyester alternatives still degrade very slowly in the environment. Our project addressed these challenges by integrating AI-driven strategies, physics-based computational methods, and innovative polymer chemistry. It engineered high-performance PET hydrolases, such as TurboPETase, to enhance PET depolymerization, used simulations and calculations to explore enzyme catalytic mechanisms, and developed controlled-degradable, bio-based polyesters. The goal was to create a scalable enzymatic PET recycling system, design environmentally responsive plastics, and establish a closed-loop plastic cycle, bridging synthetic biology, computational chemistry, and materials science to promote sustainable plastic solutions.

title: VitaPop Jelly: A Probiotic Platform for GLP-1 Delivery in Glucose Regulation
text: VitaPop Jelly: A Probiotic Platform for GLP-1 Delivery in Glucose Regulation. According to the International Diabetes Federation, approximately 589 million adults worldwide have diabetes, with Type 2 diabetes comprising over 90% of cases. Persistent hyperglycemia can lead to serious multi-organ complications. Current treatments require frequent administration, creating practical burdens and reducing quality of life.  Our project, VitaPop Jelly, addresses this through an innovative solution: using engineered E. coli Nissle 1917 to enable continuous intestinal secretion of GLP-1 for sustained glycemic control. We optimized the GLP-1 codon usage to enhance expression and implemented a dual biocontainment system using cysteine auxotrophy and a temperature-sensitive promoter to prevent transgenic leakage. We aim to provide people with diabetes with a safer, more convenient biologic treatment option that improves both health outcomes and daily life.

title: BioComplete: AI-Powered DNA Design Assistant
text: BioComplete: AI-Powered DNA Design Assistant. AI models are transforming biology by capturing complex patterns in DNA sequences. However, realizing their full potential requires both high-quality training data and user-friendly tools for scientists. The iGEM Registry contains the largest collection of synthetic biology parts, but inconsistent annotations and limited search functionality make it difficult to use directly for AI training or for everyday part discovery. Our project addresses these challenges by adapting a DNA foundation model, Evo2, to genetic circuit design. We develop representations that capture functional similarity between parts, enabling reliable retrieval and AI-guided part suggestions. To support this process, we developed a sequence-centric data model that provides easily accessible, findable metadata, including safety status. Our sequence editor and search engine makes the model's capabilities available to users at https://biocomplete.it/. Together, these components form a cycle: cleaner data improves the model, the model creates meaningful embeddings, and these embeddings power new tools for synthetic biology.

title: NanosphinX
text: NanosphinX. Our project began with bioinformatic analysis and flow cytometry experiments, which revealed that breast and pancreatic cancers frequently exhibit upregulation of both CD47 and HER2 receptors. To address this challenge, we designed a bispecific fusion protein incorporating an active antibody fragment targeting HER2 and a nanobody targeting CD47. These designed fragments, along with those retrieved from existing databases, formed a library of candidate antibody fragments. The most stable fragments with the lowest binding free energy were selected for the assembly of the active bispecific antibody, NanosphinX. Two assembly strategies were tested to link the two selected active antibody fragments into the final bispecific format. Cell viability assays demonstrated that NanosphinX exhibits cytotoxic effects against wild-type breast cancer cells and maintains strong activity even in trastuzumab-resistant cells, effectively inhibiting tumor growth. It also enhanced the cytotoxicity of gemcitabine in gemcitabine-resistant cell lines, providing a rational basis for combination therapy with gemcitabine.

title: Dermalogic - Dual Plasmid Biosensor + Response System to Mitigate Inflammation
text: Dermalogic - Dual Plasmid Biosensor + Response System to Mitigate Inflammation. Skin inflammation, like in acne, is driven by immune signals such as nitric oxide and hydrogen peroxide, which amplify irritation and tissue damage. Our therapeutic molecule, Indole-3-acetic-acid (IAA), a plant auxin, has anti-inflammatory benefits by blocking NF-κB signaling and neutralizing reactive oxygen species. Our project is focusing on designing a dual-plasmid biosensor system built as a biological AND gate to detect these cues. The system requires two concurrent inputs: NO detection (via the NorR/PnorV​ promoter to produce LuxR) and H2​O2​ detection (via OxyR/PoxyS​ to activate 3OC6HSL). Only when both LuxR and 3OC6HSL are present will they combine to activate the Plux​ promoter, driving downstream gene expression of indole-3-acetic-acid.

title: PRIME-Guard: A PRoactive Immune Modulation and Evasion-blocking Platform for Virus Prevention
text: PRIME-Guard: A PRoactive Immune Modulation and Evasion-blocking Platform for Virus Prevention. Our project aims to develop a CRISPRa/TetON fusion system for inducible antiviral gene activation, enabling precise control over immune and endocytic pathway upregulation in mammalian cells. By combining dCas9-VP64, rtTA, and sgRNAs within a modular delivery framework, we sought to create a tunable gene expression platform that could be rapidly activated through Doxycycline induction. Preliminary results have shown minimal to no detectable protein expression  across varying Doxycycline concentrations and induction times. Moreover, the system’s capacity to induce downstream gene activation via independent or co-delivered sgRNAs remains uncharacterized. Despite these challenges, our work establishes an important foundation for refining inducible CRISPRa systems and contributes valuable insights toward achieving safe, controllable antiviral gene therapy.

title: LEGO: Light-induced Expression of GLP-1 and insulin for Obesity and diabetes treatment
text: LEGO: Light-induced Expression of GLP-1 and insulin for Obesity and diabetes treatment. The global epidemics of type 2 diabetes and obesity demand innovative, long-term solutions beyond traditional invasive and single-target therapies. We developed LEGO (Light-induced Expression of GLP-1 and Insulin), an optogenetic gene therapy platform that enables precise, reversible, and non-invasive control of dual-hormone secretion. Leveraging endogenous bioluminescence or a wireless light source, LEGO regulates the co-expression of insulin and bioactive GLP-1(7-37)—a clinically validated combination for managing hyperglycemia and obesity. Activation is achieved via oral administration of a luciferase substrate or through a wearable light device, eliminating the need for repeated injections. To enable personalized treatment, we created an open-source software–hardware package that converts patient data (e.g., glucose levels, weight, meal information) into programmable light stimulation for optimized hormone release. Designed with future implantable use in mind, LEGO offers a smart, patient-friendly, and sustainable therapeutic strategy for metabolic disease management.

title: The Bisphenol A Analysis Detection System
text: The Bisphenol A Analysis Detection System. Bisphenol A (BPA) is an endocrine disruptor linked to developmental, metabolic, and reproductive risks in humans and wildlife. Lab analytics can quantify BPA accurately but are costly and inaccessible to most users. We present a low-cost detection toolkit that converts BPA binding into a visible reporter using a LexA-based yeast two-hybrid (Y2H) design. The estrogen receptor-α (ERα/ESR1) ligand-binding domain is fused to the LexA DNA-binding domain (pGilda) and the B42 activation domain (pB42AD); ligand-induced ERα dimerization juxtaposes BD and AD, activating yeast reporters. To boost sensitivity to BPA’s weak agonism, we engineered mutations in the ERα LBD (residues ~519–535) by splicing-by-overlap-extension PCR and cloned variants into pGILDA (bait) and pB42AD (prey). We will evaluate wild-type and mutant ESR1 by dose–response β-galactosidase assays with positive/negative controls and selectivity tests, as a foundation for future community kits.

title: Unburdened Intimacy: A Natural Shield of Antimicrobial Peptides Against Zoonotic Bacteria
text: Unburdened Intimacy: A Natural Shield of Antimicrobial Peptides Against Zoonotic Bacteria. As pet companionship becomes more common, zoonotic bacterial infections are an increasing health concern. Many current antibacterial products are irritating, ineffective, or may lead to bacterial resistance, making them unsuitable for daily use. Must we choose between closeness and safety? We believe not. Using synthetic biology, we engineered E. coli to efficiently produce optimized natural antimicrobial peptides. Based on this, we developed a gentle, safe, and broad-spectrum antibacterial spray for pets. Our project aims to inhibit common zoonotic pathogens while ensuring ecological safety and user convenience—helping pet families enjoy close companionship with confidence and peace of mind.

title: TCsensor: Integrated Tetracycline Detection and Biosafety Control
text: TCsensor: Integrated Tetracycline Detection and Biosafety Control. Tetracycline antibiotics (TCs), among the most globally used antibiotics, persistently accumulate in environments (e.g., water, soil), threatening ecosystems and human health. Current detection methods face limitations in sensitivity, cost, and field applicability. We developed TCsensor, a detection platform for on-site TC monitoring. An engineered Escherichia coli (E. coli) biosensor uses a tetracycline-responsive tet promoter linked to a reporter gene, enabling visual, semi-quantitative detection directly in environmental samples. To ensure biosafety, TCsensor incorporates a robust triple-induction lysis system (temperature-sensitive, L-arabinose-inducible, and lactose-inducible), enabling precise engineered cell self-destruction upon application of specific external signals post-detection, thereby preventing environmental release. This integrated "detect-and-destroy" system offers a practical, field-deployable solution for environmental TC monitoring with minimized biosafety risks.

title: Lacto-Bexo: Engineering a Lactobacillus-Derived Exosomal Protein for Sustainable Obesity Management
text: Lacto-Bexo: Engineering a Lactobacillus-Derived Exosomal Protein for Sustainable Obesity Management. The global obesity crisis demands solutions that balance efficacy, safety, and access. GLP-1 agonists show strong short-term effects but face high cost, side effects, and relapse after discontinuation. Lacto-Bexo uses the gut microbiome as a metabolic health platform. Through a Design-Build-Test-Learn cycle, we identified hisF, a protein secreted in Lactobacillus rhamnosus exosomes; in vitro, hisF cut adipocyte differentiation by ~50%, likely via AMPK activation. Beyond the bench, our Human Practices and Entrepreneurship work—clinician interviews, six-language surveys, and ethical review—addressed safety perception, accessibility, and body-image stigma. The resulting concept is a probiotic, food-grade therapeutic aligned with Korea’s R&D priorities in microbiome and lipid metabolism. Together, we show how synthetic biology, inclusivity, and design thinking can responsibly advance evidence-based obesity management.

title: Light The Way To Pain-Free——Far-infrared light-regulated bacterial pain-relieving hydrogel
text: Light The Way To Pain-Free——Far-infrared light-regulated bacterial pain-relieving hydrogel. NETMAP-PaurTx-3 project aims to develop a light-controlled, non-addictive pain management system using engineered E. coli Nissle 1917 (EcN) expressing PaurTx-3, a sodium channel blocker, specifically at pain sites. The key innovation is the first light-controlled system for targeted pain management using engineered bacteria, integrating the NETMAP system with PaurTx-3 for precise spatiotemporal control. Experimental results show Gibson Assembly achieved 65% efficiency (vs. <10% for traditional PCR cloning), but PaurTx-3 solubility was only 15% (85% formed inclusion bodies). Hydrogel encapsulation maintained >80% bacterial viability and light-responsive expression. The critical challenge is PaurTx-3 low solubility, addressed by implementing a SUMO fusion tag. The project features multiple safety mechanisms including self-destruct systems and gene blockade, complying with FDA/EMA/WHO standards. Future work includes in vivo testing to develop a non-addictive pain management solution for cancer and burn patients.

title: TERRA
text: TERRA. We want to turn red mud, a hazardous bauxite waste, into a source of rare earth elements (REEs). Using Chlamydomonas reinhardtii engineered with a high-affinity binding protein, our algae capture lanthanides from dilute solutions with low concentrations of the precious materials. The workflow is straightforward: pre-treat the red mud, let algae accumulate REEs, ash, recover. A prototype bioreactor supports easy growth and handling. The goal: pair red-mud cleanup with low-input REE recovery that plugs into classical downstream extraction. Experts told us loud and clear: turning red-mud cleanup into a win is exciting and overdue. We have been fueling that momentum, sparking awareness and enthusiasm in the next generation of students.

title: MakeSense - HEK293T cell-based hydroquinone detecting biosensor
text: MakeSense - HEK293T cell-based hydroquinone detecting biosensor. Cosmetics reflect identity, confidence, and culture, but behind their glossy image lies a growing public-health crisis. The $900 billion industry is increasingly flooded with counterfeit products containing toxic ingredients like hydroquinone, a banned skin-lightening agent in the U.S., U.K., and EU. Despite its whitening effect, hydroquinone causes oxidative stress, cytotoxicity, ochronosis, and even cancer risk. Yet in much of Asia and Africa, it remains freely sold in unregulated “brightening” creams, exploiting beauty insecurities and endangering lives. Beyond public health, counterfeit cosmetics cause massive economic losses to legitimate brands. Existing detection methods are expensive and limited to specialized labs. To address this, we developed a HEK293T cell-based biosensor using the Nrf2-ARE pathway to sense oxidative stress and activate an EGFP reporter, producing a visible signal when exposed to hydroquinone. Our biosensor offers a low-cost, portable tool for safer cosmetics to empower consumers and protect global health.

title: AMPlify
text: AMPlify. This project addresses antimicrobial resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis through the in silico design of a novel therapeutic combining lytic mycobacteriophage D29 with a computationally engineered antimicrobial peptide (AMP). Using an AI-driven pipeline, over 40 candidate peptides were generated and screened via machine learning for high antimycobacterial activity and low host toxicity. Initial targets of intracellular proteins were abandoned after molecular dynamics simulations showed poor peptide stability. The focus shifted to designing membrane-active AMPs with enhanced structural robustness. Final simulations confirmed the lead AMP’s stability in solution and its ability to disrupt a model bacterial membrane. This AMP was then conceptually integrated into a donor cassette for insertion into the D29 genome. The result is a synthesis-ready, computationally validated blueprint for a therapeutic phage, with a clear plan for experimental validation in Mycobacterium smegmatis* a safe surrogate host. This work lays the foundation for a novel, precision-engineered biotherapeutic against drug-resistant tuberculosis.

title: OdorPure: An Odor-Control Cat Litter Additive Powered by Antisense RNA
text: OdorPure: An Odor-Control Cat Litter Additive Powered by Antisense RNA. Odor control is a critical feature in the cat litter market, as ammonia produced from urea degradation is the main source of unpleasant smell. Conventional deodorization methods, such as physical adsorption or fragrance masking, carry inherent risks and limitations. To overcome these issues, we designed antisense RNA targeting bacterial urease mRNA to block urease synthesis in ureolytic bacteria, thereby suppressing ammonia release at its origin. For the first time, we developed an asRNA-chitosan-montmorillonite complex as a safe, eco-friendly, and antibacterial additive for cat litter that tackles urine odor from the source while enhancing litter performance.

title: Neurobloom: Early Interventionists for Alzheimer’s Disease
text: Neurobloom: Early Interventionists for Alzheimer’s Disease. Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is a rapidly growing global health challenge, with limited options for early intervention. We developed Neurobloom, a synthetic-biology-based probiotic system using the safe strain E. coli Nissle 1917, featuring three integrated systems: System 1 enables continuous production of sakuranetin, reducing Aβ deposition and neuroinflammation through antioxidant and anti-inflammatory effects; System 2 produces lysophosphatidylcholine (LPC), which supports gut–brain axis regulation, improves synaptic function, and optimizes gut microbiota balance; System 3 incorporates a safety suicide circuit, ensuring the strain deactivates under abnormal conditions to minimize ecological risks. These systems work synergistically to deliver a sustainable, low-barrier, and adherence-friendly intervention, particularly suited for early-stage patients and high-risk populations. Neurobloom introduces a promising strategy for preventive and adjunctive AD care, paving the way toward more equitable and innovative cognitive health solutions worldwide.

title: NeuroSplice: Low-Cost RNA Diagnostic Tool for Multiple Sclerosis
text: NeuroSplice: Low-Cost RNA Diagnostic Tool for Multiple Sclerosis. Multiple sclerosis (MS) lacks a rapid and affordable molecular screening tool, with diagnosis currently dependent on MRI and invasive CSF analysis. A key genetic risk factor involves exon-6 skipping in the interleukin-7 receptor (IL7R) gene, producing a soluble isoform (sIL7R) associated with immune activation and MS susceptibility. To address this gap, we developed NeuroSplice, a cell-free toehold-switch diagnostic platform that detects the IL7R Δ6 splice junction with high specificity. In the OFF state, the switch sequesters the RBS and start codon within a hairpin structure. The binding of the cognate RNA trigger unwinds the hairpin and activates GFP translation. Using an in-silico pipeline (NUPACK, RNAstructure, BLAST) alongside iterative design–build–test–learn cycles in TXTL assays, we optimized sequence context and incorporated sfGFP to reduce background expression and achieve strong ON/OFF discrimination in 12-µL reactions. Freeze-dry compatibility makes NeuroSplice portable, offering potential for triage in resource-limited settings, longitudinal monitoring, and therapeutic response tracking.

title: BIOMNIGEM: An AI Assistant That Truly "Understands Biology"
text: BIOMNIGEM: An AI Assistant That Truly "Understands Biology". We introduce BiomniGEM, a large language model (LLM) specifically designed for multi-omics data understanding and biological reasoning, which integrates three omics modalities (DNA / cell profile/protein) and explicitly embeds omics information during joint training, enabling the model to directly read and reason over biological data. Our text builds upon prior ideas of transforming single-cell profiles into “cell sentences” and complements sequence-level foundation models in genomics and proteomics. The SynBioCoT dataset spans cell profiles, DNA, and protein modalities and covers five categories of omics tasks, aiming to systematically teach both omics understanding and biological reasoning. Experimental results show that BiomniGEM consistently outperforms leading commercial and open-source models in understanding raw omics data and demonstrates superior reasoning performance, achieving the best results on our benchmark tasks.

title: TRACER: Targeted Relapse Assessment via Cellular Effector Response
text: TRACER: Targeted Relapse Assessment via Cellular Effector Response. TRACER is a tunable cell-based sensor that detects CD19 and reports only when the signal is strong. Its core is a SynNotch receptor that, upon CD19 engagement, releases a transcription factor to activate a reporter. An intracellular inhibitor binds the transcription factor and blocks promoter access until its concentration surpasses a preset buffer, creating a built-in threshold that filters weak signals. Using a design-build-test-learn loop, we optimized promoter strength, DNA ratios, and inhibitor dose. Dry-lab models predicted SynNotch cleavage, inhibitor binding, and reporter output, guiding mid-range expression for stable control. Wet-lab assays in HEK293T cells confirmed contact-dependent activation and graded suppression with increasing inhibitor copy number. Fixing SynNotch:Reporter at 1:10 lowered baseline, and titrating the EF1α-driven inhibitor shifted activation predictably. TRACER enables adjustable sensitivity without redesigning the receptor, offering a compact, modular platform for robust CD19 detection adaptable to other outputs and formats.

title: Sandure
text: Sandure. Kuwait’s extreme heat, scarce rainfall, and sandy soil composition contribute to rapid water loss and reduced agricultural productivity. To address this environmental challenge, this project proposes engineering Escherichia coli ATCC 25922 to enhance soil water retention through the controlled production of extracellular polymeric substances (EPS). By co-transforming the strain with plasmids pVanCC (Amp^R) and pAcu (Kan^R), the bacteria can be designed to express EPS under specific induction conditions, such as elevated temperatures. The produced EPS would act as a natural hydrogel, improving the soil’s ability to retain moisture and reduce evaporation in arid environments. When applied to Kuwaiti soil, the modified bacteria are expected to create a microenvironment that binds water and stabilizes soil particles. This theoretical approach highlights the potential of synthetic biology to provide a bio-based, sustainable solution for water conservation and agricultural resilience in Kuwait’s desert ecosystems.

title: Fleur: An Oral Delivery System for GLP-1
text: Fleur: An Oral Delivery System for GLP-1. GLP-1 receptor agonists, such as semaglutide, stimulate insulin production while blocking glucagon release and slowing down stomach emptying. Though effective at weight management, semaglutide has several adverse gastrointestinal side effects, ranging from mild nausea and diarrhea to severe damage to the kidneys and pancreas. Semaglutide’s injectable synthetic form and extended systemic half-life make it difficult for patients to access and tolerate this medication. In response, Fleur was designed as an orally delivered engineered probiotic that can express and secrete wild-type GLP-1 within the human gastrointestinal tract. By using components of the body’s own gut microbiome and avoiding synthetic products, we hope to reduce systemic exposure to semaglutide and lower the risk of adverse events, while making a product that more sustainably controls T2DM symptoms and provides a comfortable and affordable alternative to injectable products.

title: Rapid quantitative analysis of proteins or protein function in complex mixtures
text: Rapid quantitative analysis of proteins or protein function in complex mixtures. Analytical reagents and mass spectrometry-based methods using these reagents for the rapid, and quantitative analysis of proteins or protein function in mixtures of proteins. The methods employ affinity labeled protein reactive reagents having three portions: an affinity label (A) covalently linked to a protein reactive group (PRG) through a linker group (L). The linker may be differentially isotopically labeled, e.g., by substitution of one or more atoms in the linker with a stable isotope thereof. These reagents allow for the selective isolation of peptide fragments or the products of reaction with a given protein (e.g., products of enzymatic reaction) from complex mixtures. The isolated peptide fragments or reaction products are characteristic of the presence of a protein or the presence of a protein function in those mixtures. Isolated peptides or reaction products are characterized by mass spectrometric (MS) techniques. The reagents also provide for differential isotopic labeling of the isolated peptides or reaction products which facilitates quantitative determination by mass spectrometry of the relative amounts of proteins in different samples. The methods of this invention can be used for qualitative and quantitative analysis of global protein expression profiles in cells and tissues, to screen for and identify proteins whose expression level in cells, tissue or biological fluids is affected by a stimulus or by a change in condition or state of the cell, tissue or organism from which the sample originated.

title: SYSTEM AND METHOD FOR RECONSTRUCTING PATHWAYS IN LARGE GENETIC NETWORKS FROM GENETIC PERTURBATIONS
text: SYSTEM AND METHOD FOR RECONSTRUCTING PATHWAYS IN LARGE GENETIC NETWORKS FROM GENETIC PERTURBATIONS. A system and method for reconstructing pathways in large genetic networks from genetic perturbations comprises an analysis method and system that applies a recursive algorithm for determining the path between every gene pair in an arbitrarily large genetic network from large-scale gene perturbation data and reconstructs all direct and indirect regulatory gene interactions in the network. Graph theory mathematics is applied to genetic network reconstruction in the following manner: Genetic perturbation data is used to identify all genes accessible from a perturbed gene to generate an accessibility list for the gene. Graph theory mathematics is applied to the accessibility list and its graph to determine a condensation of the graph as defined by the condensation's accessibility list. Graph theory mathematics is applied to the accessibility list, such as through a recursive algorithm performed on a desktop computer, to obtain an adjacency list for the gene that characterizes a genetic network.

text: Anordnung und Verfahren zur Bestimmung der zweidimensionalen Verteilung von Funduspigmenten, insbesondere des Makulapigments Xanthophyll. An arrangement and method for determining the two-dimensional distribution of fundus pigments, particularly of the xanthophyll macular pigment. The arrangement for carrying out the method comprises an illumination unit which illuminates the retina via an illumination beam path directed to the ocular fundus, observation optics located in the observation beam path proceeding from the ocular fundus, an image processing unit, elements for beam deflection and a central controlling and evaluating unit. In the method, a two-dimensional reflection image of the retina is recorded in a selected narrow-band wavelength region. In evaluating this two-dimensional reflection image, site-specific areas are established for determining the optical density and comparison values. The optical density of the fundus pigment at every fundus location is calculated from the negative logarithmic value of the quotient of the intensity value of the reflection image I R(λ) at this fundus site to a comparison intensity value of the reflection image I R(λ)Comparison . The suggested solution for the objective detection of the two-dimensional distribution of the optical density of the macular pigment xanthophyll is also suitable in principle for determining the distribution of other fundus pigments.
